definition_zh: 敏锐的；剧烈的；严重的；急性的；锐角的
definition_en: sharp in perception or effect, severe in degree, or below ninety degrees in geometry
core_image: 一根针尖，细到几乎看不见，却能一下刺穿最厚的布
scene: 医生翻看着化验单，说这种疼痛来得快、去得也快。The patient described an acute pain in the lower back.
sceneCN: 这里 acute 指症状突然而剧烈（第 1 个义项：剧烈的）；句意为病人描述下背部一阵剧烈的疼痛。

pos.zh: 敏锐的；剧烈的；严重的；急性的

senses.title: Sharp and severe in feeling
senses.definition: of pain or feeling, sharp and intense
senses.definitionCN: 指疼痛或感受尖锐而强烈
senses.example: The patient described an acute pain in the lower back.
senses.exampleCN: 病人描述下背部一阵剧烈的疼痛。
senses.why: The Latin word meant 'sharp, pointed'; pain that feels like a point is the most direct surviving sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词意为「尖锐的」；像针尖一样的疼痛，是最直接保留下来的义项。

senses.title: Serious and urgent
senses.definition: of a problem or shortage, severe enough to demand immediate action
senses.definitionCN: 指问题或短缺严重到需要立即处理
senses.example: The city faces an acute shortage of nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市面临护士严重短缺。
senses.why: A sharp edge cuts quickly; a problem with a sharp edge is one that cannot wait.
senses.whyCN: 尖锐的边缘割得快；带有尖锐边缘的问题，就是不能等的问题。

senses.title: Keenly perceptive
senses.definition: of a person or mind, quick to notice and understand fine detail
senses.definitionCN: 指人或心智对细节反应快速、理解精细
senses.example: She is an acute observer of small changes in tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她对语气中的细微变化是敏锐的观察者。
senses.why: A pointed instrument detects what a blunt one misses; the mind is described as having a point.
senses.whyCN: 尖的工具能察觉钝工具漏掉的东西；心智被描述为带有一个尖点。

senses.title: An angle below ninety degrees
senses.definition: of an angle, measuring less than ninety degrees
senses.definitionCN: 指角度小于九十度
senses.example: The roof forms an acute angle with the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶与墙形成一个锐角。
senses.why: Geometry keeps the oldest literal sense: a sharp corner is a corner that comes to a point.
senses.whyCN: 几何保留最古老的字面义：尖锐的角就是收束成一个尖点的角。

senses.title: High and sharp in pitch
senses.definition: of a sound, high and thin rather than low and full
senses.definitionCN: 指声音高而细，而非低沉饱满
senses.example: An acute whistle came from the far end of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 场地另一端传来一声尖高的哨音。
senses.why: Sharpness in the ear is heard as height in pitch, so the same word serves both senses.
senses.whyCN: 耳中的尖锐被听成音高的上升，于是同一个词承担了两个义项。

senses.title: Sudden and short in medicine
senses.definition: of a disease, beginning suddenly and lasting a short time
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病突然发作、持续时间较短
senses.example: Acute infections usually resolve faster than chronic ones.
senses.exampleCN: 急性感染通常比慢性感染好得快。
senses.why: Medical usage borrows the sharpness of onset: an acute illness arrives like a point, not a slope.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法借用了「起势之尖锐」：急性病像一个点那样到来，而不是像一道缓坡。

senses.title: Urgent in need
senses.definition: of a need, pressing and not easily postponed
senses.definitionCN: 指需求急迫，难以拖延
senses.example: There is an acute need for clean water after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，对洁净水的需求十分迫切。
senses.why: A need that has come to a point cannot be spread over time; it presses at one moment.
senses.whyCN: 已经收束成一个尖点的需求无法摊到时间里去，它只在某一刻逼迫人。

senses.title: A mark over a vowel
senses.definition: a short diagonal mark placed over a vowel in some writing systems
senses.definitionCN: 某些文字系统中标在元音上方的短斜线符号
senses.example: The acute accent shows where the stress falls.
senses.exampleCN: 尖音符标示重音落在何处。
senses.why: The mark is literally a sharp stroke, so the name records its shape rather than its sound.
senses.whyCN: 这个符号本身就是一道尖锐的笔画，所以名称记录的是它的形状，而非它的读音。

intro.en: Acute comes from a Latin word for sharp, and every sense still carries the image of a point.
intro.cn: acute 来自拉丁语中表示「尖锐」的词，所有义项都仍带着「尖点」的意象。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the 14c. for sharp pain and keen senses, and medicine added the sense of sudden illness.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个形容词，用于剧痛与敏锐感官；医学又加入「突然发病」的义项。

items.en: Acutus meant 'sharpened, pointed, keen', the participle of acuere 'to sharpen'.
items.cn: acutus 意为「磨尖的、有尖端的、敏锐的」，是 acuere「磨尖」的分词。

items.en: Acuere 'to sharpen' comes from acus 'needle', the same root that gives acupuncture.
items.cn: acuere「磨尖」来自 acus「针」，同一个词根也产生 acupuncture。

items.en: Acus meant both 'needle' and 'chaff', two things that come to a fine point.
items.cn: acus 既指「针」，也指「谷壳」，两者都收敛成细尖。

items.en: Geometry named the sharp angle acute, medicine named the sudden illness acute, and writing named the slanted mark acute.
items.cn: 几何把尖锐的角称为锐角，医学把突发的病称为急性，书写把斜置的符号称为尖音符。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sharp root; the near-meaning group names intensity or keenness.
note.cn: 形近组共享「尖锐」词根；近义组列出强烈或敏锐。

entries.definition: sharply, severely or keenly.
entries.definitionCN: 尖锐地、剧烈地或敏锐地。

entries.definition: the quality of being sharp or severe.
sharpness of perception, especially of sight or hearing.
entries.definitionCN: 感知的敏锐，尤指视觉或听觉。

entries.definition: treatment by inserting needles, from Latin acus.
entries.definitionCN: 用针刺治疗，源自拉丁语 acus。

entries.definition: very great or harsh in degree.
quick to notice and understand.
very strong in feeling or force.
very sharp and penetrating, of sound or cold.

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the word to a needle point.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把这个词和针尖连起来。

normal.en: acus means needle: acute feelings are needle-sharp.
normal.cn: acus 意为针：acute 的感受就像针尖一样锐利。

normal.en: Think of a very sharp corner: that is an acute angle.
normal.cn: 想象一个很尖的角：那就是锐角。

normal.en: An acute illness arrives like a pinprick, suddenly and sharply.
normal.cn: 急性病像被针扎一下那样突然而尖锐地到来。

normal.en: Say a-CUTE, short and pointed like the sound.
normal.cn: 读成 a-CUTE，短促而尖。

normal.en: Link it with acupuncture, which also comes from the needle.
normal.cn: 把它和 acupuncture 联系，两者都来自「针」。

abstract.en: Sharpness of edge, of mind and of onset are one image.
abstract.cn: 刀刃的锋利、心智的敏锐与发病的突然，是同一个意象。

abstract.en: What is acute cannot be ignored, which is why it also means urgent.
abstract.cn: acutely 之物无法被忽视，所以它也意味着紧迫。

abstract.en: A point is small but decisive; the word trusts small things.
abstract.cn: 尖点虽小却决定性地刺入；这个词信任小而关键之物。

examples.en: The patient described an acute pain in the lower back.
examples.cn: 病人描述下背部一阵剧烈的疼痛。

examples.en: The city faces an acute shortage of nurses.
examples.cn: 这座城市面临护士严重短缺。

examples.en: She is an acute observer of small changes in tone.
examples.cn: 她对语气中的细微变化是敏锐的观察者。

dict_mnemonic.text: acus（针）+ ute：像针尖一样锐利，就是「尖锐的、敏锐的、剧烈的」。

root: 拉丁语 acutus（尖锐的），源自 acuere（磨尖）、acus（针）

sensesIntro.en: Acute always describes a point rather than a slope; the senses differ in whether the point is pain, a problem, a mind, a corner, a sound or a written mark.
sensesIntro.cn: acute 始终描述「点」而不是「坡」；各义项的差别在于这个点是疼痛、问题、心智、角落、声音还是书写符号。

branches.en: Pain and need felt sharply and urgently.
branches.cn: 被尖锐而紧迫地感受到的疼痛与需求。

branches.en: Severity that arrives quickly and demands action.
branches.cn: 迅速到来并要求行动之严重。

branches.en: Keen mind and high thin sound.
branches.cn: 敏锐心智与高而细的声音。

branches.en: The literal corner below ninety degrees.
branches.cn: 小于九十度的字面角。

branches.en: The written mark shaped like a stroke.
branches.cn: 形如一道短撇的书写符号。

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle used as an English adjective, and its family keeps the needle image.
intro.cn: 这个词是作英语形容词用的拉丁分词，其同族词保留「针」的意象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show sharpening, needle and point feeding one word.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「磨尖」「针」与「点」如何滋养同一个词。

items.meaning: in a sharp or severe way
items.example: She was acutely aware of the risk.
The acuteness of the pain alarmed him.
Acus is the root of acupuncture.
items.exampleCN: acus 是 acupuncture 的词根。

items.meaningCN: 被制成或具有某种性质

definition_zh: 粘附；坚持；遵守；追随
definition_en: to stick firmly to a surface, or to hold fast to a rule, belief or group
core_image: 一张湿邮票按在信封上，干了以后再也揭不下来
scene: 会上每个人都签了字，表示愿意按新流程执行。All staff must adhere to the safety rules.
sceneCN: 这里 adhere 指遵守既定规则（第 2 个义项：遵守）；句意为全体员工都必须遵守安全规则。

senses.title: Stick to a surface
senses.definition: to become firmly attached to a surface through physical contact
senses.definitionCN: 通过物理接触牢固地附着在表面上
senses.example: The label adhered to the glass and would not peel off.
senses.exampleCN: 标签粘在玻璃上，揭不下来。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to stick to'; the physical bond is the ancestor of every later loyalty.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「粘到」；物理上的结合是后来一切忠诚的祖先。

senses.title: Follow a rule
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a rule, agreement or standard
senses.definitionCN: 按照规则、协议或标准行事
senses.example: All staff must adhere to the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 全体员工都必须遵守安全规则。
senses.why: A rule is a surface that a person chooses to stick to; adherence is that choice made visible in behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 规则是一块人选择去贴住的表面；遵守就是这一选择在行为中显现出来。

senses.title: Hold a belief
senses.definition: to continue to hold a belief or principle firmly
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地继续持有某种信念或原则
senses.example: She adhered to her belief that education changes lives.
senses.exampleCN: 她坚持教育能改变人生的信念。
senses.why: Beliefs are held the way stamps are held: once fixed, they resist being lifted.
senses.whyCN: 信念的持守方式就像邮票：一旦贴定，就不容易被揭起。

senses.title: Remain loyal to a group
senses.definition: to stay loyal to a person, party or organization
senses.definitionCN: 继续忠于某人、某党或某组织
senses.example: The members adhered to the union through the long dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 成员们在漫长争端中始终追随工会。
senses.why: Loyalty is adhesion between people: the follower stays attached to the group even when it is pulled.
senses.whyCN: 忠诚是人与人之间的粘附：即使被拉扯，追随者仍贴住群体。

senses.title: Bond at a microscopic level
senses.definition: of materials or molecules, to bind to a surface by chemical or physical forces
senses.definitionCN: 指材料或分子通过化学或物理力结合到表面
senses.example: The coating adheres to the metal at a molecular level.
senses.exampleCN: 涂层在分子层面粘合到金属上。
senses.why: Chemistry makes the oldest sense precise: attraction between surfaces is the same event at a smaller scale.
senses.whyCN: 化学把最古老的义项说得更精确：表面之间的吸引，是同一件事在更小的尺度上发生。

senses.title: Cling stubbornly
senses.definition: to refuse to give up an opinion or habit despite pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下仍拒绝放弃某种观点或习惯
senses.example: He adhered to out-of-date methods long after the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 改革过后很久，他仍抱住过时的方法不放。
senses.why: Sticking can be virtue or fault: the word does not judge, it only reports that the bond holds.
senses.whyCN: 粘住可以是美德也可以是毛病：这个词不作评判，只报告结合还在。

senses.title: Stay fixed in place
senses.definition: of an object, to remain fixed and not slip or move
senses.definitionCN: 指物体保持固定，不滑动或移动
senses.example: The stamp adhered to the envelope even in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 即使下雨，邮票仍固定在信封上。
senses.why: A fixed object is simply an object whose adhesion is stronger than the forces trying to move it.
senses.whyCN: 一个固定的物体，不过是粘附强于试图移动它的那些力的物体。

senses.title: Be devoted to a cause
senses.definition: to remain committed to a cause over time
senses.definitionCN: 长期致力于某项事业
senses.example: He adhered to the movement for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他致力于这场运动三十年。
senses.why: Long commitment is adhesion in time: the bond is tested not by one pull but by years of pull.
senses.whyCN: 长期的投入是时间中的粘附：检验这种结合的不是一次拉扯，而是多年的拉扯。

intro.en: Adhere comes from a Latin verb meaning to stick to, built from 'to' and 'stick'.
intro.cn: adhere 来自一个意为「粘到」的拉丁动词，由「向」与「粘」构成。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 17c. for physical sticking, then extended it to loyalty and rules.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个动词，指物理粘附，后来扩展到忠诚与规则。

items.en: Adhaerere meant 'to stick to, cling to', from ad- 'to' and haerere 'to stick, be fixed'.
items.cn: adhaerere 意为「粘到、紧贴」，由 ad-「向」与 haerere「粘住、固定」构成。

items.en: Haerere 'to stick' also gives inherent and hesitate, both involving something held fast.
items.cn: haerere「粘住」也产生 inherent 与 hesitate，两者都涉及「被固定住」。

items.en: Adhaesio named the act of sticking, and English adhesion was formed on the same pattern.
items.cn: adhaesio 命名粘附行为，英语 adhesion 也按同样模式构成。

items.en: Political and legal writing turned physical adhesion into loyalty and compliance, especially in the phrase adhere to.
items.cn: 政治与法律文本把物理粘附转为忠诚与服从，尤其见于固定搭配 adhere to。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sticking root; the near-meaning group names forms of holding fast.
note.cn: 形近组共享「粘住」词根；近义组列出牢牢保持的各种方式。

entries.definition: the state of being stuck to a surface.
a supporter who stays loyal to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 忠于某一群体的支持者。

entries.definition: a material that sticks things together.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西粘在一起的材料。

entries.definition: held fast within something as a natural quality.
entries.definitionCN: 作为固有性质固定在事物内部。

entries.definition: to become fixed to something by contact.
entries.definitionCN: 通过接触固定在某物上。

entries.definition: to act in accordance with a rule or request.
to hold on tightly and refuse to let go.
to continue firmly despite difficulty.

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the word to a stamp pressed onto an envelope.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把这个词和「邮票按在信封上」连起来。

normal.en: Think of a wet stamp: once it dries on the envelope, it will not come off.
normal.cn: 想想湿邮票：在信封上干了以后就揭不下来。

normal.en: ad- means to, here means stick: to adhere is to stick to something.
normal.cn: ad- 意为向，here 意为粘：adhere 就是粘到某物上。

normal.en: A person who adheres to a rule is glued to it by choice.
normal.cn: 遵守规则的人，是自愿被粘在规则上。

normal.en: Say ad-HERE: the here is where the bond holds.
normal.cn: 读成 ad-HERE：here 就是粘住的所在。

normal.en: Link it with adhesive tape: the noun is the thing, the verb is the action.
normal.cn: 把它和 adhesive tape 联系：名词是粘合物，动词是粘的动作。

abstract.en: Physical adhesion becomes loyalty when the surface is a group.
abstract.cn: 当表面换成一个群体，物理粘附就变成忠诚。

abstract.en: A bond is tested by repeated pulling, not by one touch.
abstract.cn: 粘合由反复拉扯检验，而不是由一次接触检验。

abstract.en: Sticking fast can be virtue or fault; the word reports the bond, not the judgment.
abstract.cn: 牢牢粘住可以是美德也可以是毛病；这个词报告粘合，不做判断。

examples.en: All staff must adhere to the safety rules.
examples.cn: 全体员工都必须遵守安全规则。

examples.en: She adhered to her belief that education changes lives.
examples.cn: 她坚持教育能改变人生的信念。

examples.en: The label adhered to the glass and would not peel off.
examples.cn: 标签粘在玻璃上，揭不下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: ad（向）+ here（粘）：牢牢粘在某物上，就是「粘附」，用于规则则是「遵守」。

root: 拉丁语 adhaerere（粘到）：ad-（向）+ haerere（粘住）

sensesIntro.en: Adhere always means a bond that holds; the senses differ in whether the surface is glass, a rule, a belief, a party or a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: adhere 始终表示一种维持住的粘合；各义项的差别在于表面是玻璃、规则、信念、政党还是一项事业。

branches.en: Physical sticking, from stamps to molecules.
branches.cn: 从邮票到分子的物理粘附。

branches.en: Rules followed well, and habits held too long.
branches.cn: 被良好遵守的规则，以及被抱得太久的习惯。

branches.en: Beliefs that will not be lifted.
branches.cn: 不会被揭起的信念。

branches.en: Loyalty to a group and devotion to a cause.
branches.cn: 对群体的忠诚与对事业的献身。

branches.en: Commitment measured in years rather than moments.
branches.cn: 以年而非瞬间衡量的投入。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb stem with an English verb form, and its family keeps the image of something fixed in place.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动词词干加英语动词形式，其同族词保留「被固定在原处」的意象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show sticking becoming attachment and then loyalty.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「粘住」如何变成「附着」，再变成「忠诚」。

items.example: The tape adhered to the box.
Adhesion depends on a clean surface.
items.exampleCN: 粘附取决于表面是否干净。

items.meaning: one who sticks to a group
items.exampleCN: 该党失去了许多追随者。

items.example: Use a strong adhesive for tiles.
items.exampleCN: 铺瓷砖要用强力粘合剂。

items.meaning: the state of following or sticking
items.exampleCN: 对日程的遵守有所改善。

items.example: Risk is inherent in the work.
items.exampleCN: 风险是这项工作的固有部分。

items.meaning: to stick fast, hence to pause

items.example: Adhesion names the result of sticking.

definition_zh: 腐蚀；侵蚀；逐渐破坏；削弱
definition_en: to eat away a material or gradually destroy something, often by chemical action
core_image: 一块铁在盐水里放了一夜，表面浮起红褐色的鳞片，手一碰就掉渣
scene: 桥梁检查报告指出，海风与盐雾正在慢慢吃掉钢梁。Salt spray had corroded the bridge supports.
sceneCN: 这里 corrode 指盐雾化学性地侵蚀金属（第 1 个义项：腐蚀材料）；句意为盐雾已经腐蚀了桥墩。

senses.title: Eat away metal
senses.definition: of a chemical, to destroy metal slowly by oxidation or acid action
senses.definitionCN: 指化学物质通过氧化或酸作用缓慢毁坏金属
senses.example: Salt spray had corroded the bridge supports.
senses.exampleCN: 盐雾已经腐蚀了桥墩。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to gnaw': acid gnaws at metal the way teeth gnaw at a bone.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「啃咬」：酸啃金属，正如牙齿啃骨头。

senses.title: Attack a surface
senses.definition: to wear away the surface of a material
senses.definitionCN: 磨损材料表面
senses.example: The acid corroded the marble floor.
senses.exampleCN: 酸侵蚀了大理石地面。
senses.why: Surface is where the attack becomes visible; the damage begins at the boundary and works inward.
senses.whyCN: 表面是攻击变得可见的地方；损坏从边界开始，向内推进。

senses.title: Destroy gradually
senses.definition: to destroy something slowly and piece by piece
senses.definitionCN: 一点一点地缓慢毁坏某物
senses.example: Neglect had corroded the old machine beyond repair.
senses.exampleCN: 疏于维护使旧机器损坏到无法修理。
senses.why: Anything left exposed will be eaten away by something; neglect is simply exposure without protection.
senses.whyCN: 任何暴露在外的东西都会被害虫般的因素吃掉；疏于维护不过是无保护的暴露。

senses.title: Undermine trust
senses.definition: to weaken confidence, trust or morale over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间削弱信心、信任或士气
senses.example: Repeated delays corroded trust between the two teams.
senses.exampleCN: 反复延误侵蚀了两个团队之间的信任。
senses.why: Trust is a surface that holds relationships; once it is eaten through, the structure fails.
senses.whyCN: 信任是托住关系的表面；一旦被蛀穿，结构就崩塌。

senses.title: Deteriorate on its own
senses.definition: of a material, to become degraded through time and exposure
senses.definitionCN: 指材料随时间与暴露而退化
senses.example: The pipes corroded faster in the damp basement.
senses.exampleCN: 管道在潮湿的地下室里腐蚀得更快。
senses.why: The verb can drop its agent: the metal does not need to be attacked, it only needs the wrong conditions.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以省略施事者：金属不必被谁攻击，只要条件不对，它自己就会坏。

senses.title: Dissolve rock by acid
senses.definition: of acid water, to dissolve or wear rock
senses.definitionCN: 指酸性水溶解或磨损岩石
senses.example: Acid rain corroded the limestone statues.
senses.exampleCN: 酸雨腐蚀了石灰岩雕像。
senses.why: Limestone is soft enough for weak acid to eat it, so geology repeats the same gnawing at a slower pace.
senses.whyCN: 石灰岩足够软，弱酸就能吃掉它，于是地质过程以更慢的节奏重复同样的啃咬。

senses.title: Erode moral values
senses.definition: to weaken moral standards or principles
senses.definitionCN: 削弱道德标准或原则
senses.example: Cynicism can corrode a community's shared values.
senses.exampleCN: 犬儒心态会侵蚀一个社群共享的价值。
senses.why: Shared values hold a group together the way metal holds a bridge; the loss is slow, then structural.
senses.whyCN: 共享价值像金属托住桥梁那样托住一个群体；损失先是缓慢的，随后是结构性的。

senses.title: Consume little by little
senses.definition: to consume or reduce something gradually, as if by gnawing
senses.definitionCN: 像啃咬那样逐渐消耗或减少某物
senses.example: Debt corroded the family's savings year by year.
senses.exampleCN: 债务年复一年地吞噬这个家庭的储蓄。
senses.why: The gnawing image survives in abstract losses: nothing is taken at once, and that is what makes it dangerous.
senses.whyCN: 「啃咬」的意象在抽象的损失中延续：没有东西是一次被拿走的，而这正使它危险。

intro.en: Corrode comes from a Latin verb meaning to gnaw away, built from 'together' and 'gnaw'.
intro.cn: corrode 来自一个意为「啃掉」的拉丁动词，由「一起」与「啃」构成。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 17c. for chemical eating of metals, and later used it for trust and values.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个动词，指化学性侵蚀金属，后来用于信任与价值。

items.en: Corrodere meant 'to gnaw to pieces, eat away', from com- (intensive) and rodere 'to gnaw'.
items.cn: corrodere 意为「啃碎、吃掉」，由加强语气的前缀 com- 与 rodere「啃」构成。

items.en: Rodere 'to gnaw' also gives rodent, the animal that gnaws, and erode through a related verb.
items.cn: rodere「啃」也产生 rodent（啃咬的动物），并通过相关动词产生 erode。

items.en: Corrosio named the gnawing away, and English corrosion followed the same pattern.
items.cn: corrosio 命名啃蚀，英语 corrosion 沿用同一模式。

items.en: Chemistry gave the word its precise sense, and moral writing borrowed it for anything slowly eaten from within.
items.cn: 化学给了这个词精确含义，道德写作则借它指任何被从内部慢慢吃掉的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the gnawing root; the near-meaning group names kinds of wearing away.
note.cn: 形近组共享「啃」词根；近义组列出各种磨损。

entries.definition: the process of being eaten away.
able to eat away a material.
to wear away gradually, especially by wind or water.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐磨损，尤指被风或水。

entries.definition: a gnawing animal such as a rat.
to become covered with reddish iron oxide.
entries.definitionCN: 表面覆上红褐色氧化铁。

entries.definition: to destroy something gradually.
to weaken something from below or indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 从下方或间接削弱某物。

entries.definition: to reduce quality or strength over time.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间降低质量或强度。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of acid gnawing at metal.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「酸啃金属」的画面留住。

normal.en: Think of teeth: corrode means to gnaw away, only the teeth are acid.
normal.cn: 想想牙齿：corrode 就是啃掉，只不过牙齿换成了酸。

normal.en: Salt water on iron leaves red flakes; that is corrosion at work.
normal.cn: 盐水泡铁留下红色鳞片，那就是腐蚀在工作。

normal.en: Trust can be corroded the way metal is: slowly, from the surface in.
normal.cn: 信任像金属一样会被腐蚀：缓慢地，从表面向内。

normal.en: Say cor-RODE, with the stress on the gnawing.
normal.cn: 读成 cor-RODE，重音落在「啃咬」上。

normal.en: Link it with rodent: both words are about gnawing.
normal.cn: 把它和 rodent 联系：两个词都与啃咬有关。

abstract.en: Nothing is taken at once, which is why corrosion is easy to ignore.
abstract.cn: 没有东西是一次被拿走的，所以腐蚀容易被忽视。

abstract.en: A structure fails at the surface before it fails at the core.
abstract.cn: 结构先在表面失效，再在核心失效。

abstract.en: The same verb serves metal, trust and values because all three are eaten from within.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词适用于金属、信任与价值，因为三者都是从内部被吃掉。

examples.en: Salt spray had corroded the bridge supports.
examples.cn: 盐雾已经腐蚀了桥墩。

examples.en: Repeated delays corroded trust between the two teams.
examples.cn: 反复延误侵蚀了两个团队之间的信任。

examples.en: Acid rain corroded the limestone statues.
examples.cn: 酸雨腐蚀了石灰岩雕像。

dict_mnemonic.text: cor（加强）+ rode（啃）：像被酸一点点啃掉，就是「腐蚀」。

root: 拉丁语 corrodere（啃掉）：com-（加强）+ rodere（啃）

sensesIntro.en: Corrode always means being eaten away; the senses differ in what is eaten, whether metal, stone, trust, morale or savings.
sensesIntro.cn: corrode 始终表示被啃蚀；各义项的差别在于被吃掉的是金属、石头、信任、士气还是储蓄。

branches.en: Metal and stone eaten by salt, acid or damp.
branches.cn: 被盐、酸或潮气侵蚀的金属与石头。

branches.en: Slow destruction that is easy to overlook.
branches.cn: 容易被忽视的缓慢毁坏。

branches.en: Trust and values weakened from within.
branches.cn: 从内部被削弱的信任与价值。

branches.en: Rock dissolved by acid water.
branches.cn: 被酸性水溶解的岩石。

branches.en: Materials that degrade simply by being exposed.
branches.cn: 仅因暴露就退化的材料。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb stem with an English verb ending; its family keeps the gnawing image.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动词词干加英语动词词尾；其同族词保留「啃咬」意象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show gnawing becoming chemical corrosion.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「啃咬」如何变成化学腐蚀。

items.exampleCN: 一只啮齿动物啃坏了电缆。

definition_zh: 面容；表情；镇定；支持；容许
definition_en: a person's face or expression, composure, or the act of giving support and approval
core_image: 一张在喧闹中仍不变形的脸，眉目平直，像被端平的一碗水
scene: 宣布结果时，她的脸上没有一丝波动，等所有人离开才松一口气。She kept her countenance while the verdict was read.
sceneCN: 这里 countenance 指在压力下维持镇定的神色（第 2 个义项：镇定）；句意为宣读裁决时她保持着镇定。

senses.title: The face itself
senses.definition: a person's face, especially as it shows character
senses.definitionCN: 人的脸，尤指显露性格的面容
senses.example: A familiar countenance appeared at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门口出现了一张熟悉的面容。
senses.why: The word came from Latin for 'containment': the face is the container that holds and shows the inner person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语「容纳」：脸是容纳并显示内在之人的容器。

senses.title: Composure under pressure
senses.definition: calm control of the face and feelings when others are watching
senses.definitionCN: 在他人注视下对面部与情绪的冷静控制
senses.example: She kept her countenance while the verdict was read.
senses.exampleCN: 宣读裁决时她保持着镇定。
senses.why: If the face is a container, composure is the lid staying on when the contents are under pressure.
senses.whyCN: 如果脸是容器，镇定就是内容物受压时盖子仍然盖住。

senses.title: Expression of a feeling
senses.definition: the look on a face that reveals a mood
senses.definitionCN: 脸上显露情绪的神情
senses.example: His countenance changed when he heard the price.
senses.exampleCN: 听到价格时他的表情变了。
senses.why: An expression is what leaks out of the container; the same face can hold a mood or reveal it.
senses.whyCN: 表情是从容器里漏出来的东西；同一张脸可以藏住情绪，也可以显露它。

senses.title: Support or approval
senses.definition: the act of giving approval or moral backing to something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某事物认可或道义支持的行为
senses.example: The board gave its countenance to the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会支持这项合并。
senses.why: To lend one's face to a plan is to let the plan appear under one's name, which is what approval means.
senses.whyCN: 把脸借给一项计划，就是让计划以自己的名义出现，这正是批准的含义。

senses.title: Permission or tolerance
senses.definition: to allow something to happen without condemning it
senses.definitionCN: 允许某事发生而不加谴责
senses.example: The school would not countenance cheating.
senses.exampleCN: 学校不会容许作弊。
senses.why: Approval and tolerance differ in degree: the same face can back a plan or simply refuse to forbid it.
senses.whyCN: 批准与容忍只差程度：同一张脸既可以支持一项计划，也可以只是拒绝禁止它。

senses.title: Appearance or bearing
senses.definition: a person's general appearance and manner of carrying themselves
senses.definitionCN: 一个人总体的外观与举止方式
senses.example: He had the countenance of a man used to being obeyed.
senses.exampleCN: 他有一副惯于被服从的人的仪态。
senses.why: Bearing is the whole body's version of the face: how a person occupies space announces what the face only hints at.
senses.whyCN: 仪态是整副身体版本的面容：一个人如何占据空间，宣告了脸只暗示的东西。

senses.title: Moral backing
senses.definition: support that gives something respectability rather than money
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物获得体面地位而非金钱的支持
senses.example: The judge's presence lent countenance to the inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 法官的到场为调查增添了道义支持。
senses.why: Respectability is borrowed from someone whose face carries weight, so presence itself becomes a form of funding.
senses.whyCN: 体面是从一张有分量的脸上借来的，于是到场本身成了一种资助。

senses.title: Calm face in old use
senses.definition: in older writing, a calm and steady facial appearance
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，平静而稳定的面部外观
senses.example: The chronicle praises the queen's untroubled countenance.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史称赞女王平静无扰的面色。
senses.why: Old writing used the word for an achieved stillness of face, the visible proof of an ordered inner life.
senses.whyCN: 较早的文本用这个词指一种修得的脸上静止，是内在秩序可见的证据。

intro.en: Countenance comes from a Latin verb meaning to contain or hold, and the face was understood as what holds the self.
intro.cn: countenance 来自一个意为「容纳、保持」的拉丁动词，脸被理解为容纳自我的容器。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the 13c. for the face and its expression, and the verb later meant to support.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个名词，指脸与表情；动词后来表示支持。

items.en: Continentia meant 'a holding together, self-control', from continere 'to hold together'.
items.cn: continentia 意为「保持一体、自我控制」，来自 continere「保持在一起」。

items.en: Continere 'to hold together, contain' is com- 'together' plus tenere 'to hold'.
items.cn: continere「保持、容纳」由 com-「一起」与 tenere「握住」构成。

items.en: Tenere 'to hold' also gives tenant, retain and contain, all built on keeping something in place.
items.cn: tenere「握住」也产生 tenant、retain 与 contain，都建立在「使某物留在原处」。

items.en: From the face that holds composure came the verb meaning to support or tolerate: to hold something up in public.
items.cn: 从「保持镇定的脸」发展出表示支持或容许的动词：在公开场合把某物托住。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the containing root; the near-meaning group names faces, calmness and approval.
note.cn: 形近组共享「容纳」词根；近义组列出面容、镇定与支持。

entries.definition: supported or tolerated in the past.
entries.definitionCN: 过去得到支持或容许的。

entries.definition: self-restraint, especially over the body.
entries.definitionCN: 自我克制，尤指对身体的克制。

entries.definition: to hold something inside.
the quality of holding oneself in check.
the front of the head.
the look on a face that shows feeling.
calm control of one's feelings and appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 对情绪与外表的冷静控制。

entries.definition: a favourable opinion or official consent.
entries.definitionCN: 赞成的意见或正式同意。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the word to a face holding itself steady.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把这个词和「一张端住自己的脸」连起来。

normal.en: Think of contain: the face is a container that holds the self in.
normal.cn: 想想 contain：脸是容纳自我的容器。

normal.en: A countenance kept is a lid kept on under pressure.
normal.cn: 保持 countenance，就是压力下盖住盖子。

normal.en: To give countenance to a plan is to let it appear under your face.
normal.cn: 给某项计划 countenance，就是让它以你的面孔出现。

normal.en: Say coun-TEN-ance, with the holding root stressed.
normal.cn: 读成 coun-TEN-ance，重音落在表示「握住」的词根上。

normal.en: Link it with composure: both describe a face that does not spill.
normal.cn: 把它和 composure 联系：两者都描述不外泄的脸。

abstract.en: The face is the smallest public surface of the self.
abstract.cn: 脸是自我最小的公共表面。

abstract.en: Support and tolerance are the same gesture at different strengths.
abstract.cn: 支持与容许是同一姿态的不同强度。

abstract.en: A calm face can be honesty or a lid; the word does not decide.
abstract.cn: 平静的脸可以是诚实，也可以是一个盖子；这个词不作判定。

examples.en: She kept her countenance while the verdict was read.
examples.cn: 宣读裁决时她保持着镇定。

examples.en: The board gave its countenance to the merger.
examples.cn: 董事会支持这项合并。

examples.en: The school would not countenance cheating.
examples.cn: 学校不会容许作弊。

dict_mnemonic.text: count（一起）+ ten（握住）+ ance：把自我端住的那张脸，就是「面容」，端得住就是「镇定」。

root: 拉丁语 continentia（自我控制），源自 continere：com-（一起）+ tenere（握住）

sensesIntro.en: Countenance always involves a face holding something; the senses differ in whether it holds a person, a feeling, composure, approval or tolerance.
sensesIntro.cn: countenance 始终涉及一张「端住某物」的脸；各义项的差别在于它端住的是一个人、一种情绪、镇定、认可还是容忍。

branches.en: The face, its expression and its bearing.
branches.cn: 脸、它的表情与仪态。

branches.en: Calmness that keeps the container closed.
branches.cn: 让容器保持关闭的镇定。

branches.en: Support that lends respectability.
branches.cn: 赋予体面地位的支持。

branches.en: Tolerance that stops short of forbidding.
branches.cn: 未到禁止程度的容许。

branches.en: The pressure test that makes composure visible.
branches.cn: 使镇定变得可见的压力测试。

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of state with an English form, and its family is the family of holding.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁状态名词的英语形式，其同族词属于「握住」家族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show holding together becoming self-control and then social support.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁语条目展示「保持一体」如何变成自我控制，再变成社会支持。

items.example: Endurance is the state of enduring.

definition_zh: 觊觎；贪求；渴望占有（他人之物）
definition_en: to desire something strongly, especially something that belongs to another person
core_image: 一个人站在别人的院子外，隔着篱笆盯着那辆崭新的车，手指不自觉地在裤缝上蹭
scene: 邻居新买的车停在门口，他绕着车走了两圈，眼神一直没离开。He had coveted that car since the day it arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 covet 指强烈地想要本属于他人的东西（第 1 个义项：觊觎他人之物）；句意为那辆车一到，他就一直觊觎着它。

senses.title: Want what belongs to another
senses.definition: to desire a thing that is in another person's possession
senses.definitionCN: 渴望得到他人占有的东西
senses.example: He had coveted that car since the day it arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆车一到，他就一直觊觎着它。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to desire eagerly'; the modern word keeps the edge of wanting what is not yours.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「热切地想要」；现代词保留了「想要不属于自己之物」的那道锋刃。

senses.title: Crave wealth or goods
senses.definition: to long for money or material things beyond what one needs
senses.definitionCN: 渴望超过自身所需的金钱或物品
senses.example: The merchant coveted rare silks from the east.
senses.exampleCN: 这位商人贪求来自东方的稀有丝绸。
senses.why: Wanting more than one needs turns desire into appetite, and appetite is what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 当想要超过所需时，欲望就变成胃口，而这个词命名的正是这种胃口。

senses.title: Eye a position or rank
senses.definition: to want a job, title or rank held by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 想要他人占据的工作、头衔或职位
senses.example: Two ministers coveted the chancellor's chair.
senses.exampleCN: 两位大臣都觊觎首相的位子。
senses.why: A position is a seat someone else occupies; to covet it is to want the seat more than the sitter.
senses.whyCN: 职位是别人正坐着的椅子；觊觎它就是想要那把椅子，胜过想要坐着的人。

senses.title: Envy another's success
senses.definition: to feel envious longing for another person's achievements
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的成就怀有嫉妒的渴望
senses.example: She coveted her rival's reputation in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 她羡慕对手在这个领域的名声。
senses.why: Envy adds a comparison to desire: the good is measured against someone who already has it.
senses.whyCN: 嫉妒在欲望之上加了比较：这好处是参照一个已经拥有它的人来衡量的。

senses.title: Long for a prize
senses.definition: to want an award or honour intensely
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地想要某个奖项或荣誉
senses.example: Every team in the league covets the trophy.
senses.exampleCN: 联盟里的每支队伍都渴望那座奖杯。
senses.why: A prize is scarce and visible, which is exactly the combination that makes coveting possible.
senses.whyCN: 奖项稀缺而显眼，正是这种组合使觊觎成为可能。

senses.title: Forbidden desire in scripture
senses.definition: in religious language, to desire unlawfully what belongs to a neighbour
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教语言中，不正当地贪图邻人之物
senses.example: The commandment warns against coveting a neighbour's house.
senses.exampleCN: 诫命警告不可贪恋邻人的房屋。
senses.why: Religious usage gives the word its moral weight: the desire itself, not only the taking, is condemned.
senses.whyCN: 宗教用法赋予这个词道德重量：被谴责的是欲望本身，而不只是夺取。

senses.title: Crave someone's attention
senses.definition: to want another person's notice or affection intensely
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地想要他人的注意或喜爱
senses.example: The child coveted every glance from the teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 这孩子渴望老师每一道目光。
senses.why: Attention is a possession that cannot be bought, so wanting it feels like wanting what another holds.
senses.whyCN: 关注是一种买不到的财物，因此想要它就像是想要别人持有的东西。

senses.title: Wish for an abstract good
senses.definition: to long for peace, chance or rest that seems out of reach
senses.definitionCN: 渴望看似遥不可及的安宁、机会或休息
senses.example: After years of noise, he coveted silence.
senses.exampleCN: 在多年的喧闹之后，他渴望安静。
senses.why: The object need not be a thing; any good that someone else seems to have can become the target.
senses.whyCN: 对象不必是物品；任何别人似乎拥有的好处，都可能成为目标。

intro.en: Covet comes from a Latin verb for eager desire, and the word has carried a warning since its earliest English use.
intro.cn: covet 来自一个表示「热切欲求」的拉丁动词，自最早的英语用法起就带着警告意味。

items.en: English borrowed the verb from Old French in the 14c., and the Ten Commandments fixed it in religious language.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪从古法语借入这个动词，十诫又把它固定在宗教语言中。

items.en: Old French coveitier meant 'to desire eagerly', carrying the same appetite into English.
items.cn: 古法语 coveitier 意为「热切渴望」，把同一种胃口带进英语。

items.en: Latin cupiditas meant 'eagerness, desire, greed', and it names the vice rather than the mere wish.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cupiditas 意为「热切、欲望、贪婪」，命名的是恶习，而不只是愿望。

items.en: Cupere 'to desire' is also behind Cupid, the god of desire, whose name comes from the same root.
items.cn: cupere「欲求」也是爱神 Cupid 的词源，其名出自同一词根。

items.en: Modern English keeps the moral shadow: to covet is to want what is not yours, or to want it too much.
items.cn: 现代英语保留道德阴影：covet 就是想要不属于自己的东西，或者想要得太过。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the covet stem; the near-meaning group names neighbouring shades of desire.
note.cn: 形近组共享 covet 词干；近义组列出欲望的邻近色彩。

entries.definition: eager to possess what belongs to another.
with greedy longing.
the state of desiring another's goods.
eagerly wanted by many people.
wanting another's advantages and feeling pain at their having them.
entries.definitionCN: 想要他人的优势，并为其拥有而痛苦。

entries.definition: to want something with a bodily or urgent intensity.
entries.definitionCN: 以身体般或急迫的强度想要某物。

entries.definition: to feel a deep, often wistful desire for something absent.
entries.definitionCN: 对缺席之物怀有深切而怅惘的渴望。

entries.definition: to feel resentment that another has or receives something.
entries.definitionCN: 因他人拥有或得到某物而心生不满。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a person standing outside a fence, staring at what is not theirs.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「站在篱笆外盯着不属于自己之物」的画面留住。

normal.en: Think of the forbidden tenth commandment: covet names the wanting itself.
normal.cn: 想一想第十条诫命：covet 命名的是欲望本身。

normal.en: Covet and Cupid share a root: both are about desire that aims at another.
normal.cn: covet 与 Cupid 同根：两者都指朝向他人的欲望。

normal.en: Picture a covetous eye, wide open and fixed on a neighbour's gate.
normal.cn: 想象一只贪婪的眼睛，睁得很大，死死盯着邻居的院门。

normal.en: Say KOH-vet; the long o sounds like a sigh of wanting.
normal.cn: 读成 KOH-vet，长音 o 听起来像一声渴求的叹息。

normal.en: Link it with envious: covet is the wanting, envy adds the sting.
normal.cn: 把它和 envious 联系：covet 是想要，envy 又加上了刺痛。

abstract.en: Desire becomes coveting when its object belongs to someone else.
abstract.cn: 当对象属于别人时，欲望就变成觊觎。

abstract.en: The word condemns the appetite before any hand reaches out.
abstract.cn: 这个词在任何手伸出之前，就先谴责了胃口。

abstract.en: What cannot be bought is the easiest thing to covet.
abstract.cn: 买不到的东西，最容易被觊觎。

examples.en: He had coveted that car since the day it arrived.
examples.cn: 那辆车一到，他就一直觊觎着它。

examples.en: Two ministers coveted the chancellor's chair.
examples.cn: 两位大臣都觊觎首相的位子。

examples.en: After years of noise, he coveted silence.
examples.cn: 在多年的喧闹之后，他渴望安静。

dict_mnemonic.text: co（共同）+ vet（看）：一直盯着别人的东西看，就是「觊觎」。

root: 拉丁语 cupere（欲求），经古法语 coveitier 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: Covet always aims at a good that someone else holds; the senses differ in whether the good is a thing, a rank, a success or an intangible state.
sensesIntro.cn: covet 始终瞄准别人持有的某种好处；各义项的差别在于这好处是物品、职位、成就，还是一种无形的状态。

core.cn: 想要不属于自己的东西

branches.en: Things and wealth that another person owns.
branches.cn: 他人拥有的物品与财富。

branches.en: Ranks and prizes that only one person can hold.
branches.cn: 只能由一个人占据的职位与奖项。

branches.en: Success and attention that seem unfairly distributed.
branches.cn: 看似分配不公的成就与关注。

branches.en: The religious prohibition on wanting a neighbour's goods.
branches.cn: 宗教上对贪图邻人财物的禁止。

branches.en: Intangible goods such as silence or rest.
branches.cn: 安宁或休息这类无形的好处。

intro.en: The word builds a small family around desire: an adjective for the person, an adverb for the manner and a noun for the habit.
intro.cn: 这个词围绕「欲望」长出一个小的词族：形容词指人，副词指方式，名词指习性。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root cupere supplies several English words about appetite, including the name of the god of desire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 cupere 提供了若干关于欲望的英语词，其中包括爱神的名字。

items.meaning: full of desire for another's goods
items.meaningCN: 充满对他人财物的渴望
items.example: He gave the necklace a covetous look.
items.exampleCN: 他贪婪地看了那条项链一眼。

items.meaning: the habit of desiring another's goods
items.exampleCN: 布道警告人们不要贪心。

items.example: The award is the most coveted in the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个奖项是该领域最令人向往的。

items.meaning: the act of desiring another's goods
items.example: Coveting a neighbour's house was forbidden.
items.exampleCN: 贪恋邻人的房屋是被禁止的。

items.example: The night shift was an uncoveted duty.
items.exampleCN: 夜班是一项没人想要的职责。

items.example: The coveter never looked at what he already had.
items.exampleCN: 觊觎者从不看自己已经拥有的东西。

items.example: The house was covetable but far too expensive.
items.exampleCN: 那房子令人向往，但实在太贵。

definition_zh: 粗鲁无礼的；愚钝的；低俗的；粗糙的
definition_en: so insensitive, stupid or vulgar as to show a lack of thought or feeling
core_image: 在葬礼上有人大声谈股票，笑声穿过黑衣人群
scene: 追悼会还没结束，就有人开始讨论遗产怎么分。The remark was crass even by his standards.
sceneCN: 这里 crass 指全然不顾场合与他人感受的粗鲁（第 1 个义项：粗鲁无礼）；句意为这句话按他自己的标准也算粗鲁。

senses.title: Insensitive to other people
senses.definition: showing no awareness of other people's feelings or the occasion
senses.definitionCN: 对他人感受或场合毫无体察
senses.example: The remark was crass even by his standards.
senses.exampleCN: 这句话按他自己的标准也算粗鲁。
senses.why: The Latin adjective meant 'thick' or 'solid'; a thick skin cannot feel the fine grain of a situation.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词意为「厚实的、结实的」；厚皮感受不到情境的细纹。

senses.title: Vulgar in taste
senses.definition: showing poor and ostentatious taste
senses.definitionCN: 品味拙劣而炫耀
senses.example: The lobby was decorated with crass gold ornaments.
senses.exampleCN: 大堂里装饰着俗气的金色饰件。
senses.why: Thickness in the eye becomes coarseness in taste: nothing subtle survives the display.
senses.whyCN: 眼中的「厚」变成品味上的「粗」：在这样的展示里，细腻的东西都活不下来。

senses.title: Grossly materialistic
senses.definition: valuing money and display above all else
senses.definitionCN: 把金钱与炫耀看得高于一切
senses.example: Critics called the campaign crass commercialism.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这场活动是庸俗的商业主义。
senses.why: A thick desire for gain blunts every finer motive, so the word judges the appetite behind the display.
senses.whyCN: 对获利的厚实欲望磨钝了所有更精细的动机，因此这个词评判的是展示背后的胃口。

senses.title: Blatantly tactless
senses.definition: stated or done so openly that it cannot be excused as a slip
senses.definitionCN: 说得或做得过于露骨，无法以无心之失开脱
senses.example: It was a crass attempt to profit from the disaster.
senses.exampleCN: 那是借灾难牟利的露骨企图。
senses.why: Tact depends on a thin awareness of context; crassness is that awareness missing altogether.
senses.whyCN: 得体依赖于对情境的细微觉察；粗鲁则是这种觉察完全缺席。

senses.title: Coarse in texture, in old use
senses.definition: in older texts, literally thick, coarse or solid in texture
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，字面指质地厚、粗或结实
senses.example: The old grammarian described the stone as crass and heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 那位古代语法学家称这块石头粗糙而沉重。
senses.why: The physical sense is the root: what is thick cannot be penetrated by light or feeling.
senses.whyCN: 物理义是根：厚实之物无法被光或感受穿透。

senses.title: Grossly stupid
senses.definition: so foolish that the stupidity seems wilful
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢到仿佛是有意为之
senses.example: It was a crass mistake to ignore the warning.
senses.exampleCN: 无视警告是个愚不可及的错。
senses.why: Stupidity becomes crass when it could have been avoided by the simplest attention.
senses.whyCN: 当只需最简单的留心就能避免时，愚蠢就变成「愚不可及」。

senses.title: Ignorant disregard
senses.definition: a blunt refusal to learn or consider what is obvious to others
senses.definitionCN: 生硬地拒绝了解或考虑他人眼中显然的事
senses.example: His crass ignorance of the local customs offended the hosts.
senses.exampleCN: 他对当地习俗的愚钝无知冒犯了主人。
senses.why: Ignorance can be innocent, but crass ignorance is thick on purpose: it will not let information in.
senses.whyCN: 无知可以是无辜的，但 crass ignorance 是有意地厚实：它不让信息进入。

senses.title: Thick-headed in old medicine
senses.definition: in old physiology, having a thick or dull constitution
senses.definitionCN: 在旧时生理学中，指体质厚钝
senses.example: Old writers blamed a crass humour for slow wit.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时作者把迟钝的才思归咎于粗厚的体液。
senses.why: The last sense records an old theory of temperament; the metaphor of thickness survived after the theory died.
senses.whyCN: 最后一个义项记录了旧的性情理论；理论消亡之后，「厚」的比喻仍然活着。

intro.en: Crass comes from a Latin adjective meaning thick or solid, and thickness became the image for a mind that lets nothing fine through.
intro.cn: crass 来自一个表示「厚实、结实」的拉丁形容词，而「厚」成了「什么细腻之物都透不进去的心智」的意象。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the 17c. for coarse matter, then applied it to coarse manners.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，指粗糙的物质，随后用于粗鲁的举止。

items.en: Latin crassus meant 'thick, solid, fat', used of soil, air and bodies alike.
items.cn: 拉丁语 crassus 意为「厚的、结实的、肥的」，土壤、空气与身体都可以用它形容。

items.en: Crassitudo named thickness itself, a quality one could measure rather than judge.
items.cn: crassitudo 命名厚度本身，是一种可以测量而非评判的性质。

items.en: The move from thick matter to thick wit happened in English: a dense substance became a dense mind.
items.cn: 从「厚的物质」到「厚的心智」的转变发生在英语中：致密的实体变成了迟钝的头脑。

items.en: Today the word is almost always a judgement of taste or tact rather than a description of texture.
items.cn: 今天这个词几乎总是对品味或得体的评判，而不是对质地的描述。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crass stem; the near-meaning group names kinds of coarseness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crass 词干；近义组列出粗俗的各种形态。

entries.definition: in an insensitive or vulgar way.
the quality of being insensitive or vulgar.
more insensitive or vulgar.
the most insensitive or vulgar.
saying or doing things without sensitivity to others.
entries.definitionCN: 说话做事不顾他人感受。

entries.definition: lacking refinement in taste or manners.
awkward and unsure in social situations.
entries.definitionCN: 在社交场合笨拙而不自在。

entries.definition: unable or unwilling to understand what is clear.
entries.definitionCN: 无法或不愿理解明显之事。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a loud remark in a silent room.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「安静房间里突然一句大声的话」这一画面留住。

normal.en: Crass means thick: a thick hide feels nothing, and a crass remark feels nothing either.
normal.cn: crass 意为厚：厚皮什么都感觉不到，粗鲁的话也什么都感觉不到。

normal.en: Picture a joke told at a funeral, and the silence that follows.
normal.cn: 想象在葬礼上讲了个笑话，随后的一片沉默。

normal.en: The Latin crassus described thick soil; thick manners grow in the same ground.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 crassus 描述厚实的土壤；粗鲁的举止也长在同样的土里。

normal.en: Say KRASS, one hard syllable, like a blunt object landing.
normal.cn: 读成 KRASS，一个硬邦邦的音节，像钝器落地。

normal.en: Link it with tactless: both describe a missing filter.
normal.cn: 把它和 tactless 联系：两者都描述缺失的过滤。

abstract.en: What is thick cannot be penetrated by nuance.
abstract.cn: 厚的东西无法被细微之物穿透。

abstract.en: Crassness is not ignorance of the rule but indifference to it.
abstract.cn: 粗鲁不是不知道规则，而是对规则漠不关心。

abstract.en: A single crass remark can reveal a whole way of seeing.
abstract.cn: 一句粗鲁的话，就能暴露一整套看世界的方式。

examples.en: The remark was crass even by his standards.
examples.cn: 这句话按他自己的标准也算粗鲁。

examples.en: Critics called the campaign crass commercialism.
examples.cn: 批评者称这场活动是庸俗的商业主义。

examples.en: His crass ignorance of the local customs offended the hosts.
examples.cn: 他对当地习俗的愚钝无知冒犯了主人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「厚」：脸皮厚、感觉钝，什么都透不进去，就是「粗鲁、愚钝」。

root: 拉丁语 crassus（厚的、结实的）

sensesIntro.en: Crass always describes a thickness that blocks feeling or understanding; the senses differ in whether what is blocked is tact, taste, thought or texture.
sensesIntro.cn: crass 始终描述一种阻断感受或理解的「厚」；各义项的差别在于被阻断的是得体、品味、思考还是质地。

branches.en: Failure to feel or to learn what others see.
branches.cn: 感受不到或学不会他人看得见的东西。

branches.en: Vulgar display and greed rather than subtlety.
branches.cn: 低俗的展示与贪婪，而非细腻。

branches.en: Tactlessness so open it cannot be excused.
branches.cn: 露骨到无法开脱的不得体。

branches.en: The old literal sense of coarse texture.
branches.cn: 质地粗糙的古老字面义。

branches.en: Stupidity and the old theory of a dull constitution.
branches.cn: 愚钝，以及旧时关于迟钝体质的理论。

intro.en: The family is small: an adverb, a noun and two comparison forms, all carrying the same judgement.
intro.cn: 这个词族很小：一个副词、一个名词和两个比较形式，都带着同一种评判。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root describes thickness in soil and body; English moved the thickness into manners.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根描述土壤与身体之厚；英语把这种厚搬到了举止上。

items.meaning: in a manner that shows no tact
items.example: He crassly asked about her salary.
items.exampleCN: 他粗鲁地打听她的薪水。

items.example: The crassness of the joke silenced the room.
items.exampleCN: 那个玩笑的粗俗让全场安静。

items.example: The second ad was even crasser.
It was the crassest thing he had ever said.
items.exampleCN: 那是他说过的最粗俗的话。

items.example: Critics mocked the crassitude of the plot.
items.exampleCN: 批评者嘲弄情节的粗笨。

items.example: The wedding became a display of crass materialism.
items.exampleCN: 婚礼成了一场粗鄙拜金的展示。

items.example: The holiday was buried under crass commercialism.
items.exampleCN: 这个节日被庸俗的商业主义掩埋了。

items.example: He told a crass joke and lost the room.
items.exampleCN: 他讲了个低俗玩笑，失去了全场。

definition_zh: 罪责；应受责备；责任程度
definition_en: the state of being blameworthy or legally responsible for wrongdoing
core_image: 法庭上一个人低着头，手指交握，面前的桌上放着一份写满名字的报告
scene: 调查报告列出每一道被跳过的检查，最后把责任指向值班主管。The inquiry established the culpability of the shift supervisor.
sceneCN: 这里 culpability 指对失职行为应负的责任（第 2 个义项：法律责任）；句意为调查认定值班主管负有责任。

senses.title: Blameworthiness
senses.definition: the quality of deserving blame for something that went wrong
senses.definitionCN: 对出错之事应受责备的性质
senses.example: No one doubted his culpability in the failure.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人怀疑他在这项失败中应受责备。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'fault'; culpability is the condition of having a fault that can be laid at your door.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「过错」；culpability 就是拥有一个可以归到你门口的过错。

senses.title: Legal responsibility
senses.definition: responsibility for an offence as established by law or an inquiry
senses.definitionCN: 由法律或调查认定的违法责任
senses.example: The inquiry established the culpability of the shift supervisor.
senses.exampleCN: 调查认定值班主管负有责任。
senses.why: Law separates the act from the person: culpability is the bridge that lets a penalty reach a name.
senses.whyCN: 法律把行为与人分开：罪责是让惩罚能够抵达一个名字的那座桥。

senses.title: Moral responsibility
senses.definition: the sense that a person ought to have known and acted better
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人本应知道得更多、做得更好的判断
senses.example: She felt a moral culpability that no court could assign.
senses.exampleCN: 她感到一种任何法庭都无法认定的道德责任。
senses.why: Courts assign blame by rules; conscience assigns it by what a person could have done.
senses.whyCN: 法庭按规则归责；良心按一个人本可以做到的事归责。

senses.title: Degree of fault
senses.definition: how much blame a person carries relative to others
senses.definitionCN: 一个人相对于他人承担多少责任
senses.example: The report graded each official's culpability.
senses.exampleCN: 报告对每位官员的责任程度作了分级。
senses.why: When several hands touch one failure, the word asks not whether but how much.
senses.whyCN: 当多只手共同造成一次失败时，这个词问的不是有没有责任，而是有多少。

senses.title: Shared responsibility
senses.definition: blame distributed among several people or bodies
senses.definitionCN: 由若干人或机构分担的责任
senses.example: The court found shared culpability among the contractors.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定承包商之间共同负有责任。
senses.why: A system can fail through many small omissions, so the word can be used in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 一个系统可能因许多小的疏忽而失灵，因此这个词可以用复数。

senses.title: Admission of guilt
senses.definition: the act of accepting that the blame is one's own
senses.definitionCN: 接受责任属于自己的行为
senses.example: His public culpability ended the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 他公开认责，结束了争论。
senses.why: Admission turns a disputed fact into a settled one, which is why institutions resist it so long.
senses.whyCN: 承认把有争议的事实变成已定的事实，这正是机构长期抗拒它的原因。

senses.title: Responsibility in negligence
senses.definition: blame for harm caused by a failure to take reasonable care
senses.definitionCN: 因未采取合理注意而造成损害所负的责任
senses.example: The engineer's culpability lay in ignoring the test results.
senses.exampleCN: 这位工程师的责任在于无视检测结果。
senses.why: Negligence is not intent; the word can attach blame to a mind that simply did not look.
senses.whyCN: 过失不是故意；这个词可以把责任归于一个干脆没有去看的心。

senses.title: Corporate culpability
senses.definition: blame attributed to an organization rather than a single person
senses.definitionCN: 归于组织而非个人的责任
senses.example: Regulators examined the firm's culpability in the spill.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构审查该公司在泄漏事件中的责任。
senses.why: An organization has no single hand, yet the word lets blame be placed on a structure.
senses.whyCN: 组织没有单独的一只手，但这个词让责任可以被放在一个结构上。

intro.en: Culpability comes from Latin for fault, and its family includes culprit and exculpate.
intro.cn: culpability 来自拉丁语中表示「过错」的词，同族词包括 culprit 与 exculpate。

items.en: English formed culpability in the 17c. from culpable, as legal writing needed a noun for the state of being at fault.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪由 culpable 造出 culpability，因为法律文本需要一个指「有过错状态」的名词。

items.en: Culpa meant 'fault, blame, negligence', a word used in Roman law for degrees of carelessness.
items.cn: culpa 意为「过错、责备、疏忽」，罗马法用它区分不同程度的粗心。

items.en: Culpabilis meant 'blameworthy', built from culpa with an adjective ending.
items.cn: culpabilis 意为「应受责备的」，由 culpa 加形容词词尾构成。

items.en: Culprit began as an English court formula and was later heard as a single word meaning the guilty person.
items.cn: culprit 最初是英语法庭用语，后来被听成一个词，指有罪之人。

items.en: Exculpare 'to clear of blame' gives English exculpate, the opposite motion of the same root.
items.cn: exculpare「洗清责备」产生英语 exculpate，是同一词根的反向运动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the culpa root; the near-meaning group names related forms of blame.
note.cn: 形近组共享 culpa 词根；近义组列出与责备相关的各种形态。

entries.definition: deserving blame.
in a blameworthy manner.
the person responsible for an offence.
to clear someone of blame.
legal responsibility for loss or harm.
entries.definitionCN: 对损失或损害的法定责任。

entries.definition: the duty to explain and answer for one's actions.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己的行为作出解释并承担后果的义务。

entries.definition: responsibility for something wrong.
the fact of having committed an offence, or the feeling that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 犯下过错的事实，或随之而来的感受。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a name being attached to a failure.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「把某个名字挂到一次失败上」的画面留住。

normal.en: Culpa is Latin for fault; culpability is the state of having one.
normal.cn: culpa 是拉丁语「过错」；culpability 就是拥有过错的状态。

normal.en: Think of culprit: both words place a fault on a person.
normal.cn: 想一想 culprit：两个词都把过错放在某个人身上。

normal.en: Exculpate is the reverse: ex- takes the blame away.
normal.cn: exculpate 是反向的：ex- 把责任拿走。

normal.en: Say kull-puh-BIL-uh-tee, with the stress on the blame itself.
normal.cn: 读成 kull-puh-BIL-uh-tee，重音落在「责任」上。

normal.en: Link it with accountability: one names the fault, the other names the answer.
normal.cn: 把它和 accountability 联系：一个命名过错，一个命名回答。

abstract.en: Blame needs a name before it can become a penalty.
abstract.cn: 责备需要先有一个名字，才能变成惩罚。

abstract.en: The law asks how much fault, not whether someone feels sorry.
abstract.cn: 法律问的是有多少过错，而不是谁感到抱歉。

abstract.en: A structure can be blamed even without a face.
abstract.cn: 即使没有一张脸，结构也可以被归责。

examples.en: The inquiry established the culpability of the shift supervisor.
examples.cn: 调查认定值班主管负有责任。

examples.en: The report graded each official's culpability.
examples.cn: 报告对每位官员的责任程度作了分级。

examples.en: Regulators examined the firm's culpability in the spill.
examples.cn: 监管机构审查该公司在泄漏事件中的责任。

dict_mnemonic.text: culp（过错）+ ability（能力／状态）：一个人身上带着过错的状态，就是「罪责」。

root: 拉丁语 culpa（过错、疏忽）

sensesIntro.en: Culpability always answers the question of whose fault it is; the senses differ in whether the answer is moral, legal, shared or corporate.
sensesIntro.cn: culpability 始终回答「这是谁的过错」；各义项的差别在于答案属于道德、法律、共同还是企业层面。

branches.en: The bare state of deserving blame, and its moral weight.
branches.cn: 应受责备的赤裸状态及其道德分量。

branches.en: Legal and negligence-based responsibility.
branches.cn: 法律与过失基础上的责任。

branches.en: How much blame, and how it is shared.
branches.cn: 有多少责任，以及如何分担。

branches.en: The act of admitting that the fault is one's own.
branches.cn: 承认过错属于自己的行为。

branches.en: Responsibility placed on an organization.
branches.cn: 放在组织身上的责任。

intro.en: The word belongs to a legal family built on a single Latin noun for fault.
intro.cn: 这个词属于一个以单个拉丁名词「过错」为基础的法律词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin culpa and its derivatives supply the vocabulary of blame, acquittal and guilt.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 culpa 及其派生词提供了责备、开脱与罪责的词汇。

items.example: The court found the driver culpable.
The firm acted culpably in hiding the report.
items.exampleCN: 公司在隐瞒报告一事上负有责任。

items.meaning: the state of being at fault
items.example: The inquiry measured culpability by role.

items.meaning: the person charged with an offence
items.example: The culprit was identified by a camera.
items.exampleCN: 监控摄像头认出了肇事者。
新证据洗清了守卫的责任。
辩方提交了可用于开脱的录像。
这封信使两名官员受到牵连。

items.example: The prosecutor relied on inculpatory evidence.

definition_zh: 决定性的；果断的；确凿的；关键的
definition_en: settling a question or outcome, or showing the ability to decide quickly and firmly
core_image: 一枚砝码落在天平的一端，指针立刻停住，不再摆动
scene: 比赛还剩最后一分钟，他带球突破，一脚把比分定在了终点。Her decisive goal settled the match.
sceneCN: 这里 decisive 指直接决定了结果（第 1 个义项：决定性的）；句意为她那个决定性的进球定了胜负。

pos.zh: 决定性的；果断的；确凿的

senses.title: Settling the outcome
senses.definition: having the power to settle a contest or question
senses.definitionCN: 具有决定比赛或问题结果的力量
senses.example: Her decisive goal settled the match.
senses.exampleCN: 她那个决定性的进球定了胜负。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to cut off'; a decision cuts away the other possibilities, and a decisive act does so in one stroke.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「切掉」；决定切掉其他可能，而 decisive 的行为是一刀切完。

senses.title: Able to decide firmly
senses.definition: of a person, able to choose quickly and without hesitation
senses.definitionCN: 指人能迅速选择、毫不犹豫
senses.example: She is decisive under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 她在压力下很果断。
senses.why: A person who can cut off options does not linger at the fork, and the word praises that speed.
senses.whyCN: 能切掉选项的人不会在岔口徘徊，这个词赞赏的正是这种速度。

senses.title: Conclusive in evidence
senses.definition: of evidence or proof, strong enough to end doubt
senses.definitionCN: 指证据或证明强到足以终结怀疑
senses.example: The fingerprints were decisive evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 指纹是确凿的证据。
senses.why: Proof decides a case the way a verdict decides a trial: once it arrives, argument has nowhere left to go.
senses.whyCN: 证据决定案件，正如裁决决定审判：它一旦出现，争论就无处可去。

senses.title: A battle that ends a war
senses.definition: of a battle or campaign, one that determines the larger outcome
senses.definitionCN: 指决定更大结局的战役或行动
senses.example: The battle was decisive for the whole campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 这场战役对整个战局具有决定性意义。
senses.why: Not every victory changes the war; the word marks the one after which the rest is a formality.
senses.whyCN: 并非每场胜利都改变战争；这个词标记的是那一场之后其余都成形式的胜利。

senses.title: A turning moment
senses.definition: of a moment, the point at which the future is fixed
senses.definitionCN: 指未来在此被固定的时刻
senses.example: That winter was the decisive moment in his career.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冬天是他事业中的关键时刻。
senses.why: Time has joints, and the word names the one where the limb can bend no other way.
senses.whyCN: 时间有关节，而这个词命名的是那个肢体再也不能向别的方向弯曲的关节。

senses.title: A clear advantage
senses.definition: of an advantage, large or well placed enough to guarantee success
senses.definitionCN: 指优势大到或位置好到足以保证成功
senses.example: Air power gave them a decisive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 空中力量给了他们决定性优势。
senses.why: An advantage is decisive when it cannot be answered by the other side's resources.
senses.whyCN: 当对方的资源无法回应时，优势就是决定性的。

senses.title: A firm tone
senses.definition: of speech, firm and final rather than exploratory
senses.definitionCN: 指言语坚定而最终，而非试探性的
senses.example: He answered in a decisive tone that ended the discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 他用斩钉截铁的语气回答，结束了讨论。
senses.why: Tone can cut a conversation short the way a decision cuts options; nothing is left open.
senses.whyCN: 语气可以像决定切掉选项那样截断对话；没有留下任何开放之处。

senses.title: The determining factor
senses.definition: the element that determines how something else turns out
senses.definitionCN: 决定其他事物如何发展的要素
senses.example: Cost was the decisive factor in the choice.
senses.exampleCN: 成本是这一选择中的决定因素。
senses.why: Among many causes, one is decisive when removing it changes the result.
senses.whyCN: 在众多原因中，当移除某个原因会改变结果时，它就是决定性的。

intro.en: Decisive comes from a Latin verb meaning to cut off, because a decision cuts away alternatives.
intro.cn: decisive 来自一个意为「切掉」的拉丁动词，因为决定就是把其他可能切掉。

items.en: English formed decisive in the 17c. from decision, and applied it to battles, evidence and character alike.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪由 decision 造出 decisive，并把它用于战役、证据与性格。

items.en: Decisio meant 'a cutting off' and also 'a settlement', the moment when a dispute is cut short.
items.cn: decisio 意为「切掉」，也指「了结」，即争端被截断的那一刻。

items.en: Decidere combined de- 'off' with caedere 'to cut', giving 'to cut off, settle'.
items.cn: decidere 由 de-「离开」与 caedere「切」组合，意为「切掉、了结」。

items.en: Caedere 'to cut' also gives cement, incision and concise, all built on cutting.
items.cn: caedere「切」也产生 cement、incision 与 concise，都以「切」为基底。

items.en: The metaphor widened from legal settlement to character: a decisive person is one who can cut off hesitation.
items.cn: 这个比喻从法律了结扩展到性格：果断的人就是能切掉犹豫的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the decision stem; the near-meaning group names kinds of finality.
note.cn: 形近组共享 decision 词干；近义组列出各种终结性。

entries.definition: a choice or a settlement reached.
entries.definitionCN: 作出的选择或达成的了结。

entries.definition: in a way that settles or acts firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 以决定性或果断的方式。

entries.definition: the quality of acting firmly or settling matters.
entries.definitionCN: 行动果断或了结事情的性质。

entries.definition: unable to decide, or not settling anything.
entries.definitionCN: 无法决定，或不能了结任何事。

entries.definition: putting an end to doubt or argument.
having the power to fix how something ends.
entries.definitionCN: 有力量固定事物如何收场。

entries.definition: firm and unwavering in a decision already made.
entries.definitionCN: 对已作的决定坚定不动摇。

entries.definition: at a point where the outcome is decided.
entries.definitionCN: 处于结局被决定的关口。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a blade cutting away every other option.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「刀刃把其他选项全部切掉」的画面留住。

normal.en: Decide and decisive share the Latin image of cutting off: one stroke, no options left.
normal.cn: decide 与 decisive 共享拉丁语「切掉」的意象：一刀下去，没剩别的选项。

normal.en: Picture a scale that stops swinging the moment the weight lands.
normal.cn: 想象天平在砝码落下的那一刻停止摆动。

normal.en: A decisive person does not stand at the fork counting roads.
normal.cn: 果断的人不会站在岔口数路。

normal.en: Say dih-SY-siv, with the stress on the cut.
normal.cn: 读成 dih-SY-siv，重音落在那一刀上。

normal.en: Link it with conclusive: both end the argument.
normal.cn: 把它和 conclusive 联系：两者都终结争论。

abstract.en: A choice is a cut; hesitation is the blade that will not fall.
abstract.cn: 选择是一次切割；犹豫就是不肯落下的刀。

abstract.en: One cause is decisive when removing it changes everything.
abstract.cn: 当移除某个原因会改变一切时，它就是决定性的。

abstract.en: Finality can live in a tone as well as in a battle.
abstract.cn: 终结性既可以活在战役里，也可以活在语气里。

examples.en: Her decisive goal settled the match.
examples.cn: 她那个决定性的进球定了胜负。

examples.en: The fingerprints were decisive evidence.
examples.cn: 指纹是确凿的证据。

examples.en: Cost was the decisive factor in the choice.
examples.cn: 成本是这一选择中的决定因素。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（离开）+ cis（切）：把其他可能都切掉、只留一个，就是「果断、决定性」。

root: 拉丁语 decidere（切掉、了结）：de-（离开）+ caedere（切）

sensesIntro.en: Decisive always means that alternatives have been cut away; the senses differ in whether the cutting is done by an event, a person, a proof or a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: decisive 始终表示其他选项已被切掉；各义项的差别在于这一刀是由事件、人、证据还是原因落下的。

branches.en: Outcomes and battles that settle a larger contest.
branches.cn: 了结更大争夺的结果与战役。

branches.en: The personal and vocal firmness of a decided mind.
branches.cn: 已决之心在个人与语气上的坚定。

branches.en: Proof strong enough to end doubt.
branches.cn: 强到足以终结怀疑的证据。

branches.en: Turning moments and advantages that fix the future.
branches.cn: 固定未来的关键时刻与优势。

branches.en: The one cause whose removal changes the result.
branches.cn: 移除后便改变结果的那个原因。

intro.en: The word belongs to a family built on cutting: decide, decision, decisive and their negatives.
intro.cn: 这个词属于一个以「切」为基础建立的词族：decide、decision、decisive 及其否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin caedere 'to cut' supplies a whole set of English words about endings and precision.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caedere「切」提供了一整组关于终结与精确的英语词。

items.meaning: to cut off options and choose
items.example: They decided to postpone the launch.

items.meaning: the act or result of choosing
items.exampleCN: 决定是一夜之间作出的。

items.example: The indecisive reply cost them the deal.
items.exampleCN: 含糊的答复让他们失去了交易。

definition_zh: 描绘；描述；刻画；表现
definition_en: to show or represent something in a picture, a story or words
core_image: 一支笔在纸上落下第一道线，一个侧脸渐渐有了轮廓
scene: 墙上那幅画里，渔民正把网从水里拉起，绳索绷得很紧。The painting depicts fishermen hauling in their nets.
sceneCN: 这里 depict 指用图像表现一个场景（第 1 个义项：用图像描绘）；句意为这幅画描绘渔民收网的场景。

senses.title: Show in a picture
senses.definition: to represent a scene or person in a painting, drawing or photograph
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画、素描或照片中表现场景或人物
senses.example: The painting depicts fishermen hauling in their nets.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画描绘渔民收网的场景。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to paint'; the hand and the pigment are the oldest part of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「绘画」；手与颜料是这个词最古老的部分。

senses.title: Describe in words
senses.definition: to describe something in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 用言语或文字描述某事物
senses.example: The novel depicts village life in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说描述了上个世纪的乡村生活。
senses.why: Words paint too: the same verb serves the brush and the pen because both make a scene visible.
senses.whyCN: 文字也在作画：同一个动词服务画笔与钢笔，因为两者都让场景变得可见。

senses.title: Portray a character
senses.definition: to present a person in a story with particular traits
senses.definitionCN: 在故事中呈现具有特定特征的人物
senses.example: The author depicts her as generous but proud.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把她刻画得慷慨却骄傲。
senses.why: A character is built line by line, and the word covers the accumulation of those lines.
senses.whyCN: 人物是一笔一笔建起来的，这个词涵盖的就是这些笔画的累积。

senses.title: Represent symbolically
senses.definition: to stand for something larger through an image
senses.definitionCN: 通过图像代表更宏大的事物
senses.example: The mural depicts peace as a white bird over ruins.
senses.exampleCN: 壁画把和平表现为废墟上的一只白鸟。
senses.why: A symbol is a picture that carries more than it shows, and depiction is how that load is attached.
senses.whyCN: 象征是一幅承载多于其所显示之物的画，而描绘就是附上这份重量的方式。

senses.title: Present a scene vividly
senses.definition: to set a scene before the reader's or viewer's mind
senses.definitionCN: 把场景呈现在读者或观者心中
senses.example: The opening chapter depicts a storm at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 开篇一章呈现了海上风暴。
senses.why: Vividness depends on selection: a few details make the whole scene appear.
senses.whyCN: 生动取决于取舍：少数细节就能让整个场景浮现。

senses.title: Reflect accurately
senses.definition: to show something as it really is, without distortion
senses.definitionCN: 不失真地显示事物的真实样貌
senses.example: The report depicts conditions in the camp honestly.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告如实反映了营地里的状况。
senses.why: When accuracy is the goal, depiction becomes a test of honesty rather than skill.
senses.whyCN: 当目标是准确时，描绘就成了对诚实的检验，而不只是对技巧的检验。

senses.title: Portray in a certain light
senses.definition: to present someone or something with a chosen bias
senses.definitionCN: 带着选定的偏向呈现某人或某物
senses.example: The article depicts the reform as a disaster.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把改革描绘成一场灾难。
senses.why: Every depiction chooses an angle, and the choice can be innocent or deliberate.
senses.whyCN: 每一种描绘都选了一个角度，而这个选择可以无辜，也可以是有意。

senses.title: Graphic representation
senses.definition: to represent data or structure by a diagram
senses.definitionCN: 用图表表现数据或结构
senses.example: The chart depicts the fall in prices over a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图展示了价格一年内的下跌。
senses.why: A diagram is depiction stripped to relations: no faces, only lines that show what connects to what.
senses.whyCN: 图表是被剥到只剩关系的描绘：没有面孔，只有显示连接关系的线。

intro.en: Depict comes from a Latin verb meaning to paint, and painting remains its core image.
intro.cn: depict 来自一个意为「绘画」的拉丁动词，绘画始终是它的核心意象。

items.en: English borrowed depict in the 17c. for painting and later extended it to writing and diagrams.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 depict，指绘画，后来扩展到文字与图表。

items.en: Depingere meant 'to paint, portray', built from de- and pingere 'to paint'.
items.cn: depingere 意为「绘画、描绘」，由 de- 与 pingere「画」构成。

items.en: Pingere 'to paint' also gives picture and pigment, both about colour laid on a surface.
items.cn: pingere「画」也产生 picture 与 pigment，两者都关于涂在表面上的颜色。

items.en: Pictura meant 'painting' and supplied English pictura and pictorial through other routes.
items.cn: pictura 意为「绘画」，并通过其他路径提供英语的 pictorial 等词。

items.en: The verb widened from canvas to language, so that a sentence can depict a scene no one has painted.
items.cn: 这个动词从画布扩展到语言，于是一句话也可以描绘无人画过的场景。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pict stem; the near-meaning group names ways of showing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 pict 词干；近义组列出各种呈现方式。

entries.definition: a picture or description of something.
shown in a picture or words.
entries.definitionCN: 在图画或文字中显示的。

entries.definition: serving to represent something.
expressed in pictures rather than words.
entries.definitionCN: 以图画而非文字表达的。

entries.definition: to show a person or thing in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 以特定方式表现人或物。

entries.definition: to give a spoken or written account of something.
entries.definitionCN: 用口头或书面方式叙述某物。

entries.definition: to make something clear by examples or pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 用例子或图画使某物清楚。

entries.definition: to represent something in a particular medium or style.
entries.definitionCN: 以特定媒介或风格表现某物。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a hand making the first line of a face.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「一只手画出一张脸的第一道线」的画面留住。

normal.en: Depict shares a root with picture: both come from the Latin verb to paint.
normal.cn: depict 与 picture 同根：两者都来自拉丁语「画」的动词。

normal.en: Picture a painter blocking in a face with three strokes.
normal.cn: 想象画家用三笔勾出一张脸的轮廓。

normal.en: A diagram is a depiction with no faces, only connections.
normal.cn: 图表是没有面孔的描绘，只有连接。

normal.en: Say dih-PIKT, like a brush tapping the canvas.
normal.cn: 读成 dih-PIKT，像画笔点在画布上。

normal.en: Link it with describe: one paints for the eye, the other for the ear.
normal.cn: 把它和 describe 联系：一个为眼睛作画，一个为耳朵叙述。

abstract.en: Every depiction chooses an angle and leaves something out.
abstract.cn: 每一种描绘都选了一个角度，并遗漏了某些东西。

abstract.en: Words can paint a scene no one has ever seen.
abstract.cn: 文字可以画出无人见过的场景。

abstract.en: Accuracy in depiction is a form of honesty.
abstract.cn: 描绘中的准确，是一种诚实。

examples.en: The painting depicts fishermen hauling in their nets.
examples.cn: 这幅画描绘渔民收网的场景。

examples.en: The novel depicts village life in the last century.
examples.cn: 这部小说描述了上个世纪的乡村生活。

examples.en: The chart depicts the fall in prices over a year.
examples.cn: 这张图展示了价格一年内的下跌。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（向下）+ pict（画）：把形象画下来，就是「描绘」。

root: 拉丁语 depingere（绘画）：de- + pingere（画）

sensesIntro.en: Depict always makes something visible, whether to the eye or to the mind; the senses differ in the medium and in the honesty of the showing.
sensesIntro.cn: depict 始终让某物变得可见，无论对眼睛还是对心智；各义项的差别在于媒介，以及这种显示是否诚实。

branches.en: Pictures and vivid scenes made for the eye.
branches.cn: 为眼睛而作的图画与生动场景。

branches.en: Words that build a scene or a person.
branches.cn: 构建场景或人物的文字。

branches.en: Images that carry a meaning larger than themselves.
branches.cn: 承载着大于自身的意义的图像。

branches.en: Honest or slanted versions of the same thing.
branches.cn: 同一事物诚实或有偏向的版本。

branches.en: Diagrams that show only relations.
branches.cn: 只显示关系的图表。

intro.en: The word's family is built on the Latin verb for painting.
intro.cn: 这个词的词族建立在拉丁语「绘画」动词之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin pingere and pictura supply several English words about images and colour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pingere 与 pictura 提供了若干关于图像与颜色的英语词。

items.meaning: the act or result of showing
items.example: The film's depiction of war is restrained.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影对战争的表现很克制。

items.meaning: shown in an image or account
items.meaningCN: 在图像或叙述中显示的
items.example: The scene is depicted in three panels.
items.exampleCN: 这个场景被画在三块板上。

items.example: A fresco depicting the harvest covers the wall.
items.exampleCN: 一幅描绘收获的壁画覆盖整面墙。
摄影是一种再现性的媒介。

items.example: The depicter of court life was a minor painter.
items.exampleCN: 这位描绘宫廷生活的人是个小画家。

items.example: The magazine is famous for its pictorial coverage.
items.exampleCN: 这本杂志以图片报道闻名。

items.example: The village is almost too picturesque.
items.exampleCN: 这个村庄几乎美得像画。
有些悲伤几乎无法表现。

definition_zh: 荒凉的；无人居住的；孤寂的；使荒芜
definition_en: empty and ruined, or deeply unhappy and alone; as a verb, to lay waste
core_image: 一扇没有玻璃的窗，风穿过空屋，地上只有碎瓦和干草
scene: 车开了很久，窗外只剩断墙和被风翻起的黄土。They walked through a desolate village with no sign of life.
sceneCN: 这里 desolate 指地方荒凉、无人居住（第 1 个义项：荒凉无人）；句意为他们走过一个毫无生命迹象的荒村。

senses.title: Empty and ruined
senses.definition: of a place, empty, broken down and without people
senses.definitionCN: 指地方空荡、破败、无人居住
senses.example: They walked through a desolate village with no sign of life.
senses.exampleCN: 他们走过一个毫无生命迹象的荒村。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to leave alone'; a desolate place is one that has been abandoned by its people.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「使孤单」；荒凉之地就是被人遗弃的地方。

senses.title: Bare and barren
senses.definition: of land, unable to support plants or animals
senses.definitionCN: 指土地无法供养植物或动物
senses.example: The desert is beautiful but desolate.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沙漠美丽却荒芜。
senses.why: Abandonment and barrenness meet here: nothing grows because nothing stays.
senses.whyCN: 遗弃与贫瘠在此相遇：没有东西生长，因为没有东西留下。

senses.title: Deeply lonely
senses.definition: of a person, feeling utterly alone and without comfort
senses.definitionCN: 指人感到彻底孤独、无所慰藉
senses.example: He felt desolate after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后他感到无比孤寂。
senses.why: A place becomes a feeling: the empty room outside is reproduced as an empty room inside.
senses.whyCN: 地方变成感受：外面的空房间，被复制成内心的空房间。

senses.title: Devastated by loss
senses.definition: overcome by grief at a loss
senses.definitionCN: 因失去而陷入极度悲伤
senses.example: She was desolate when the letters stopped coming.
senses.exampleCN: 来信中断后，她悲痛欲绝。
senses.why: Grief empties the inner landscape, which is why the same word serves both a ruin and a mourner.
senses.whyCN: 悲伤清空了内心的风景，这就是同一个词既能指废墟、又能指哀悼者的原因。

senses.title: A bleak prospect
senses.definition: of a future, offering no comfort or growth
senses.definitionCN: 指未来没有安慰或成长的可能
senses.example: The report painted a desolate future for the town.
senses.exampleCN: 报告为这座小镇描绘了暗淡的未来。
senses.why: Time can be barren too: a future with nothing growing in it looks like a wasteland.
senses.whyCN: 时间也可以贫瘠：一个没有东西生长的未来，看上去就像荒地。

senses.title: To lay waste
senses.definition: as a verb, to destroy a place so that it becomes empty
senses.definitionCN: 作动词，指毁坏某地使其空无
senses.example: War desolated the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 战争使整个山谷变成废墟。
senses.why: The verb restores the cause: someone did the abandoning, and the word records the act.
senses.whyCN: 动词恢复了原因：是有人造成了遗弃，而这个词记录了那个行为。

senses.title: To leave abandoned
senses.definition: as a verb, to leave people or a place without support
senses.definitionCN: 作动词，指使人们或某地失去支持
senses.example: The policy desolated the fishing communities.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策使渔业社区陷入遗弃境地。
senses.why: Abandonment can be a decree rather than an event, and the verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 遗弃可以是一纸命令而非一起事件，动词涵盖了两者。

senses.title: To make miserable
senses.definition: as a verb, to make a person feel utterly alone
senses.definitionCN: 作动词，指使某人感到彻底孤独
senses.example: The silence desolated him more than any argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这沉默比任何争吵都更使他孤寂。
senses.why: The inner sense of the verb closes the circle: a place can desolate a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词的内在义项闭合了这个循环：一个地方可以使一个人变得孤寂。

intro.en: Desolate comes from a Latin verb meaning to leave alone, and solitude is the thread through all its senses.
intro.cn: desolate 来自一个意为「使孤单」的拉丁动词，孤独是贯穿它所有义项的线。

items.en: English borrowed both adjective and verb in the 14c. from Latin, and used them for ruined places and ruined spirits.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪从拉丁语借入形容词与动词，用于被毁的地方与被毁的精神。

items.en: Desolare meant 'to leave alone, abandon', built from de- and solus 'alone'.
items.cn: desolare 意为「使孤单、遗弃」，由 de- 与 solus「独自」构成。

items.en: Solus 'alone' also gives solitude, solitary and solo, all about being one.
items.cn: solus「独自」也产生 solitude、solitary 与 solo，都与「单一」有关。

items.en: Desolatus meant 'abandoned, laid waste', the participle that became the English adjective.
items.cn: desolatus 意为「被遗弃的、被毁的」，这个分词后来成为英语形容词。

items.en: The word lives two lives in English: a place can be desolate, and a person can be desolated by grief.
items.cn: 这个词在英语里有双重生活：地方可以是荒凉的，人也可以因悲伤而变得孤寂。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sol root; the near-meaning group names kinds of emptiness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sol 词根；近义组列出各种空无。

entries.definition: ruin, emptiness or deep loneliness.
in a bleak and lonely way.
the state of being alone.
done or living alone.
unable to produce plants or young.
entries.definitionCN: 无法长出植物或后代的。

entries.definition: cold, empty and offering no comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 寒冷、空荡、不给人安慰的。

entries.definition: left alone and pitiful.
ruined or overwhelmed by shock and grief.
entries.definitionCN: 被毁的，或被震惊与悲伤压垮的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of an empty house with wind passing through.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「风穿过空屋」的画面留住。

normal.en: Sol means alone: desolate is what is left when everyone and everything has gone.
normal.cn: sol 意为独自：desolate 就是人和万物都离开后剩下的样子。

normal.en: Picture a window with no glass and a floor covered in broken tiles.
normal.cn: 想象一扇没有玻璃的窗，地上铺满碎瓦。

normal.en: The same word serves a ruined town and a grieving person.
normal.cn: 同一个词既服务被毁的城镇，也服务哀伤的人。

normal.en: Say DES-uh-lut as an adjective, DES-uh-layt as a verb.
normal.cn: 形容词读 DES-uh-lut，动词读 DES-uh-layt。

normal.en: Link it with solitude: one is chosen, the other is imposed.
normal.cn: 把它和 solitude 联系：一个是自愿的，一个是被强加的。

abstract.en: Emptiness outside and emptiness inside borrow the same word.
abstract.cn: 外面的空与内心的空，借用同一个词。

abstract.en: Grief empties the inner landscape the way war empties a valley.
abstract.cn: 悲伤清空内心风景，正如战争清空山谷。

abstract.en: A desolate future is a wasteland measured in time.
abstract.cn: 暗淡的未来，是以时间度量的荒地。

examples.en: They walked through a desolate village with no sign of life.
examples.cn: 他们走过一个毫无生命迹象的荒村。

examples.en: He felt desolate after the funeral.
examples.cn: 葬礼之后他感到无比孤寂。

examples.en: War desolated the whole valley.
examples.cn: 战争使整个山谷变成废墟。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（加强）+ sol（独自）：只剩下一个人、一个空地方，就是「荒凉、孤寂」。

root: 拉丁语 desolare（使孤单、遗弃）：de- + solus（独自）

sensesIntro.en: Desolate always records an absence; the senses differ in whether what is missing is people, growth, comfort or hope.
sensesIntro.cn: desolate 始终记录一种缺席；各义项的差别在于缺失的是人、生长、慰藉还是希望。

branches.en: Places that are empty or cannot support life.
branches.cn: 空荡或无法供养生命的地方。

branches.en: Loneliness and grief inside a person.
branches.cn: 一个人内心的孤独与悲伤。

branches.en: A future with nothing growing in it.
branches.cn: 没有东西生长的未来。

branches.en: The act of laying waste or abandoning.
branches.cn: 使荒芜或遗弃的行为。

branches.en: A place or silence that makes a person feel alone.
branches.cn: 使一个人感到孤独的地方或沉默。

intro.en: The word shares its root with the vocabulary of solitude, which helps separate chosen aloneness from imposed emptiness.
intro.cn: 这个词与「独处」词汇共享词根，有助于区分自愿的独处与被强加的空无。

latinIntro.en: Latin solus 'alone' gives a whole family of English words about being one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 solus「独自」给出了一整族关于「单一」的英语词。

items.example: The desolation of the camp shocked the visitors.
items.exampleCN: 营地的荒凉让来访者震惊。

items.example: The house stood desolately at the end of the road.
items.exampleCN: 那座房子孤零零地立在路的尽头。

items.example: The storm desolated the coastal farms.
items.exampleCN: 风暴摧毁了沿海的农田。

items.example: It was a desolating piece of news.
items.exampleCN: 那是一条令人心碎的消息。

items.example: He sought solitude in the hills.
A solitary figure walked the beach.
items.exampleCN: 一个孤独的身影走在海滩上。

items.example: She sang a solo at the concert.

items.exampleCN: 哈姆雷特的独白显露他的悲伤。

definition_zh: 减损；贬低；有损于；分散（注意）
definition_en: to reduce the value, quality or reputation of something
core_image: 一面完好的墙上被划出一道浅痕，整面墙看上去都不再完整
scene: 那道裂缝本来很小，但每次有人经过都会先看它一眼。A few scratches detract from the beauty of the table.
sceneCN: 这里 detract 指使某物的美感减损（第 1 个义项：减损价值）；句意为几道划痕有损这张桌子的美感。

senses.title: Reduce value or quality
senses.definition: to make something less valuable or less good
senses.definitionCN: 使某物价值降低或品质变差
senses.example: A few scratches detract from the beauty of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 几道划痕有损这张桌子的美感。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to draw away'; value is drawn off the way water is drawn from a full vessel.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「拉走」；价值被拉走，就像水从满的容器里被舀出。

senses.title: Diminish an achievement
senses.definition: to make an accomplishment seem smaller than it is
senses.definitionCN: 使一项成就显得比实际更小
senses.example: Nothing can detract from what the team achieved.
senses.exampleCN: 没有什么能贬低这个团队所取得的成就。
senses.why: Praise adds weight, and detraction removes it; the same scale is used in both directions.
senses.whyCN: 赞扬增加分量，贬低则移除分量；两个方向用的是同一杆秤。

senses.title: Spoil a pleasing quality
senses.definition: to lessen the pleasure or attractiveness of something
senses.definitionCN: 减少某物的愉悦感或吸引力
senses.example: The noisy road detracts from the charm of the house.
