senses.exampleCN: 嘈杂的道路有损这座房子的魅力。
senses.why: Charm is a delicate balance; one wrong element pulls the whole composition down.
senses.whyCN: 魅力是一种精细的平衡；一个不对的元素就把整个构图拉低。

senses.title: Divert attention
senses.definition: to draw attention away from the main matter
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力从主要事情上引开
senses.example: Constant notifications detract attention from the work.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的通知分散了对工作的注意。
senses.why: Attention is a finite beam; whatever detracts turns part of it elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是一束有限的光；任何减损都把其中一部分转向别处。

senses.title: Speak disparagingly
senses.definition: to speak of someone in a way that lowers their standing
senses.definitionCN: 以降低他人地位的方式谈论某人
senses.example: He never missed a chance to detract from his rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不放过贬低对手的机会。
senses.why: Words can remove value from a reputation as surely as scratches remove it from a table.
senses.whyCN: 言语能从名声上拿走价值，正如划痕能从桌子上拿走价值。

senses.title: Harm a reputation
senses.definition: to damage the good name of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 损害个人或团体的好名声
senses.example: The scandal detracted from the university's reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻损害了这所大学的声誉。
senses.why: Reputation is held by others, so it can be lowered by talk even when nothing has changed.
senses.whyCN: 声誉由他人持有，因此即使事实未变，也能被言论拉低。

senses.title: Lessen enjoyment
senses.definition: to reduce the pleasure of an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 减少某个场合的乐趣
senses.example: One rude guest detracted from the whole evening.
senses.exampleCN: 一个无礼的客人破坏了整个夜晚。
senses.why: Pleasure is a total made of many small contributions, and one rude guest removes more than their own share.
senses.whyCN: 愉悦由许多小的贡献构成一个总数，而一个无礼的客人拿走的比他自己那一份更多。

senses.title: Subtract, in old use
senses.definition: in older mathematics, to take away a quantity
senses.definitionCN: 在旧时数学中，减去一个量
senses.example: The old text says to detract three from ten.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文本说从十中减去三。
senses.why: The arithmetic sense is the literal skeleton: detraction is subtraction applied to value.
senses.whyCN: 算术义是字面的骨架：减损就是把减法用在价值上。

intro.en: Detract comes from a Latin verb meaning to draw away, and the image of subtraction runs through every sense.
intro.cn: detract 来自一个意为「拉走」的拉丁动词，「减法」的意象贯穿所有义项。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 15c. and fixed the phrase detract from for value and reputation.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，并用 detract from 固定搭配表示价值与声誉的减损。

items.en: Detrahere meant 'to draw off, take away', from de- 'away' and trahere 'to draw'.
items.cn: detrahere 意为「拉走、拿走」，由 de-「离开」与 trahere「拉」构成。

items.en: Trahere 'to draw' also gives traction, tractor and attract, all about pulling.
items.cn: trahere「拉」也产生 traction、tractor 与 attract，都与拖拉有关。

items.en: Detractio meant 'a taking away', used for both subtraction and slander.
items.cn: detractio 意为「拿走」，既用于减法，也用于诽谤。

items.en: The word moved from arithmetic to reputation: to detract from a person is to subtract from their standing.
items.cn: 这个词从算术移到声誉：贬低一个人，就是从其地位中减去。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tract root; the near-meaning group names kinds of reduction.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tract 词根；近义组列出各种削减。

entries.definition: the act of belittling or reducing value.
entries.definitionCN: 贬低或减损价值的行为。

entries.definition: someone who criticizes and lessens another's worth.
entries.definitionCN: 批评并贬低他人价值的人。

entries.definition: taking value or attention away.
to draw something toward oneself.
to make something seem or become smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物显得或变得更小。

entries.definition: to weaken something gradually and indirectly.
to speak of someone or something as unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人或某物说得不重要。

entries.definition: to reduce the quality or value of something.
entries.definitionCN: 降低某物的品质或价值。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a scratch on an otherwise perfect surface.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「完好表面上的一道划痕」这一画面留住。

normal.en: Tract means to draw; detract means to draw value away.
normal.cn: tract 意为拉；detract 就是把价值拉走。

normal.en: Think of a subtraction sign in front of a reputation.
normal.cn: 想象在声誉前面放一个减号。

normal.en: Picture a fine table with one deep scratch; the eye keeps returning to it.
normal.cn: 想象一张好桌子上有一道深划痕；目光总回到那里。

normal.en: Say dih-TRAKT, one clean pull away from the whole.
normal.cn: 读成 dih-TRAKT，从整体上干净地拉走一次。

normal.en: Link it with diminish: both make the total smaller.
normal.cn: 把它和 diminish 联系：两者都让总量变小。

abstract.en: Value can be removed without anything being taken.
abstract.cn: 不必拿走任何东西，价值也能被移除。

abstract.en: A single wrong element can pull down a whole composition.
abstract.cn: 一个不对的元素就能拉低整个构图。

abstract.en: Slander is subtraction performed on a person's standing.
abstract.cn: 诽谤就是在人的地位上做减法。

examples.en: A few scratches detract from the beauty of the table.
examples.cn: 几道划痕有损这张桌子的美感。

examples.en: The noisy road detracts from the charm of the house.
examples.cn: 嘈杂的道路有损这座房子的魅力。

examples.en: The scandal detracted from the university's reputation.
examples.cn: 丑闻损害了这所大学的声誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（离开）+ tract（拉）：把价值或注意力拉走，就是「减损」。

root: 拉丁语 detrahere（拉走）：de-（离开）+ trahere（拉）

sensesIntro.en: Detract always takes something away from a whole; the senses differ in whether what is removed is value, standing, pleasure or attention.
sensesIntro.cn: detract 始终从整体上拿走一点东西；各义项的差别在于被拿走的是价值、地位、乐趣还是注意力。

branches.en: Beauty and quality reduced by a small flaw.
branches.cn: 被小瑕疵削减的美感与品质。

branches.en: Achievements and rivals measured downward by talk.
branches.cn: 被言论压低的分量与对手。

branches.en: Attention pulled away from the main matter.
branches.cn: 从主要事情上被拉走的注意力。

branches.en: Reputations and occasions that lose their shine.
branches.cn: 失去光彩的声誉与场合。

branches.en: The old arithmetic sense of subtracting.
branches.cn: 减去的古老算术义。

intro.en: The word belongs to the tract family, where every member involves pulling.
intro.cn: 这个词属于 tract 词族，其中每个成员都涉及「拉」。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere 'to draw' supplies a large family of English words about pulling and dragging.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere「拉」提供了大量关于拖拉的英语词。

items.meaning: the act of taking value away
items.example: The article was a long detraction of his career.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章是对他职业生涯的长篇贬损。

items.example: His detractors called the plan naive.
items.exampleCN: 贬低他的人称这个计划天真。

items.example: The fence is detracting from the view.
The remarks were detractive rather than helpful.
items.exampleCN: 这些话是贬损性的，而非有帮助的。

items.example: The exhibit attracts thousands of visitors.
items.exampleCN: 这个展览吸引成千上万的参观者。

items.example: The tires lost traction on the ice.
items.exampleCN: 轮胎在冰上失去了抓地力。

items.example: The tractor pulled the broken cart.
items.exampleCN: 拖拉机拉走了坏掉的车。

items.example: The idea is too abstract to picture.
items.exampleCN: 这个观念太抽象，难以想象。

definition_zh: 洞察力；辨别力；鉴赏力；明断
definition_en: the ability to judge well and to see differences that others miss
core_image: 两杯几乎一样的茶摆在面前，她端起来闻了一下，就指出了哪一杯多放了一片叶子
scene: 两份合同只差一个词，他翻了两遍就指出了那一处。Her discernment saved the company from a costly mistake.
sceneCN: 这里 discernment 指看出细微差别并作出正确判断的能力（第 2 个义项：辨别力）；句意为她的辨别力使公司免于一次代价高昂的错误。

senses.title: Good judgement
senses.definition: the ability to form sound judgements about people and situations
senses.definitionCN: 对人与情境作出可靠判断的能力
senses.example: The board trusted her discernment on hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会在招聘上信任她的判断力。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to separate'; judgement begins by separating one thing from another.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「分开」；判断始于把一物与另一物分开。

senses.title: Perceiving fine differences
senses.definition: the ability to notice small distinctions that others overlook
senses.definitionCN: 察觉他人忽略的细微差别的能力
senses.example: Her discernment saved the company from a costly mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 她的辨别力使公司免于一次代价高昂的错误。
senses.why: A difference must be seen before it can be judged, so perception comes first and judgement follows.
senses.whyCN: 差别必须先被看见才能被判断，因此知觉在前，判断在后。

senses.title: Refined taste
senses.definition: the ability to recognize quality in art, food or design
senses.definitionCN: 识别艺术、食物或设计中品质的能力
senses.example: His discernment in wine was famous among collectors.
senses.exampleCN: 他在葡萄酒上的鉴赏力在收藏家之间很有名。
senses.why: Taste is discrimination applied to pleasure: the palate separates the good from the merely expensive.
senses.whyCN: 品味是把辨别力用在愉悦上：味觉把好的与仅仅昂贵的分开。

senses.title: Moral insight
senses.definition: the capacity to judge right and wrong in complex cases
senses.definitionCN: 在复杂情形中判断是非的能力
senses.example: The novel asks for moral discernment, not easy answers.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说要求道德见识，而非轻易的答案。
senses.why: Moral cases rarely come labelled, so the word describes the eye that reads them.
senses.whyCN: 道德情形很少带着标签，因此这个词描述的是读懂它们的眼力。

senses.title: Spiritual insight
senses.definition: in religious writing, the ability to perceive truth or guidance
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教文本中，察觉真理或指引的能力
senses.example: The abbot was consulted for his spiritual discernment.
senses.exampleCN: 人们因这位院长的精神洞察力而向他请教。
senses.why: Religious use adds a hidden order: the discerning person sees what is not obvious to the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 宗教用法加上了隐藏的秩序：有辨别力的人看见众人看不明显的东西。

senses.title: Judicial understanding
senses.definition: the quality of a judge who weighs evidence wisely
senses.definitionCN: 法官明智权衡证据的素质
senses.example: The ruling showed careful discernment of the facts.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决显示出对事实的审慎明断。
senses.why: A judge separates claims from proofs, which is the oldest image inside the word.
senses.whyCN: 法官把主张与证据分开，这是这个词内部最古老的意象。

senses.title: Sensitive reading of a text
senses.definition: the ability to read a text or situation accurately and with nuance
senses.definitionCN: 准确而细腻地解读文本或情境的能力
senses.example: Her discernment of the poem's tone impressed the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这首诗语调的敏锐解读让全班佩服。
senses.why: Reading between lines is literal discernment: the important text is often the space between.
senses.whyCN: 读出言外之意就是字面上的辨别：重要的文本常常在行间。

senses.title: Perceptual discrimination
senses.definition: the sensory ability to tell similar things apart
senses.definitionCN: 从感官上区分相似事物的能力
senses.example: A taster's discernment depends on years of practice.
senses.exampleCN: 品鉴者的分辨力依赖多年练习。
senses.why: The last sense is the ground floor: before judgement, there is the trained eye or tongue.
senses.whyCN: 最后一个义项是底层：在判断之前，先有训练过的眼或舌。

intro.en: Discernment comes from a Latin verb meaning to separate, because judging begins with telling things apart.
intro.cn: discernment 来自一个意为「分开」的拉丁动词，因为判断始于把事物区分开。

items.en: English formed discernment in the 16c. from discern, and used it for judgement in law, morals and taste.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪由 discern 造出 discernment，用于法律、道德与品味上的判断。

items.en: Discernere meant 'to separate, distinguish', from dis- 'apart' and cernere 'to sift'.
items.cn: discernere 意为「分开、区分」，由 dis-「分开」与 cernere「筛」构成。

items.en: Cernere 'to sift, decide' also gives certain and secret through different paths.
items.cn: cernere「筛、判定」也通过不同路径产生 certain 与 secret。

items.en: A discerniculum was a hairpin, a small tool for separating strands: the image of parting is very old.
items.cn: discerniculum 是发簪，用来分开发丝的小工具：分开的意象非常古老。

items.en: The word now covers perception, taste and moral judgement, all versions of separating the better from the rest.
items.cn: 这个词现在涵盖知觉、品味与道德判断，都是把较好的与其余分开的版本。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the discern stem; the near-meaning group names kinds of wise perception.
note.cn: 形近组共享 discern 词干；近义组列出明智知觉的各种形态。

entries.definition: to perceive or distinguish something.
showing good judgement.
able to be perceived.
impossible to tell apart or perceive.
a deep and accurate understanding of something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物深入而准确的理解。

entries.definition: the ability to make sensible decisions.
the ability to notice and understand things.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉与理解事物的能力。

entries.definition: the ability to recognize what is good or beautiful.
entries.definitionCN: 识别好或美的事物的能力。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of two almost identical cups being told apart.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「两只几乎一样的杯子被分辨出来」的画面留住。

normal.en: Discern means to separate; discernment is the skill of separating what looks the same.
normal.cn: discern 意为分开；discernment 就是把看似相同之物分开的本领。

normal.en: Picture a taster who notices one extra leaf in a cup.
normal.cn: 想象一位品鉴者察觉杯里多了一片叶子。

normal.en: Think of a judge sifting claims from proofs.
normal.cn: 想象法官把主张与证据筛分开。

normal.en: Say dih-SURN-munt, with the stress on the separating.
normal.cn: 读成 dih-SURN-munt，重音落在「分开」上。

normal.en: Link it with insight: one sees deeper, the other sees finer.
normal.cn: 把它和 insight 联系：一个看得更深，一个看得更细。

abstract.en: Judgement begins the moment two things are told apart.
abstract.cn: 判断始于两物被区分开的那一刻。

abstract.en: Taste is discernment applied to pleasure.
abstract.cn: 品味是把辨别力用在愉悦上。

abstract.en: The most important text is often the space between the lines.
abstract.cn: 最重要的文本常常在行间。

examples.en: Her discernment saved the company from a costly mistake.
examples.cn: 她的辨别力使公司免于一次代价高昂的错误。

examples.en: The board trusted her discernment on hiring.
examples.cn: 董事会在招聘上信任她的判断力。

examples.en: The ruling showed careful discernment of the facts.
examples.cn: 这项裁决显示出对事实的审慎明断。

dict_mnemonic.text: dis（分开）+ cern（筛）：把相似的东西筛分开来，就是「辨别力」。

root: 拉丁语 discernere（分开、区分）：dis-（分开）+ cernere（筛）

sensesIntro.en: Discernment always separates something from something else; the senses differ in whether what is separated is fact, quality, right or sensation.
sensesIntro.cn: discernment 始终把某物与另一物分开；各义项的差别在于被分开的是事实、品质、是非还是感觉。

branches.en: Sound judgement in practical and legal matters.
branches.cn: 实务与法律事务中的可靠判断。

branches.en: Perception fine enough to catch small differences.
branches.cn: 细到能抓住微小差别的知觉。

branches.en: Taste that separates quality from expense.
branches.cn: 把品质与昂贵分开的品味。

branches.en: Moral and spiritual reading of complex cases.
branches.cn: 对复杂情形的道德与精神解读。

branches.en: Accurate reading of tone and implication.
branches.cn: 对语调与言外之意的准确解读。

intro.en: The word belongs to the cern family, where separation and sifting are the shared image.
intro.cn: 这个词属于 cern 词族，其中分离与筛选是共享的意象。

latinIntro.en: Latin cernere 'to sift' gives English words about certainty, secrecy and discrimination.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cernere「筛」给出了关于确定、隐秘与辨别的英语词。

items.example: She could discern a change in his voice.
items.exampleCN: 她能察觉他声音的变化。

items.example: A discerning reader notices the shift in tone.
items.exampleCN: 有辨别力的读者会注意到语调的转变。
这个职位需要政治判断力。

items.example: There was a discernible pause before she answered.
items.exampleCN: 她回答前有一处可察觉的停顿。

items.example: We are certain of the date.
The doctor certified the cause of death.

definition_zh: 谨慎；判断力；自行裁量的自由
definition_en: the quality of judging wisely, and the freedom to act on that judgement
core_image: 一位老管家站在宴会厅门口，把该说的话咽回去，把该放的人放进去，手一直按在门把上
scene: 宴会厅门口有人争执起来，管家没有立刻表态。The steward left the seating to her discretion.
sceneCN: 这里 discretion 指依自己的判断作决定的自由（第 2 个义项：自行裁量）；句意为管家让她自行安排座位。

senses.title: Ability to judge wisely
senses.definition: the quality of seeing what a situation calls for and acting accordingly
senses.definitionCN: 看清情势所需并据此行事的能力
senses.example: She handled the quarrel with great discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 她极为明智地处理了那场争吵。
senses.why: The word names a kind of judgement that shows itself in the timing of action and silence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的判断力，体现在行动与沉默的时机上。

senses.title: Freedom to decide
senses.definition: the power to choose how to act without being told by another
senses.definitionCN: 不受他人指派而自行选择行动方式的权力
senses.example: The steward left the seating to her discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 管家让她自行安排座位。
senses.why: Discretion here is a grant of space: someone hands you the decision instead of a rule.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 discretion 是一种空间授予：别人把决定交给你，而不是给你一条规则。

senses.title: Formal right to choose
senses.definition: a legal or official right to decide within set limits
senses.definitionCN: 在既定范围内作出决定的法律或官方权利
senses.example: The trustee may sell the land at his discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 受托人可自行决定出售这块土地。
senses.why: In law the word defines a bounded freedom: the holder chooses, but only inside the granted scope.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，这个词界定一种有边界的自由：持有者可以选，但只在被授予的范围内。

senses.title: Habit of keeping quiet
senses.definition: the practice of not revealing what one knows about others
senses.definitionCN: 不泄露自己所知的他人私事的习惯
senses.example: He told the secret to no one, and his discretion was admired.
senses.exampleCN: 他没把秘密告诉任何人，这份守口如瓶令人称道。
senses.why: Silence is often the clearest proof of discretion, because nothing said cannot be repeated.
senses.whyCN: 沉默常是谨慎最清楚的证明，因为没说出口的话无法被复述。

senses.title: Tact in choosing words
senses.definition: care in speech so that nothing needlessly wounds or exposes
senses.definitionCN: 说话时避免无谓伤人、揭短的分寸
senses.example: She described the failure with discretion, sparing the young man's name.
senses.exampleCN: 她得体地描述这次失败，没有点出那个年轻人的名字。
senses.why: Tact is discretion applied to language: the same fact, told in a way that protects.
senses.whyCN: 得体是用于语言的谨慎：同一件事，用保护人的方式说出来。

senses.title: The age of reason
senses.definition: the age at which a child is treated as able to judge right from wrong
senses.definitionCN: 孩子被视为能分辨是非的年龄
senses.example: The court found that he had reached the age of discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定他已到了懂事年龄。
senses.why: The phrase turns judgement into a threshold: past a certain age, one is held responsible for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法把判断力变成一道门槛：过了某个年龄，就要为自己的判断负责。

senses.title: Latitude within the law
senses.definition: the room a judge or official has to interpret rules case by case
senses.definitionCN: 法官或官员逐案解释规则时拥有的余地
senses.example: The sentence fell within the judge's discretion.
senses.exampleCN: 这一判决在法官的裁量范围内。
senses.why: Rules cannot cover every case, so the system deliberately leaves a pocket of choice.
senses.whyCN: 规则无法覆盖每个案子，于是制度故意留下一个可选择的口袋。

senses.title: Keeping something private
senses.definition: the state of being kept from public knowledge by choice
senses.definitionCN: 因选择而不让公众知晓的状态
senses.example: The details were handled with discretion and never reached the press.
senses.exampleCN: 细节被谨慎处理，从未传到媒体。
senses.why: Here discretion is not a person's skill but an outcome: information stays inside a closed circle.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 discretion 不是个人技能，而是一种结果：信息留在封闭的圈子里。

intro.en: Discretion comes from a Latin verb for sifting apart, and the image of separating good from bad still sits inside it.
intro.cn: discretion 来自一个表示「分开筛拣」的拉丁动词，把好坏分开的画面至今仍在词里。

items.en: English took the noun from Old French in the 14c., first as a word for discernment.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪从古法语借入这个名词，最初指辨别力。

items.en: Old French discrecion meant 'judgement, prudence', the practical side of discernment.
items.cn: 古法语 discrecion 意为「判断、审慎」，是辨别力中偏实践的一面。

items.en: Late Latin discretio meant 'a separating, a distinction', like sifting grain from chaff.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 discretio 意为「分开、区分」，像把谷粒从糠里筛出来。

items.en: Cernere 'to sift, to separate' is the root; the same root gives discern and discriminate.
items.cn: cernere「筛、分」是词根；同一词根还给出 discern 与 discriminate。

items.en: Modern usage adds a legal sense: the bounded freedom an official has to choose.
items.cn: 现代用法又添了法律义：官员拥有的一种有边界的自由。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on one letter that separates two very different words; the near-meaning group names neighbouring virtues.
note.cn: 形近组的关键只在一个字母，却分出两个差别很大的词；近义组列出相邻的美德。

entries.definition: careful not to reveal private matters.
separate and distinct, not continuous.
entries.definitionCN: 分开而独立的，不连续的。

entries.definition: left to one's own judgement.
in a careful, quiet manner.
good judgement about risks before acting.
entries.definitionCN: 行动前对风险的明智判断。

entries.definition: the ability to say difficult things without giving offence.
entries.definitionCN: 把难说的话说得不得罪人的能力。

entries.definition: the amount of freedom allowed in a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 决定时被允许的自由幅度。

entries.definition: care taken to avoid danger or error.
entries.definitionCN: 为避免危险或错误而采取的谨慎。

normalIntro.en: The hooks hold on to the picture of a hand resting on a door handle, deciding who may pass.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「一只手放在门把上、决定谁能通过」的画面留住。

normal.en: Discretion contains crest: a wise person keeps a cool crest above the crowd.
normal.cn: discretion 里有 crest（ crest 山脊）：明智的人能站在高处看清全局。

normal.en: Discreet and discrete differ by the t in the middle: keep the t for the careful one.
normal.cn: discreet 与 discrete 只差中间两个字母的位置：谨慎的那个保留 e 在末尾。

normal.en: Think of a doorman who lets the right people in and keeps the secret out.
normal.cn: 想象一个门房，放对的人进来，把秘密关在门外。

normal.en: Say dis-KRESH-un; the stressed syllable sounds like a hushed decision.
normal.cn: 读成 dis-KRESH-un，重读音节听起来像一次压低声音的决定。

normal.en: Pair it with judgement: discretion is judgement with a door in its hand.
normal.cn: 把它和 judgement 配对：discretion 是手里握着门的判断力。

abstract.en: Freedom and care live in the same word because a good decision needs both.
abstract.cn: 自由与谨慎住在同一个词里，因为好的决定两者都需要。

abstract.en: What is left unsaid is often the strongest exercise of discretion.
abstract.cn: 没有说出口的话，常常是谨慎最有力的行使。

abstract.en: Every rule leaves a small pocket of choice; that pocket is discretion.
abstract.cn: 每条规则都留下一个小小的选择口袋，那个口袋就是裁量。

examples.en: She handled the quarrel with great discretion.
examples.cn: 她极为明智地处理了那场争吵。

examples.en: The steward left the seating to her discretion.
examples.cn: 管家让她自行安排座位。

examples.en: The details were handled with discretion and never reached the press.
examples.cn: 细节被谨慎处理，从未传到媒体。

dict_mnemonic.text: dis（分开）+ cret（筛）+ ion（名词）：把该说的与该藏的筛开，就是「谨慎、裁量」。

root: 拉丁语 cernere（筛、分）→ discretio（区分），经古法语 discrecion 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses grow from one act: separating what fits from what does not, then choosing inside that cleared space.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一个动作长出来：把合宜的与不合宜的分开，然后在这块清出来的空间里作选择。

branches.en: The inner skill of judging and the tact that shows it in speech.
branches.cn: 内在的判断力，以及在言语中体现它的得体。

branches.en: Freedom granted by a person, a contract or a court.
branches.cn: 由人、契约或法院授予的自由。

branches.en: Silence that protects a secret from being repeated.
branches.cn: 保护秘密不被复述的沉默。

branches.en: The age at which judgement becomes a legal duty.
branches.cn: 判断力成为法律义务的那个年龄。

branches.en: The same word names the skill and the room to use it.
branches.cn: 同一个词既命名技能，也命名使用技能的空间。

intro.en: The family splits into two spellings: discreet for the careful person, discrete for the separate thing, and discretion holding both ideas.
intro.cn: 这个词族分成两种拼法：discreet 指谨慎的人，discrete 指分开的事物，而 discretion 同时握住这两个念头。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root cernere means to sift, and its past participle cretus gives the noun its shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 cernere 意为筛，其过去分词 cretus 给了名词现在的形状。

items.meaning: a sifting apart, then a judgement
items.meaningCN: 分开筛拣，而后作出判断

items.example: He was discreet about the visit.
items.exampleCN: 他对这次拜访守口如瓶。

items.meaningCN: 被分成各自独立的部分
items.example: The plot has three discrete stages.
items.exampleCN: 这个情节有三个独立阶段。

items.example: She could discern a change in his voice.
items.exampleCN: 她能辨出他声音里的变化。
他的辨别力救了这个项目。

items.meaning: to draw a line between things
items.example: The test discriminates between close answers.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试能区分接近的答案。

items.meaning: to set apart and hide away
items.example: The gland secretes a thin fluid.
items.exampleCN: 这个腺体分泌一种稀薄的液体。

items.example: One thing is certain: the door was locked.
items.exampleCN: 有一件事是确定的：门是锁着的。

definition_zh: 驱散；消除（疑虑、恐惧、误解）
definition_en: to drive something away and make it disappear, especially a feeling or a false idea
core_image: 清晨的雾压在湖面上，一阵风从岸边推过来，把整片白气撕开、赶走
scene: 会议开始前，走廊里的人越聚越多，他拿出一份数据。A single chart dispelled the rumour within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 dispel 指把谣言赶走（第 3 个义项：驳斥谣言）；句意为一张图表几分钟内就驱散了谣言。

senses.title: Drive away a fear
senses.definition: to make a fear lose its hold on a person
senses.definitionCN: 使恐惧失去对人的控制
senses.example: Her calm voice dispelled the child's fear of the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静的声音驱散了孩子对黑暗的恐惧。
senses.why: Fear behaves like mist: it blurs everything until something warm moves through it.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧像雾：它把一切弄模糊，直到有温暖的东西穿过去。

senses.title: Scatter a crowd
senses.definition: to make a gathered group break up and leave
senses.definitionCN: 使聚集的人群散开离去
senses.example: The guards dispelled the crowd before the gates opened.
senses.exampleCN: 大门开启前，守卫驱散了人群。
senses.why: A crowd is held together by a shared mood; once that mood breaks, the bodies follow.
senses.whyCN: 人群由共同的情绪聚在一起；情绪一散，身体也就跟着散了。

senses.title: Refute a rumour
senses.definition: to show that a story is false so that people stop believing it
senses.definitionCN: 证明传言不实，使人不再相信
senses.example: A single chart dispelled the rumour within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 一张图表几分钟内就驱散了谣言。
senses.why: A rumour lives on belief alone, so evidence is the wind that clears it.
senses.whyCN: 谣言只靠相信存活，因此证据就是吹散它的那阵风。

senses.title: Break an illusion
senses.definition: to destroy a false picture that someone has been holding
senses.definitionCN: 摧毁某人一直抱持的错误图景
senses.example: The first rehearsal dispelled any illusion of ease.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次排练就打碎了任何轻松的幻想。
senses.why: An illusion is a picture kept in place by hope; contact with the real thing removes it.
senses.whyCN: 幻想是被希望撑住的图景；与真实接触就会把它移走。

senses.title: Clear mist or fog
senses.definition: to make mist, fog or smoke thin out and vanish
senses.definitionCN: 使雾、烟变薄并消失
senses.example: A warm wind dispelled the fog over the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵暖风吹散了港口上的雾。
senses.why: This is the word's oldest picture: something visible but without substance is moved away.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的画面：可见却无实质的东西被移开。

senses.title: Remove a doubt
senses.definition: to settle a question in someone's mind so that doubt ends
senses.definitionCN: 在某人心中解决一个问题，使疑虑终止
senses.example: One sentence from the doctor dispelled her doubts.
senses.exampleCN: 医生的一句话消除了她的疑虑。
senses.why: Doubt is a fog in the mind, and a clear answer works like wind on it.
senses.whyCN: 疑虑是心里的雾，一个清楚的回答就像吹在雾上的风。

senses.title: Banish a mood
senses.definition: to make a heavy or gloomy mood lift from a place or group
senses.definitionCN: 使沉重或阴郁的气氛从某处或某群人中散开
senses.example: His joke dispelled the gloom of the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑话驱走了会议的阴郁。
senses.why: Moods hang in a room like smoke; a single bright act can clear the air.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像烟一样悬在房间里；一个明亮的举动就能让空气清朗。

senses.title: Dispel darkness
senses.definition: to drive back darkness with light, literally or as an image
senses.definitionCN: 用光逼退黑暗，无论实指或比喻
senses.example: The first lamp dispelled the darkness of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 第一盏灯驱散了门厅的黑暗。
senses.why: Darkness is the clearest case of something that retreats when something else arrives.
senses.whyCN: 黑暗是「别的东西一来就退走」最清楚的例子。

intro.en: Dispel is built from a prefix meaning apart and a verb meaning to drive, so it says exactly what it does: drive apart.
intro.cn: dispel 由一个意为「分开」的前缀和一个意为「驱赶」的动词构成，因此它说的就是它做的：赶开。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 17c. from Latin, first used of clouds and then of fears.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪从拉丁语借入这个动词，最初用于云，后来用于恐惧。

items.en: Dispellere meant 'to drive apart, to scatter', used of troops and of weather.
items.cn: dispellere 意为「赶开、驱散」，用于军队，也用于天气。

items.en: The prefix dis- means apart, in different directions, which gives the scattering motion.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 意为分开、朝不同方向，赋予它四散的动作。

items.en: Pellere 'to push, to drive' is also the root of compel and repel.
items.cn: pellere「推、驱」也是 compel 与 repel 的词根。

items.en: The verb moved from weather to the mind: rumours, doubts and fears are now what get dispelled.
items.cn: 这个动词从天气移到心智：如今被驱散的是谣言、疑虑与恐惧。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the pell drive; the near-meaning group names other ways of making something disappear.
note.cn: 形近组保留 pell「推、驱」；近义组列出其它让事物消失的方式。

entries.definition: able to be driven away.
in the act of driving something away.
to push something back from a surface.
to drive someone to act by force.
to throw or drive things in different directions.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西朝不同方向抛开。

entries.definition: to make fear or worry less intense.
to prove that a claim is wrong.
to send something away so that it does not return.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物赶走使其不再回来。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of wind tearing a sheet of mist into pieces that drift away.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「风把一片雾撕成碎块、吹向远处」的画面。

normal.en: Dispel shares pell with repel: one pushes back, the other pushes apart.
normal.cn: dispel 与 repel 共享 pell：一个往后推，一个往四周推。

normal.en: Think of a fan switched on in a foggy room: the fog leaves, the fan stays.
normal.cn: 想象雾屋里打开一台风扇：雾走了，风扇还在。

normal.en: Spell it dis + pel; the single l is doubled only in the past: dispelled.
normal.cn: 拼作 dis + pel；只有过去式才双写 l：dispelled。

normal.en: Say dis-PEL; the stress lands on the push, not on the apart.
normal.cn: 读成 dis-PEL，重音落在「推」上，而不在「分开」上。

normal.en: A rumour is fog with a voice; evidence is the wind.
normal.cn: 谣言是有声音的雾；证据就是风。

abstract.en: What has no substance is easiest to drive away, which is why doubt yields to clarity.
abstract.cn: 没有实质的东西最容易被赶走，所以疑虑会向清晰让步。

abstract.en: Dispelling is not arguing; it is changing the air until the thing cannot stay.
abstract.cn: 驱散不是争论；它是改变空气，直到那东西待不下去。

abstract.en: A light does not fight darkness; it simply arrives.
abstract.cn: 光不与黑暗搏斗；它只是到达。

examples.en: A single chart dispelled the rumour within minutes.
examples.cn: 一张图表几分钟内就驱散了谣言。

examples.en: Her calm voice dispelled the child's fear of the dark.
examples.cn: 她平静的声音驱散了孩子对黑暗的恐惧。

examples.en: A warm wind dispelled the fog over the harbour.
examples.cn: 一阵暖风吹散了港口上的雾。

dict_mnemonic.text: dis（分开）+ pel（推）：把东西往四周推开，就是「驱散」。

root: 拉丁语 pellere（推、驱），加前缀 dis-（分开）→ dispellere

sensesIntro.en: Dispel always needs two things: something without solidity and a force that moves through it; the senses differ only in what the mist stands for.
sensesIntro.cn: dispel 总需要两样东西：一样没有实质的东西，以及一股穿过它的力量；各义项的差别只在雾代表什么。

branches.en: Literal mist and darkness moved away by wind or light.
branches.cn: 被风或光移走的真实的雾与黑暗。

branches.en: Inner weather: fear, doubt and gloom.
branches.cn: 内心的天气：恐惧、疑虑与阴郁。

branches.en: False stories and false pictures destroyed by evidence.
branches.cn: 被证据摧毁的假故事与假图景。

branches.en: A crowd losing the mood that held it together.
branches.cn: 人群失去维系它的那种情绪。

branches.en: The word moves easily from weather to the mind.
branches.cn: 这个词从天气轻松移到心智。

intro.en: The pell family is all about driving: repel pushes back, compel drives forward, expel drives out, dispel drives apart.
intro.cn: pell 词族全与「驱」有关：repel 往后推，compel 往前驱，expel 往外赶，dispel 往四周赶。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere gives the push; the prefix dis- decides the direction, and direction is the whole difference in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 提供推力，前缀 dis- 决定方向，而方向正是这个词族全部的区别。

items.meaning: to drive apart in all directions
to drive back toward its source
to drive out of a place

items.example: The spray is a mosquito repellent.

definition_zh: 持不同政见者；异见分子；持异见的
definition_en: a person who publicly disagrees with an established authority, especially a government
core_image: 一间小公寓的灯亮到深夜，桌上摊着被划满红线的报纸，主人把文稿塞进信封
scene: 墙上的广播一遍遍重复同一条消息，他关掉了开关。The dissident kept writing anyway.
sceneCN: 这里 dissident 指持不同政见者（第 1 个义项：与当权者公开意见相左的人）；句意为这位异见者仍继续写作。

senses.title: One who disagrees publicly
senses.definition: a person who states disagreement with an authority in public
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达与权威意见相左的人
senses.example: The dissident kept writing anyway.
senses.exampleCN: 这位异见者仍继续写作。
senses.why: The word names a person, not a mood: disagreement made visible and repeated.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是人，不是情绪：被看见、被重复的分歧。

senses.title: A voice inside a group
senses.definition: someone whose objection arises within an institution rather than outside it
senses.definitionCN: 在机构内部而非外部产生异议的人
senses.example: The party expelled its own dissident members.
senses.exampleCN: 该党开除了自己的异见成员。
senses.why: A dissident is most dangerous to a group when the disagreement comes from inside the house.
senses.whyCN: 当分歧来自屋里时，异见者对团体最危险。

senses.title: A political opponent
senses.definition: a citizen who opposes the policies or claims of a ruling power
senses.definitionCN: 反对执政者政策或主张的公民
senses.example: The regime jailed the leading dissident for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 该政权把主要异见者判了十年监禁。
senses.why: Here the word becomes political shorthand: the disagreement is with the state itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词变成政治简称：分歧的对象是国家本身。

senses.title: A religious nonconformist
senses.definition: a believer who refuses an official doctrine or church order
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝官方教义或教会命令的信徒
senses.example: The dissident priest was removed from his parish.
senses.exampleCN: 这位持异见的牧师被免去了教区职务。
senses.why: Long before politics, the word described those who would not sign a creed.
senses.whyCN: 远在政治之前，这个词描述的是拒绝签署信条的人。

senses.title: A writer in exile
senses.definition: an author whose work is banned at home and continues abroad
senses.definitionCN: 作品在本国被禁、在国外继续写作的作者
senses.example: The dissident published her memoir in another country.
senses.exampleCN: 这位异见作家在另一个国家出版了回忆录。
senses.why: Exile turns disagreement into a place: the writing continues, the audience changes.
senses.whyCN: 流亡把分歧变成一个地点：写作继续，读者换了。

senses.title: Adjective: holding dissent
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean that the person or group dissents
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前，表示该人或团体持异议
senses.example: A dissident faction split from the ruling party.
senses.exampleCN: 一个异见派系从执政党中分裂出去。
senses.why: Here the word stops naming a person and starts labelling a whole group by its disagreement.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词不再指一个人，而是用「有异议」给整个团体贴标签。

senses.title: An internal critic
senses.definition: a member who criticises the group in order to improve or change it
senses.definitionCN: 为改进或改变团体而批评它的成员
senses.example: She played the dissident at every board meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在每次董事会上都扮演内部批评者的角色。
senses.why: This sense carries loyalty inside the objection: the critic wants the group to survive.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项在异议里带着忠诚：批评者希望团体活下去。

senses.title: A movement of dissent
senses.definition: a loose network of people whose shared objection becomes organised
senses.definitionCN: 共同异议组织化后形成的松散网络
senses.example: The dissident movement grew quietly in the universities.
senses.exampleCN: 异见运动在大学里悄然壮大。
senses.why: Once individual voices find each other, the word shifts from person to current.
senses.whyCN: 当个体的声音彼此找到，这个词就从人转向潮流。

intro.en: Dissident is built from a prefix meaning apart and a verb meaning to sit, so it literally means sitting apart.
intro.cn: dissident 由一个意为「分开」的前缀和一个意为「坐」的动词构成，字面就是「分开坐」。

items.en: English took the adjective from Latin in the 16c., first for religious disagreement.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁语借入这个形容词，最初用于宗教分歧。

items.en: Dissidere meant 'to sit apart, to disagree', as two people who will not share a bench.
items.cn: dissidere 意为「分开坐、意见不合」，像两个人不愿共用一条长凳。

items.en: Sedere 'to sit' also gives sediment and session, all about settling into place.
items.cn: sedere「坐」也给出 sediment 与 session，都与落到某处有关。

items.en: Dis- means apart; the sitting apart is the whole image of disagreement.
items.cn: dis- 意为分开；「分开坐」正是意见不合的整个画面。

items.en: In the 20c. the noun narrowed toward political opposition, especially under authoritarian rule.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个名词收窄为政治反对，尤其在威权统治之下。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sitting root; the near-meaning group lays out degrees of disagreement.
note.cn: 形近组共享「坐」的词根；近义组排列出分歧的各个程度。

entries.definition: the state or act of disagreeing with authority.
entries.definitionCN: 与权威意见相左的状态或行为。

entries.definition: in a manner that shows disagreement.
one who disagrees, especially with an official church.
entries.definitionCN: 持异议者，尤指不服从官方教会者。

entries.definition: an action that harms instead of helping.
the expression of disagreement with a majority or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 对多数或权威表达不同意。

entries.definition: a person who publicly demonstrates against a policy.
entries.definitionCN: 公开针对某项政策示威的人。

entries.definition: a person who fights against an established power.
a person who will not follow established customs or doctrines.
entries.definitionCN: 不遵循既定习俗或教义的人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks hold on to the picture of a person deliberately sitting on a separate bench.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一个人故意坐到另一条长凳上」的画面。

normal.en: Dissident contains sed, to sit: the dissident sits apart.
normal.cn: dissident 含 sed（坐）：异见者坐到别处。

normal.en: Two s sounds at the start: dis-si-dent, like a hiss of refusal.
normal.cn: 开头连着两个 s 音：dis-si-dent，像一声拒绝的嘶气。

normal.en: Think of a lone chair moved to the back of the hall.
normal.cn: 想象一把孤零零的椅子被搬到会场最后面。

normal.en: Link with sediment: both settle, one to the bottom, one to the edge.
normal.cn: 和 sediment 联系：两者都落定，一个沉底，一个落到边缘。

normal.en: The adjective and noun look the same; only the article tells you which is which.
normal.cn: 形容词和名词长得一样；只有冠词告诉你哪个是哪个。

abstract.en: Disagreement becomes identity when it is spoken often enough in public.
abstract.cn: 当分歧在公众面前被说得足够多，它就变成身份。

abstract.en: A dissident keeps the group honest, which is why groups rarely thank them.
abstract.cn: 异见者让团体保持诚实，因此团体很少感谢他们。

abstract.en: Sitting apart is not leaving; the dissident is still in the room.
abstract.cn: 分开坐不等于离开；异见者仍在这间屋里。

examples.en: The dissident kept writing anyway.
examples.cn: 这位异见者仍继续写作。

examples.en: The party expelled its own dissident members.
examples.cn: 该党开除了自己的异见成员。

examples.en: The dissident movement grew quietly in the universities.
examples.cn: 异见运动在大学里悄然壮大。

dict_mnemonic.text: dis（分开）+ sid（坐）+ ent（人）：分开坐的人，就是「持不同政见者」。

root: 拉丁语 dissidere（分开坐、不同意），由 dis- 与 sedere（坐）构成

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a single act of sitting apart to a whole movement, first religious, then political, then organised.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项从「分开坐」这一个动作，扩展到一个完整的运动，先宗教，再政治，最后组织化。

core.en: SITTING APART IN THE SAME ROOM

branches.en: The single person who objects, inside or outside the group.
branches.cn: 提出异议的那一个人，无论团体内外。

branches.en: Opposition organised against a state, including exile.
branches.cn: 针对国家组织起来的反对，包括流亡。

branches.en: The older religious sense of refusing a creed.
branches.cn: 较古老的宗教意义：拒绝信条。

branches.en: The same word used as an adjective before a noun.
branches.cn: 同一个词用作名词前的形容词。

branches.en: Individual voices joining into a visible movement.
branches.cn: 个体声音汇成可见的运动。

intro.en: The sed family is about sitting and settling: dissident sits apart, resident sits back, president sits before.
intro.cn: sed 词族与坐和落定有关：dissident 分开坐，resident 坐回去，president 坐在前面。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere gives every member its seat; the prefixes say where the sitting happens.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 给每个成员一个座位；前缀说明这个「坐」发生在哪里。

items.example: A dissident spoke from the back.
items.exampleCN: 一位异见者从后排发言。

items.meaning: one who sits back in a place
one who sits before the others

items.example: A layer of sediment covered the floor.
items.exampleCN: 一层沉积物覆盖了底面。
这场会议持续了两小时。

items.example: His sedentary life hurt his back.
items.exampleCN: 久坐的生活伤了他的背。

items.example: The new rule supersedes the old one.

definition_zh: 教条；教义；不容置疑的信条
definition_en: a belief or set of beliefs accepted as certainly true, often without evidence or question
core_image: 教堂里一块刻满字的大石板，人人从它前面走过，没有人停下来读第二遍
scene: 教室里老师说这条规则不可讨论，全班安静下来。Nobody dared to question the dogma of the department.
sceneCN: 这里 dogma 指不容置疑的信条（第 1 个义项：被当作确定真理的信念）；句意为没人敢质疑系里那条铁律。

senses.title: Fixed doctrine
senses.definition: a principle held as certainly true and placed beyond discussion
senses.definitionCN: 被当作确定真理、置于讨论之外的原则
senses.example: Nobody dared to question the dogma of the department.
senses.exampleCN: 没人敢质疑系里那条铁律。
senses.why: The word marks not the content of a belief but its status: closed to argument.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记的不是信念的内容，而是它的地位：对论证关闭。

senses.title: Church teaching
senses.definition: an official teaching of a church that members must accept
senses.definitionCN: 教会官方教导、成员必须接受的教义
senses.example: The council restated the dogma on the Trinity.
senses.exampleCN: 会议重申了关于三位一体的教义。
senses.why: In religious use the word is neutral: a teaching received, not an insult.
senses.whyCN: 在宗教用法中，这个词是中性的：被领受的教导，而非贬语。

senses.title: Unquestioned belief
senses.definition: an idea accepted by a group without ever being tested
senses.definitionCN: 被一群人不加检验就接受的观念
senses.example: It was dogma that a good degree guaranteed a good job.
senses.exampleCN: 当时有一种信条：好学位必然带来好工作。
senses.why: An untested idea repeated by enough people stops looking like an idea at all.
senses.whyCN: 一个未经检验的观念被足够多的人重复后，就不再像观念了。

senses.title: The party line
senses.definition: the official position that members of a political group must repeat
senses.definitionCN: 政治团体成员必须复述的官方立场
senses.example: He repeated the party dogma word for word.
senses.exampleCN: 他把党的教条一字不差地重复了一遍。
senses.why: Politics shows how a belief becomes a test of loyalty rather than a claim about the world.
senses.whyCN: 政治展示了信念如何变成忠诚的考验，而不是关于世界的断言。

senses.title: Rigid principle
senses.definition: a rule applied mechanically, without regard to the case in front of it
senses.definitionCN: 机械套用、不顾眼前个案的规则
senses.example: The committee applied the dogma and ignored the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会套用了那条僵化原则，无视证据。
senses.why: When a principle stops listening, it hardens into dogma.
senses.whyCN: 当原则不再倾听，它就硬化为教条。

senses.title: Dogma as comfort
senses.definition: a belief kept because it makes an uncertain world easier to bear
senses.definitionCN: 因能让不确定的世界更易承受而被保留的信念
senses.example: For many, the old dogma was a kind of shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多人来说，旧教条是一种庇护。
senses.why: A settled answer soothes more than an open question, even when the answer is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 一个已定的答案比一个开放的问题更让人安心，即使答案是错的。

senses.title: Rejection of dogma
senses.definition: the stance of refusing beliefs that demand acceptance without reason
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝接受那些要求无条件相信的信念的立场
senses.example: The young scholars were united only in their rejection of dogma.
senses.exampleCN: 这些年轻学者唯一一致的地方就是拒斥教条。
senses.why: Refusing closed beliefs can itself become a shared position, and a shared position can harden.
senses.whyCN: 拒斥封闭的信念本身也可能成为共同立场，而共同立场也会硬化。

senses.title: Dogmatic assertion
senses.definition: a statement delivered as certain in a tone that forbids reply
senses.definitionCN: 以确定无疑、禁止回应的口吻作出的陈述
senses.example: His essay opened with a dogma rather than a question.
senses.exampleCN: 他的文章以一个独断的断言开头，而不是一个问题。
senses.why: Here the word has moved from the belief to the way it is spoken.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词已从信念移到了说出它的方式。

intro.en: Dogma is a Greek word for opinion, and its journey from 'what seems right' to 'what may not be questioned' is the whole story.
intro.cn: dogma 是希腊语中表示「意见」的词，它从「看起来对的」走到「不许质疑的」，整个过程就是这个词的故事。

items.en: Greek dogma meant 'an opinion, a decree', something a person or a city decided to hold.
items.cn: 希腊语 dogma 意为「意见、法令」，是某人或城邦决定持守的东西。

items.en: Dokein 'to seem' is the root: a dogma is what seems true to someone.
items.cn: dokein「显得、看来」是词根：dogma 就是某人觉得为真的东西。

items.en: The early church used it for official teachings, giving the word its neutral religious sense.
items.cn: 早期教会用它指官方教导，赋予这个词中性的宗教含义。

items.en: English took the word in the 16c., and by the 17c. it could already carry a sneer.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个词，到十七世纪它已能带讥讽。

items.en: Today the word usually criticises: a belief held as beyond question is rarely thought healthy.
items.cn: 今天这个词通常带批评：被视为不容置疑的信念很少被认为是健康的。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dogm stem; the near-meaning group moves from neutral teaching to closed conviction.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dogm 词干；近义组从中文性的教导移向封闭的确信。

entries.definition: asserting beliefs as certainly true.
entries.definitionCN: 把信念断言为确定真理的。

entries.definition: the habit of asserting beliefs without evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 无证据断言信念的习惯。

entries.definition: a person who holds beliefs beyond question.
the Greek plural of dogma.
a set of beliefs taught by a church or party.
entries.definitionCN: 教会或党派所教导的一套信念。

entries.definition: a formal summary of what a group believes.
entries.definitionCN: 一个团体信念的正式摘要。

entries.definition: the belief officially accepted as correct.
entries.definitionCN: 被官方认定正确的信念。

entries.definition: a principle held as true by a group.
entries.definitionCN: 团体认为为真的一条原则。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a stone slab that people pass without ever stopping to read.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「人们走过一块石板、却从不停下细读」的画面。

normal.en: Dogma and doctor share a d-o-g start but nothing else: a doctor questions, dogma does not.
normal.cn: dogma 与 doctor 都以 d-o 开头，但别无关系：医生会质疑，教条不会。

normal.en: Think of a museum guard who forbids anyone to touch the display.
normal.cn: 想象一位博物馆守卫，禁止任何人触碰展品。

normal.en: Dogma ends in a: a is the first letter, and dogma claims to be the first word.
normal.cn: dogma 以 a 结尾：a 是第一个字母，而教条自称是第一句话。

normal.en: Say DOG-muh; the flat first syllable sounds like a rule read aloud.
normal.cn: 读成 DOG-muh，平直的第一个音节像在朗读一条规则。

normal.en: Link it with doctrine: doctrine is what is taught, dogma is what may not be asked.
normal.cn: 和 doctrine 联系：doctrine 是被教导的，dogma 是不许被追问的。

abstract.en: A belief becomes dogma at the moment questioning it becomes rude.
abstract.cn: 当质疑它变得失礼时，信念就变成了教条。

abstract.en: Dogma saves thought in the short run and costs it in the long run.
abstract.cn: 教条短期省下思考，长期却要付出思考的代价。

abstract.en: Every age has a dogma it cannot see, which is why history is useful.
abstract.cn: 每个时代都有自己看不见的教条，这正是历史有用的原因。

examples.en: Nobody dared to question the dogma of the department.
examples.cn: 没人敢质疑系里那条铁律。

examples.en: The council restated the dogma on the Trinity.
examples.cn: 会议重申了关于三位一体的教义。

examples.en: He repeated the party dogma word for word.
examples.cn: 他把党的教条一字不差地重复了一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: dog（doc，教导）+ ma（名词）：被教导到不许再问的东西，就是「教条」。

root: 希腊语 dogma（意见、法令），源自 dokein（显得、看来）

sensesIntro.en: Dogma always names a belief plus a rule about that belief: it may not be questioned; the senses differ in who enforces the rule.
sensesIntro.cn: dogma 总是命名一个信念，再加上关于这个信念的一条规则：不许质疑；各义项的差别在于是谁在执行这条规则。

core.cn: 被放到质疑之外的信念

branches.en: The belief and its official religious form.
branches.cn: 信念本身及其正式的宗教形式。

branches.en: Why people keep it: it feels settled and it comforts.
branches.cn: 人们保留它的原因：它显得已定，而且令人安心。

branches.en: How institutions enforce it, in politics and in procedure.
branches.cn: 机构如何执行它，无论在政治还是程序上。

branches.en: The reaction against it, and the tone that gives it away.
branches.cn: 对它的反弹，以及暴露它的那种语气。

branches.en: A principle hardens into dogma when it stops listening.
branches.cn: 原则在不再倾听时硬化为教条。

intro.en: The dogm family describes the closed mind: a belief, the habit of asserting it, and the person who never asks.
intro.cn: dogm 词族描述封闭的心：一个信念，断言它的习惯，以及从不发问的人。

latinIntro.en: Greek dokein, to seem, gives dogma and also docent and document, all tied to what is shown or taught.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 dokein（显得）给出 dogma，也给出 docent 与 document，都与被显示或被教导的东西有关。

items.meaning: a thing held as settled opinion
items.meaningCN: 被当作既定意见持守的东西
items.exampleCN: 这条教条经历三次改革仍存。

items.example: His dogmatic tone ended the debate.
items.exampleCN: 他独断的语气终结了讨论。
教条主义挡住了每一个问题。

items.example: A dogmatist fears the second question.
items.exampleCN: 教条主义者害怕第二个问题。

items.meaning: what is taught as a body
items.meaningCN: 作为整体被教导的内容
items.exampleCN: 这套学说塑造了这所学校。

items.meaning: a thing that shows or teaches
items.meaningCN: 用来显示或教导的东西

items.example: He was raised in an orthodox home.
items.exampleCN: 他在一个正统的家庭长大。

definition_zh: 兴高采烈；热情洋溢；沸腾
definition_en: a bubbling overflow of high spirits and energy
core_image: 锅里滚开的水顶起一串串气泡，汽笛一样往上冲，盖子被推得咔咔响
scene: 她一站上台，声音就把整个礼堂填满。Her ebullience carried the tired audience through the last hour.
sceneCN: 这里 ebullience 指热情洋溢的劲头（第 1 个义项：兴高采烈）；句意为她的热情撑住了疲惫的听众。

pos.zh: 兴高采烈；热情洋溢；沸腾

senses.title: A bubble of high spirits
senses.definition: an overflow of cheerful energy that others can feel
senses.definitionCN: 能被他人感受到的欢快能量的外溢
senses.example: Her ebullience carried the tired audience through the last hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她的热情撑住了疲惫的听众，直到最后一小时。
senses.why: The word began at the boiling pot, and joy here behaves the same way: it rises and spills over.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起于滚沸的锅，而这里的喜悦也一样：它向上升，然后溢出。

senses.title: Liveliness of a crowd
senses.definition: the excited, noisy energy of many people together
senses.definitionCN: 许多人聚在一起时兴奋喧闹的能量
senses.example: The ebullience of the crowd spilled into the street.
senses.exampleCN: 人群的热烈漫溢到街上。
senses.why: A crowd can boil too; the same word covers heat that belongs to no single person.
senses.whyCN: 人群也会沸腾；同一个词覆盖了不属于任何个人的热度。

senses.title: Boiling motion
senses.definition: the literal bubbling of a liquid as it turns to vapour
senses.definitionCN: 液体化为蒸汽时真实的冒泡运动
senses.example: The pot's ebullience stopped as soon as the flame was cut.
senses.exampleCN: 火一关，锅里的沸腾就停了。
senses.why: This is the physical base of the word, still used in chemistry and old prose.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的物理底层，至今仍用于化学与旧式散文。

senses.title: Exuberant talk
senses.definition: speech that pours out fast and warm, with little pause
senses.definitionCN: 快速、热烈、很少停顿地涌出的言谈
senses.example: His ebullience on the phone made the call twice as long.
senses.exampleCN: 他在电话里的滔滔不绝让通话长了一倍。
senses.why: Talk can bubble as well; the metaphor moves from liquid to voice without losing its motion.
senses.whyCN: 言谈也会冒泡；这个比喻从液体移到声音，却不丢掉它的运动。

senses.title: Youthful energy
senses.definition: the unguarded enthusiasm often associated with being young
senses.definitionCN: 常与年轻联系在一起、不加防备的热忱
senses.example: At seventy he still had the ebullience of a first-year student.
senses.exampleCN: 七十岁时他仍有大一学生的劲头。
senses.why: Age is not the point; what the word notes is energy that has not yet learned to hold back.
senses.whyCN: 重点不在年龄；这个词注意到的是还没学会收敛的能量。

senses.title: Overflowing optimism
senses.definition: confidence so high that it spills past what the facts allow
senses.definitionCN: 高到超出事实许可范围的信心
senses.example: The ebullience before the launch looked naive in hindsight.
senses.exampleCN: 回看之下，发布前的乐观显得天真。
senses.why: The same bubbling can be a virtue or a blind spot; the word itself does not judge.
senses.whyCN: 同样的沸腾可以是美德，也可以是盲点；这个词本身不作判断。

senses.title: Effervescence of style
senses.definition: a lively, sparkling quality in writing or performance
senses.definitionCN: 写作或表演中活泼、闪亮的气质
senses.example: The essay has an ebullience that survives even its grim subject.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章有一种奔涌的劲头，连阴郁的主题也压不住。
senses.why: Style can fizz; a text that bubbles keeps the reader moving even through hard material.
senses.whyCN: 风格会起泡；冒泡的文字能让读者在艰难材料中继续前行。

senses.title: Emotional overflow
senses.definition: a feeling that cannot stay inside and shows in voice or face
senses.definitionCN: 无法留在内部、从声音或脸上露出来的情感
senses.example: Tears and laughter came with the same ebullience.
senses.exampleCN: 眼泪和笑声以同样外溢的方式一起出来。
senses.why: When feeling exceeds containment, English reaches for the boiling pot.
senses.whyCN: 当情感超出容器，英语就伸手去拿那口滚锅。

intro.en: Ebullience comes from a Latin verb meaning to boil up, and the image of bubbles rising has never left the word.
intro.cn: ebullience 来自一个意为「煮到沸起」的拉丁动词，气泡上升的画面从未离开这个词。

items.en: English took the noun in the 17c., first for literal boiling and then for temperament.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，先指真实的沸腾，后指性情。

items.en: Ebullire meant 'to boil over, to bubble up', built from ex- and bullire.
items.cn: ebullire 意为「煮溢、冒泡上涌」，由 ex- 与 bullire 构成。

items.en: Bullire 'to boil' is also behind the English word boil itself.
items.cn: bullire「煮沸」也是英语 boil 本身的来源。

items.en: Bulla meant a bubble or a round boss, the shape of something swelling upward.
items.cn: bulla 意为气泡或圆形凸起，正是向上鼓起的形状。

items.en: By the 19c. the word settled on high spirits, keeping the fizz but losing the fire.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个词落在高涨的情绪上，保留气泡，去掉火。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the boiling root; the near-meaning group names other forms of overflowing energy.
note.cn: 形近组保留「沸腾」词根；近义组列出其它外溢能量的形态。

entries.definition: bubbling with cheerful energy.
a boiling up or a sudden outburst.
fizzing, lively in manner.
overflowing with vigour and joy.
a rush of gladness that lifts the body.
entries.definitionCN: 把身体托起的欢快冲击。

entries.definition: keen enjoyment shown in doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 做事时显露的强烈享受。

entries.definition: quick, bright energy in manner or speech.
entries.definitionCN: 举止言谈中轻快明亮的精神。

entries.definition: intense, almost burning feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈到近乎灼热的情感。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a pot boiling over, bubbles pushing at the lid.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「锅沸腾溢出、气泡顶着盖子」的画面。

normal.en: Ebullience contains bull: a boiling pot throws up bubbles like a bull snorting.
normal.cn: ebullience 里有 bull（公牛）：沸腾的锅冒起泡，像公牛打响鼻。

normal.en: The double l keeps the bubbles double: e-bull-ience.
normal.cn: 双写的 l 让气泡也成双：e-bull-ience。

normal.en: Link with boil: both come from Latin bullire, and both rise.
normal.cn: 和 boil 联系：两者都出自拉丁语 bullire，都在往上冒。

normal.en: Think of a shaken soda bottle opened at a party.
normal.cn: 想象聚会上被摇过再打开的一瓶汽水。

normal.en: Say ih-BUL-yuns; the stress is where the bubbles push hardest.
normal.cn: 读成 ih-BUL-yuns，重音正落在气泡推得最猛的地方。

abstract.en: Energy that cannot be contained shows up as overflow, not as force.
abstract.cn: 无法被容纳的能量表现为溢出，而不是力量。

abstract.en: The same bubbling that warms a room can also flood it.
abstract.cn: 温暖房间的那股沸腾，也可能淹了房间。

abstract.en: Joy, like heat, is measured by what it moves, not by what it says.
abstract.cn: 喜悦像热一样，看它推动了什么，而不是看它说了什么。

examples.en: Her ebullience carried the tired audience through the last hour.
examples.cn: 她的热情撑住了疲惫的听众，直到最后一小时。

examples.en: The ebullience of the crowd spilled into the street.
examples.cn: 人群的热烈漫溢到街上。

examples.en: At seventy he still had the ebullience of a first-year student.
examples.cn: 七十岁时他仍有大一学生的劲头。

dict_mnemonic.text: e（外）+ bull（气泡）+ ience（名词）：气泡往外涌，就是「热情洋溢」。

root: 拉丁语 bullire（煮沸），加前缀 ex-（向外）→ ebullire（沸腾溢出）

sensesIntro.en: Every sense keeps the same motion, something rising and spilling over; only the container changes, pot, crowd, voice or face.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都保留同一个动作：某物向上升并溢出；变的只是容器，锅、人群、声音或脸。

branches.en: The physical base: a liquid boiling in a pot.
branches.cn: 物理底层：锅里沸腾的液体。

branches.en: Joy and crowd energy that fill a space.
branches.cn: 填满空间的喜悦与人群能量。

branches.en: Talk and style that bubble as they move.
branches.cn: 流动时冒泡的言谈与文风。

branches.en: Young energy and feeling too large to hold.
branches.cn: 年轻的能量与大到装不下的情感。

branches.en: The risk inside the overflow: optimism past the facts.
branches.cn: 溢出里的风险：超出事实的乐观。

intro.en: The bull family is about boiling and bubbling: ebullience bubbles up, ebullition bursts out, and boil itself is the plain form.
intro.cn: bull 词族与煮沸、冒泡有关：ebullience 向上冒，ebullition 向外爆，而 boil 本身就是最朴素的形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin bullire supplies the heat; the prefix ex- says the motion is outward, and that outwardness is the point.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bullire 提供热量，前缀 ex- 说明动作向外，而「向外」正是要点。

items.example: An ebullition of anger ended the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 一阵怒火爆发结束了会议。

items.meaning: to heat a liquid to bubbling
items.example: The water boiled in a minute.

items.exampleCN: 沸点测定法可求分子量。

items.example: The kettle answered with a rebullition.

definition_zh: 引出；诱出；引起（反应）
definition_en: to draw out a response, fact or feeling that was not offered freely
core_image: 一根细线从水面下慢慢提起，把藏在深处的东西一点点带出水面
scene: 记者把录音笔推到桌子中间，只问了一个很轻的问题。The question elicited a long silence, then a name.
sceneCN: 这里 elicit 指引出回答或信息（第 1 个义项：把未主动说出的东西带出来）；句意为这个问题先引出沉默，然后引出一个名字。

senses.title: Draw out an answer
senses.definition: to get someone to say something they had not planned to say
senses.definitionCN: 使某人说出原本没打算说的话
senses.example: The question elicited a long silence, then a name.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题先引出沉默，然后引出一个名字。
senses.why: The word assumes resistance: the answer exists but is not on the surface, so it must be drawn.
senses.whyCN: 这个词预设了阻力：答案存在，却不在表面，因此必须被拉出来。

senses.title: Obtain a reaction
senses.definition: to produce a response from a body, a market or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 使身体、市场或人群产生反应
senses.example: The new rule elicited protests from every department.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定引起每个部门的抗议。
senses.why: Reactions are also hidden until something touches them, and the touch is what elicits.
senses.whyCN: 反应也一直藏着，直到有东西触碰；而触碰就是 elicit。

senses.title: Extract a confession
senses.definition: to draw out an admission through questioning rather than force
senses.definitionCN: 通过提问而非强力取得承认
senses.example: The lawyer elicited a detail the witness had forgotten.
senses.exampleCN: 律师引出了证人已经忘记的一个细节。
senses.why: Careful questioning works like fishing: it does not push, it waits and lifts.
senses.whyCN: 细致的问话像钓鱼：不推，只等，然后提起来。

senses.title: Evoke a memory
senses.definition: to bring a half-lost memory back into speech or mind
senses.definitionCN: 把半失的记忆带回言语或意识中
senses.example: The old song elicited a story about his first job.
senses.exampleCN: 那首老歌唤起了一个关于他第一份工作的故事。
senses.why: Memory is stored below speech; a small cue can pull it up whole.
senses.whyCN: 记忆储存在言语之下；一个小小的线索就能把整块提上来。

senses.title: Win applause
senses.definition: to cause an audience to give a visible sign of approval
senses.definitionCN: 使观众给出可见的赞许表示
senses.example: Her final line elicited applause that lasted a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她最后一句赢得了持续一分钟的掌声。
senses.why: Applause is offered, not commanded, so when it is elicited the performance has done the pulling.
senses.whyCN: 掌声是自愿给出的，不是被命令的，因此被引出时，是表演做了拉动。

senses.title: Gather information
senses.definition: to obtain facts from people or systems by skilled asking
senses.definitionCN: 通过有技巧的询问从人或系统中取得事实
senses.example: The survey elicited useful answers about commuting.
senses.exampleCN: 这份调查获取了关于通勤的有用回答。
senses.why: In research the word is neutral: information is collected by design, not by luck.
senses.whyCN: 在研究语境中这个词是中性的：信息按设计收集，而非靠运气。

senses.title: Draw out a smile
senses.definition: to cause a small, often involuntary expression of pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 使一个细小、常常不由自主的愉快表情出现
senses.example: A single silly drawing elicited a smile from the child.
senses.exampleCN: 一幅傻气的简笔画逗出了孩子的微笑。
senses.why: A smile is the least guarded reaction, which makes it the clearest proof of eliciting.
senses.whyCN: 微笑是最不设防的反应，因此是「引出」最清楚的证据。

senses.title: Provoke a response
senses.definition: to stir a strong response, sometimes against the responder's will
senses.definitionCN: 激起强烈回应，有时违背回应者的意愿
senses.example: The speech elicited anger he had not expected.
senses.exampleCN: 这场演讲激起了他未曾预料的愤怒。
senses.why: Here eliciting shades toward provoking: the response comes out before it can be filtered.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 elicit 已偏向 provoke：回应还没来得及过滤就出来了。

intro.en: Elicit comes from a Latin verb meaning to lure out, and its old cousins include lace and delicacy.
intro.cn: elicit 来自一个意为「诱出」的拉丁动词，它的古老亲属包括 lace 与 delicacy。

items.en: English took the verb in the 17c. from Latin, mostly in scholarly prose.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪从拉丁语借入这个动词，多见于学术文字。

items.en: Elicere meant 'to draw out, to entice forth', as bait draws a fish.
items.cn: elicere 意为「引出、诱出」，像饵把鱼引出来。

items.en: The prefix ex- means out; the motion is always from inside to surface.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 意为向外；动作总是从内部到表面。

items.en: Lacere 'to entice' is the base, related to the idea of a lure.
items.cn: lacere「引诱」是词基，与「饵」的观念相关。

items.en: Modern English uses it for answers, data and reactions, all drawn out by method.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指回答、数据与反应，都是被方法引出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group sounds nearly identical and is often confused; the near-meaning group names other ways of bringing something forth.
note.cn: 形近组读音几乎相同，常被混淆；近义组列出其它把事物带出来的方式。

entries.definition: forbidden by law or rule.
the act of drawing something out.
well chosen and apt in speech.
omitted or merged in sound.
to bring a memory or feeling into the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 把记忆或情感唤入心中。

entries.definition: to remove something by force or process.
entries.definitionCN: 用力量或工序取出某物。

entries.definition: to stir a strong response, often deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 激起强烈回应，常为有意。

entries.definition: to bring out something that exists in hidden form.
entries.definitionCN: 把以隐藏形式存在的东西带出来。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a line lifting something slowly from under the water.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一根线把水下的东西慢慢提上来」的画面。

normal.en: Elicit begins like e-lect: a question elects one answer out of many.
normal.cn: elicit 开头像 e-lect：一个问题从许多答案中选出一个。

normal.en: Elicit and illicit differ by one letter and a whole moral world.
normal.cn: elicit 与 illicit 只差一个字母，却隔着一整个道德世界。

normal.en: Think of a fisherman waiting, not pulling hard.
normal.cn: 想象一个钓鱼的人，他在等，而不是猛拉。

normal.en: Say ih-LISS-it; the soft s sounds like something slipping out.
normal.cn: 读成 ih-LISS-it，柔和的 s 音像有东西滑出来。

normal.en: Pair it with question: a good question elicits, a bad one forces.
normal.cn: 和 question 配对：好问题引出，坏问题逼出。

abstract.en: What is freely offered is not elicited; the word always implies a small resistance.
abstract.cn: 自愿给出的东西不算被引出；这个词总含一点阻力。

abstract.en: Asking well is the art of making the hidden willing to appear.
abstract.cn: 好好发问，是让隐藏之物愿意出现的艺术。

abstract.en: The response was already there; the question only opened the door.
abstract.cn: 回应本来就在；问题只是开了门。

examples.en: The question elicited a long silence, then a name.
examples.cn: 这个问题先引出沉默，然后引出一个名字。

examples.en: The new rule elicited protests from every department.
examples.cn: 新规定引起每个部门的抗议。

examples.en: The old song elicited a story about his first job.
examples.cn: 那首老歌唤起了一个关于他第一份工作的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: e（向外）+ lic（诱）+ it：把深处的答案诱出来，就是「引出」。

root: 拉丁语 lacere（引诱），加前缀 ex-（向外）→ elicere（诱出）

sensesIntro.en: Elicit always describes a two-way event: something hidden on one side, a skilled touch on the other, and a result that comes out.
sensesIntro.cn: elicit 总描述一个双向事件：一边藏着东西，一边有技巧性的触碰，然后有个结果出来。

branches.en: Answers, details and data obtained by asking.
branches.cn: 通过提问得到的回答、细节与数据。

branches.en: Reactions such as protest, applause and anger.
branches.cn: 抗议、掌声与愤怒这类反应。

branches.en: Memories carried back into the present.
branches.cn: 被带回当下的记忆。

branches.en: Small involuntary signs, like a smile.
branches.cn: 微笑这类不由自主的小信号。

branches.en: The same pulling can inform or provoke.
branches.cn: 同一种拉拽，可以告知，也可以激怒。

intro.en: The lic family is about attracting and drawing: elicit draws out, allure attracts, and lace once meant a snare.
intro.cn: lic 词族与吸引、牵引有关：elicit 引出，allure 吸引，而 lace 曾指一道网罗。

latinIntro.en: Latin lacere means to entice; the prefix ex- turns enticement into extraction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lacere 意为引诱；前缀 ex- 把「诱」变成「取出」。

items.example: The test elicited a clear answer.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试引出了一个清楚的答案。

items.example: Her elicitous reply pleased the room.
items.exampleCN: 她得体的回答让全场满意。

items.meaningCN: 不被允许、在法律之外的
items.example: The illicit trade continued at night.

items.exampleCN: 这个报价吸引了许多买家。

items.example: The delicacy melted on the tongue.

definition_zh: 谜；难以理解的人或事物
definition_en: something or someone that is puzzling and hard to explain
core_image: 一封信上写满看不懂的符号，纸角还压着一枚不属于任何国家的邮票
scene: 她从不解释自己为什么每周三消失，办公室的人猜了很久。Her silence remained an enigma to everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 enigma 指难以理解的人（第 1 个义项：谜一般的人）；句意为她的沉默对所有人始终是个谜。

senses.title: A puzzling person
senses.definition: a person whose motives or history cannot be read
senses.definitionCN: 动机或经历无法被读懂的人
senses.example: Her silence remained an enigma to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 她的沉默对所有人始终是个谜。
senses.why: People become enigmas when the usual signs, face, tone and habit, stop yielding meaning.
senses.whyCN: 当惯常的符号，表情、语气与习惯，不再给出意义时，人就变成谜。

senses.title: A puzzling event
senses.definition: an occurrence that has no obvious explanation
senses.definitionCN: 没有明显解释的事件
senses.example: The empty boat was an enigma the village never solved.
senses.exampleCN: 那条空船是村子始终没解开的谜。
senses.why: An event becomes an enigma when its cause is missing but its effect is plain.
senses.whyCN: 当原因缺失而结果清楚时，事件就成了谜。

senses.title: A coded message
senses.definition: a text or signal written to be unreadable without a key
senses.definitionCN: 没有密钥便无法读懂的文本或信号
senses.example: The message was an enigma until the key was found.
senses.exampleCN: 在找到密钥之前，这段讯息是个谜。
senses.why: Here the word is technical: the meaning exists, but the route to it is locked.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词是技术性的：意义存在，通往它的路线却被锁住。

senses.title: An unexplained natural thing
senses.definition: a feature of nature whose cause science has not settled
senses.definitionCN: 科学尚未确定成因的自然特征
senses.example: The migration of the birds is still an enigma.
senses.exampleCN: 这些鸟的迁徙仍是一个谜。
senses.why: Nature keeps a store of questions that resist every simple model.
senses.whyCN: 自然保存着一批拒绝任何简单模型的问题。

senses.title: A work hard to interpret
senses.definition: a book, film or painting whose meaning stays open
senses.definitionCN: 意义始终敞着、难以定论的书、影片或画
senses.example: The final chapter is an enigma by design.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一章是刻意留下的谜。
senses.why: Art can use the same lock as a code, but here the missing key is the point.
senses.whyCN: 艺术可以使用与密码相同的锁，但这里缺失的钥匙正是重点。

senses.title: A national puzzle
senses.definition: a public mystery that a whole society discusses
senses.definitionCN: 整个社会都在讨论的公共谜团
senses.example: The vanished ship became a national enigma.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘消失的船成了举国之谜。
senses.why: Scale turns a private puzzle into a shared one, and sharing keeps it alive.
senses.whyCN: 规模把私人的谜变成共同的谜，而共同讨论让它活下来。

senses.title: Enigma as charm
senses.definition: the attractive quality of a person who does not explain everything
senses.definitionCN: 一个不把一切说清的人身上的吸引力
senses.example: He cultivated his enigma as other men cultivate a garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他像别人打理花园那样打理自己的神秘感。
senses.why: Mystery can be a strategy: what is not told keeps other people thinking.
senses.whyCN: 神秘可以是一种策略：没说出的部分让别人一直想着。

senses.title: A riddle of history
senses.definition: an unresolved question about the past that evidence cannot close
senses.definitionCN: 证据无法收束的、关于过去的未解问题
senses.example: Historians still argue over the enigma of the lost colony.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家仍在争论那个消失殖民地的谜。
senses.why: The past leaves gaps that no amount of evidence can fill, and the gap itself becomes a subject.
senses.whyCN: 过去留下的空白，再多证据也填不满，而空白本身成了主题。

intro.en: Enigma is a Greek word for a riddle, and it shares an origin with the word 'guess'.
intro.cn: enigma 是希腊语中表示谜语的词，它与英语的 guess 出自同一来源。

items.en: Greek ainigma meant 'a dark saying, a riddle', something spoken to be decoded.
items.cn: 希腊语 ainigma 意为「隐语、谜语」，是为被解码而说出的东西。

items.en: Ainissesthai 'to speak darkly' is the verb behind it, from a root for tale or story.
items.cn: ainissesthai「隐晦地说」是其背后的动词，词根与故事有关。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as aenigma, keeping both the riddle and the darkness.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 aenigma，把谜语与晦暗都保留下来。

items.en: English took it in the 16c.; by the 17c. it could describe a person as well as a text.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入；到十七世纪它已能形容人，也能形容文本。

items.en: Today it covers ciphers, natural puzzles and anyone whose motives stay closed.
items.cn: 今天它覆盖密码、自然谜题，以及任何动机封闭的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the enigmatic stem; the near-meaning group distinguishes kinds of unexplained things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 enigmatic 词干；近义组区分不同种类的未解之物。

entries.definition: puzzling and hard to read.
in a puzzling manner.
the Greek plural of enigma.
the quality of being puzzling.
a question posed as a puzzle to be solved.
entries.definitionCN: 作为待解谜题提出的问题。

entries.definition: something unknown or unexplained.
a problem that confuses the mind.
a secret way of writing or a text in it.
entries.definitionCN: 秘密写法或以此写成的文本。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a letter full of symbols that no one in the room can read.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一封信写满符号、屋里没人读得懂」的画面。

normal.en: Enigma hides a name: the Enigma machine was the coded puzzle of the war.
normal.cn: enigma 藏着一个名字：Enigma 密码机就是那场战争中的谜。

normal.en: Say ih-NIG-muh; the short i sounds like a locked door.
normal.cn: 读成 ih-NIG-muh，短促的 i 像一扇锁住的门。

normal.en: Link with guess: both come from the same old root for telling a tale.
normal.cn: 和 guess 联系：两者都出自同一个表示「讲故事」的古词根。

normal.en: Think of a box with no lid and no visible seam.
normal.cn: 想象一个没有盖子、也看不到接缝的盒子。

normal.en: Enigma ends in -ma, like drama: a mystery is something staged for others to watch.
normal.cn: enigma 以 -ma 结尾，像 drama：谜是被摆出来给人看的戏。

abstract.en: A code and a person can be equally unreadable; the word does not care which.
abstract.cn: 密码和人可以同样难读；这个词不在乎是哪一个。

abstract.en: Mystery is not ignorance; it is knowledge that something is deliberately withheld.
abstract.cn: 神秘不是无知；它是知道有东西被刻意扣住。

abstract.en: What resists explanation longest often attracts the most attention.
abstract.cn: 最久拒绝解释的东西，往往吸引最多注意。

examples.en: Her silence remained an enigma to everyone.
examples.cn: 她的沉默对所有人始终是个谜。

examples.en: The empty boat was an enigma the village never solved.
examples.cn: 那条空船是村子始终没解开的谜。

examples.en: The migration of the birds is still an enigma.
examples.cn: 这些鸟的迁徙仍是一个谜。

dict_mnemonic.text: e（出）+ nig（暗）+ ma（名词）：从暗处说出的东西，就是「谜」。

root: 希腊语 ainigma（谜语），源自 ainissesthai（隐晦地说）

sensesIntro.en: An enigma is a meaning that exists but will not come out; the senses differ in what is holding the door shut.
sensesIntro.cn: enigma 是一个存在却不肯出来的意义；各义项的差别在于谁把门关着。

core.en: A MEANING THAT WILL NOT COME OUT

branches.en: A person whose motives stay closed, and the charm that follows.
branches.cn: 动机封闭的人，以及随之而来的魅力。

branches.en: Events and public puzzles that a whole society discusses.
branches.cn: 整个社会讨论的事件与公共谜团。

branches.en: Coded text that needs a key.
branches.cn: 需要钥匙的密码文本。

branches.en: Nature and history keeping questions open.
branches.cn: 自然与历史保持开放的问题。

branches.en: Art that leaves the key missing on purpose.
branches.cn: 故意让钥匙缺失的艺术。

intro.en: The enigm family keeps the same lock: a noun for the puzzle, an adjective for its manner and an adverb for how it is done.
intro.cn: enigm 词族守着同一把锁：名词指谜，形容词指其气质，副词指其做法。

latinIntro.en: Greek ainigma came through Latin aenigma; the spelling settled on en-, but the darkness stayed.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 ainigma 经拉丁语 aenigma 传来；拼写落定为 en-，而晦暗留了下来。

items.meaning: of the nature of a riddle

items.example: The old enigmata were never solved.
items.exampleCN: 那些古老的谜从未被解开。

items.meaning: a question with a hidden answer

items.example: The cipher used a shifting key.
items.exampleCN: 这套密码使用移位密钥。

definition_zh: 模棱两可的；含糊其辞的；可疑的
definition_en: open to more than one interpretation, often on purpose
core_image: 天平两端各放一个相同的砝码，指针停在正中，谁也说不出它偏向哪边
scene: 发言人被追问三次，每次都给出同一句可以两解的话。His equivocal answer satisfied nobody in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 equivocal 指故意含糊其辞（第 2 个义项：刻意回避明确表态）；句意为他的模棱两可谁也没能满意。

pos.zh: 模棱两可的；含糊的；可疑的

senses.title: Ambiguous wording
senses.definition: language that can be taken in two ways at once
senses.definitionCN: 可以同时被理解为两种意思的语言
senses.example: The clause is equivocal and will be argued over for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个条款措辞含混，会被争论多年。
senses.why: The word names a balance held between two readings, not a failure to write clearly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是两种读法之间的平衡，而不是没写清楚。

senses.title: Deliberately evasive
senses.definition: an answer shaped to avoid committing to either side
senses.definitionCN: 被塑造成不偏向任何一方的回答
senses.example: His equivocal answer satisfied nobody in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他的模棱两可谁也没能满意。
senses.why: Evasion is ambiguity with a purpose: the speaker could be clear and chooses not to be.
senses.whyCN: 回避是有目的的含糊：说话者本可以清楚，却选择不清楚。

senses.title: An uncertain result
senses.definition: an outcome that does not clearly favour one conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 没有明显偏向某个结论的结果
senses.example: The trial produced equivocal results.
senses.exampleCN: 这项试验得出了不确定的结果。
senses.why: Data can sit on the fence too, and when it does, no decision can lean on it.
senses.whyCN: 数据也会骑在墙上；它这样做时，任何决定都无法依靠它。

senses.title: Doubtful evidence
senses.definition: proof that may point either way, or may not be sound
senses.definitionCN: 可能指向任一方向、也可能本身不可靠的证据
senses.example: The equivocal witness damaged the case.
senses.exampleCN: 这位证词可疑的证人损害了案子。
senses.why: In law the word moves from unclear to suspect: what can mean anything proves nothing.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，这个词从「不清楚」移向「可疑」：什么都能证明的，什么也证明不了。

senses.title: Double-edged praise
senses.definition: a compliment that may also be heard as criticism
senses.definitionCN: 也可能被听成批评的称赞
senses.example: They called the design interesting, an equivocal compliment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们说这个设计「有意思」，这是一句两面性的称赞。
senses.why: Praise becomes equivocal when a second reading is left open beside the first.
senses.whyCN: 当第一种读法旁边还敞着第二种，称赞就变得模棱两可。

senses.title: Unreliable support
senses.definition: backing that is given in words too vague to count on
senses.definitionCN: 以含糊到无法依赖的言辞给出的支持
senses.example: The minister offered equivocal support for the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 部长对该计划给予了含糊的支持。
senses.why: Support that will not say what it will do is support that can be withdrawn later.
senses.whyCN: 不肯说明会做什么的支持，就是以后可以撤回的支持。

senses.title: An ambiguous signal
senses.definition: a sign that could mean yes, no, or something else
senses.definitionCN: 可能意味着是、否或别的什么的信号
senses.example: The light gave an equivocal signal and the driver stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 那盏灯给出含糊的信号，司机停了下来。
senses.why: A machine or a person can send a sign that leaves the choice of meaning entirely to the receiver.
senses.whyCN: 机器或人都能发出一种信号，把意义的选择完全留给接收者。

senses.title: An answer that avoids yes
senses.definition: a reply that neither accepts nor refuses
senses.definitionCN: 既不接受也不拒绝的回应
senses.example: Asked to resign, he gave an equivocal reply and stayed.
senses.exampleCN: 被要求辞职时，他给了个不置可否的回答，然后留了下来。
senses.why: Saying nothing clearly is still a move in the game, and often the safest one.
senses.whyCN: 不说清楚仍然是棋局中的一步，而且常常是最安全的一步。

intro.en: Equivocal joins equal and voice: it means two voices speaking from one word.
intro.cn: equivocal 把「相等」与「声音」接在一起：它指一个词里有两个声音在说话。

items.en: English formed the word in the 16c. from Latin pieces rather than borrowing it whole.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪用拉丁语部件造出这个词，而不是整体借入。

items.en: Aequus means equal, level, fair, and gives equal and equity.
items.cn: aequus 意为相等、平、公正，给出 equal 与 equity。

items.en: Vox means voice; the word pictures two voices of equal strength.
items.cn: vox 意为声音；这个词描绘两个力量相等的声音。

items.en: Late Latin aequivocus meant 'of the same name, ambiguous'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 aequivocus 意为「同名、歧义」。

items.en: The modern word adds suspicion: ambiguity that benefits the speaker.
items.cn: 现代词又添了怀疑：对说话者有利的含糊。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on the equal-voice root; the near-meaning group names kinds of unclear speech.
note.cn: 形近组围绕「声音相等」的词根；近义组列出各种不清楚的说法。

entries.definition: clear and leaving no doubt.
to speak vaguely so as to avoid commitment.
the act of using ambiguous words.
equal in value or meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 在价值或意义上相等的。

entries.definition: having more than one possible meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 有不止一种可能含义的。

entries.definition: not clearly expressed or defined.
deliberately avoiding a direct answer.
not revealing one's position.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a balance holding perfectly still between two equal weights.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「天平在两个相等砝码之间完全静止」的画面。

normal.en: Equivocal = equal + voice: two voices of the same volume, neither winning.
normal.cn: equivocal = equal + voice：两个声音音量相同，谁也不赢。

normal.en: Compare unequivocal: adding un- tips the balance to one side.
normal.cn: 对比 unequivocal：加上 un- 就把天平倾向一边。

normal.en: Think of a coin standing on its edge.
normal.cn: 想象一枚硬币立在边缘上。

normal.en: Say ih-KWIV-uh-kl; the quick middle sounds like a dodge.
normal.cn: 读成 ih-KWIV-uh-kl，中间的快音像一次闪避。

normal.en: Link with vocal: both are about voice, and here the voice is doubled.
normal.cn: 和 vocal 联系：两者都与声音有关，而这里声音是双重的。

abstract.en: Ambiguity can be a mistake or a shelter; the word suspects the shelter.
abstract.cn: 含糊可以是错误，也可以是掩体；这个词怀疑的是掩体。

abstract.en: A statement that can mean two things has not yet said either of them.
abstract.cn: 能表示两件事的话，其实哪件都还没说。

abstract.en: Where nothing is risked in words, nothing is promised either.
abstract.cn: 言语里不冒风险的地方，也没有承诺。

examples.en: His equivocal answer satisfied nobody in the room.
examples.cn: 他的模棱两可谁也没能满意。

examples.en: The trial produced equivocal results.
examples.cn: 这项试验得出了不确定的结果。

examples.en: The minister offered equivocal support for the plan.
examples.cn: 部长对该计划给予了含糊的支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: equi（相等）+ voc（声音）+ al：两个声音一样响，就是「模棱两可」。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（相等）+ vox（声音）→ aequivocus（同名的、歧义的）

sensesIntro.en: Every sense keeps two readings in balance; the difference is whether the balance is an accident, a tactic or a warning sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都让两种读法保持平衡；差别在于这平衡是意外、战术，还是警示。

branches.en: Wording, compliments and signals that carry two readings.
branches.cn: 带两种读法的措辞、称赞与信号。

branches.en: Answers built to avoid commitment.
branches.cn: 为回避表态而造的回答。

branches.en: Results and evidence that point both ways.
branches.cn: 指向两边的结果与证据。

branches.en: Support too vague to be relied on.
branches.cn: 含糊到无法依赖的支持。

branches.en: The same balance may be honest doubt or a tactic.
branches.cn: 同一种平衡，可能是诚实的疑问，也可能是战术。

intro.en: The equi family measures equality: equivocal balances two voices, equivalent balances two values, equity balances two claims.
intro.cn: equi 词族衡量相等：equivocal 平衡两个声音，equivalent 平衡两个价值，equity 平衡两个主张。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus supplies the balance and vox the sound; the compound literally weighs two voices against each other.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 提供平衡，vox 提供声音；这个复合词字面上把两个声音互相比量。

items.exampleCN: 含糊其辞为他争得了时间。
这项政策以公平为目标。

definition_zh: 博学；学识；学问
definition_en: deep and wide learning gained from serious reading and study
core_image: 书房里四面是书，桌上摊开三本对照的旧注，页边写满细小的铅笔字
scene: 他在讨论中随口引了三个世纪的注释，却从不炫耀。Her erudition made the lecture feel effortless.
sceneCN: 这里 erudition 指深厚的学问（第 1 个义项：广博而扎实的学识）；句意为她的博学让讲座显得毫不费力。

senses.title: Deep book learning
senses.definition: knowledge built up through long and serious reading
senses.definitionCN: 通过长期认真阅读积累起来的知识
senses.example: Her erudition made the lecture feel effortless.
senses.exampleCN: 她的博学让讲座显得毫不费力。
senses.why: The word respects depth: it is not knowing many facts but having read into a subject.
senses.whyCN: 这个词尊重深度：它不是知道许多事实，而是读进了某个领域。

senses.title: Wide reading
senses.definition: breadth of reading that lets a person connect distant fields
senses.definitionCN: 广到能把遥远领域连起来的阅读量
senses.example: His erudition let him move from law to poetry in one sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他的博览让他一句话里从法律走到诗歌。
senses.why: Breadth shows up as ease of movement; the reader is at home in more than one room.
senses.whyCN: 广度表现为移动的轻松；读者在不止一个房间里都自在。

senses.title: Scholarly display
senses.definition: the visible showing of learning in a way that draws attention
senses.definitionCN: 把学识摆出来以引人注意
senses.example: The footnote was erudition worn on the sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 那条脚注是把学问穿在袖子上。
senses.why: The same noun can turn critical: learning shown off reads as vanity rather than depth.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也会转成批评：被炫耀的学识读起来是虚荣，而不是深度。

senses.title: Mastery of a field
senses.definition: the specialised knowledge that comes from years inside one discipline
senses.definitionCN: 在某一学科内多年积累出的专门知识
senses.example: The essay shows real erudition in medieval law.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章在中世纪法律上显出真正的专门学问。
senses.why: Depth in one field looks different from breadth: it knows the small quarrels, not only the big names.
senses.whyCN: 一域的深度与广度不同：它知道细小的争论，不只知名的大名字。

senses.title: Learning in writing
senses.definition: the quality of a text that carries a long tradition behind it
senses.definitionCN: 一个文本承载着悠久传统的品质
senses.example: The preface has an erudition that no summary can replace.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇序言有一种任何摘要都替代不了的学识。
senses.why: A preface carries the history of how a book came to be, which no summary can compress.
senses.whyCN: 序言承载着一本书如何形成的历史，这是任何摘要都无法压缩的。

senses.title: Erudition as dryness
senses.definition: knowledge that has lost contact with ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 已经与日常语言失去联系的知识
senses.example: The book's erudition keeps most readers at a distance.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书的学问让大多数读者敬而远之。
senses.why: When learning stops translating itself, it starts to feel like a wall rather than a window.
senses.whyCN: 当学问不再翻译自己，它开始像一堵墙，而不是一扇窗。

senses.title: Old-world scholarship
senses.definition: the traditional learning of commentaries, languages and marginal notes
senses.definitionCN: 由注释、语言与边注构成的传统学问
