senses.example: He was the last of a line of erudition in three languages.
senses.exampleCN: 他是三代三语学问的最后一人。
senses.why: The word carries a faint nostalgia for a time when reading was a lifetime trade.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带一点怀旧，怀念阅读曾是一门终身手艺的时代。

senses.title: Learning without wisdom
senses.definition: knowledge accumulated without the judgement to use it well
senses.definitionCN: 积累起来却缺乏善用它的判断力的知识
senses.example: His erudition was immense and his conclusions were careless.
senses.exampleCN: 他的学问极大，结论却草率。
senses.why: The word itself stays neutral, but its pairing exposes the old worry: knowing is not yet understanding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身是中性的，但它与「草率」并置时暴露了古老的忧虑：知道还不等于理解。

intro.en: Erudition comes from a Latin word meaning out of roughness: a mind taken out of its raw state by teaching.
intro.cn: erudition 来自一个意为「从粗朴中出来」的拉丁词：经过教导，心智从原始状态里被带出来。

items.en: English took the noun in the 16c., when scholarship was still a public ornament.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个名词，当时学问仍是一种公共装饰。

items.en: Eruditio meant 'instruction, learning', the process as well as the result.
items.cn: eruditio 意为「教导、学问」，既指过程也指结果。

items.en: Erudire meant 'to bring out of roughness, to instruct', built from ex- and rudis.
items.cn: erudire 意为「使脱出粗糙、教导」，由 ex- 与 rudis 构成。

items.en: Rudis meant raw, rough, untrained, and gives the English word rude.
items.cn: rudis 意为生的、粗的、未受训练的，也给出英语 rude。

items.en: By the 18c. the word could already be used with irony for mere book display.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词已能带反讽地指单纯的书本展示。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the erudite stem; the near-meaning group separates kinds of knowledge.
note.cn: 形近组共享 erudite 词干；近义组区分不同种类的知识。

entries.definition: showing deep learning.
in a learned manner.
the quality of being learned.
moral or intellectual improvement.
careful academic study and its results.
entries.definitionCN: 严谨的学术研究及其成果。

entries.definition: knowledge gained by study, in general.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指通过学习获得的知识。

entries.definition: learning shown off through unnecessary detail.
entries.definitionCN: 借不必要的细节炫耀学问。

entries.definition: refined knowledge of the world and its ways.
entries.definitionCN: 对世界及其运作的老练认识。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a study with books open on every table and pencil marks in every margin.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「书房里每张桌子都摊着书、每页边都写着铅笔字」的画面。

normal.en: Erudition shares a root with rude: learning is what takes the roughness off.
normal.cn: erudition 与 rude 同根：学问就是把粗糙去掉。

normal.en: Think of an old library where the floor creaks under the weight of notes.
normal.cn: 想象一座老图书馆，地板被笔记的重量压得吱呀作响。

normal.en: Say eh-roo-DISH-un; the ending sounds like a mouth full of footnotes.
normal.cn: 读成 eh-roo-DISH-un，结尾听起来像满嘴脚注。

normal.en: Link with read: erudition is what many thousands of pages leave behind.
normal.cn: 和 read 联系：博学是几千页阅读留下的东西。

normal.en: Erudite has the same pattern as polite: a quality worn, not a thing owned.
normal.cn: erudite 与 polite 结构相似：是穿在身上的品质，不是占有的东西。

abstract.en: Learning becomes erudition when it can move between fields without losing its footing.
abstract.cn: 当学问能在领域间移动而不失脚，它就成了博学。

abstract.en: The same knowledge can be a window or a wall, depending on whether it translates.
abstract.cn: 同样的知识可以是窗也可以是墙，取决于它是否翻译自己。

abstract.en: Reading widely is not the same as thinking widely, though it helps.
abstract.cn: 读得广不等于想得广，虽然读得广有帮助。

examples.en: Her erudition made the lecture feel effortless.
examples.cn: 她的博学让讲座显得毫不费力。

examples.en: His erudition let him move from law to poetry in one sentence.
examples.cn: 他的博览让他一句话里从法律走到诗歌。

examples.en: The footnote was erudition worn on the sleeve.
examples.cn: 那条脚注是把学问穿在袖子上。

dict_mnemonic.text: e（出）+ rud（粗）+ ition（名词）：把粗朴的心智带出来，就是「博学」。

root: 拉丁语 rudis（粗朴、未受训）加前缀 ex-（出）→ erudire（教导）

sensesIntro.en: Erudition is accumulated reading made visible; the senses differ in whether the reading is deep, wide, displayed or dried out.
sensesIntro.cn: erudition 是被积累并被看见的阅读；各义项的差别在于这阅读是深、是广、是被展示，还是已经干枯。

branches.en: Depth built inside one discipline.
branches.cn: 在一个学科内部积成的深度。

branches.en: Breadth that lets a text or a speaker cross fields.
branches.cn: 让文本或讲者跨越领域的广度。

branches.en: The same learning shown off or gone dry.
branches.cn: 被炫耀或已干枯的同一种学问。

branches.en: The traditional scholarship of languages and notes.
branches.cn: 语言与注释构成的传统学问。

branches.en: Knowledge that outruns judgement.
branches.cn: 跑在判断力前面的知识。

intro.en: The rud family is about rawness and training: erudition removes roughness, and rude names what is still rough.
intro.cn: rud 词族与生糙和训练有关：erudition 去掉粗糙，rude 则命名仍然粗糙的东西。

latinIntro.en: Latin rudis means raw; ex- means out of, so erudire is literally to bring a mind out of its raw state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rudis 意为生的；ex- 意为出自，因此 erudire 字面就是把心智从生涩状态里带出来。

items.example: The erudite judge cited old cases.
items.exampleCN: 这位博学的法官引用了旧案。

items.example: A rude shelter stood by the road.
items.exampleCN: 路边有一座简陋的棚子。

items.example: He learned the rudiments of sailing.
The journal is an eruditional project.
items.exampleCN: 这份期刊是一项学术工程。

latinEntries.meaning: to instruct, to bring out of rawness

definition_zh: 短暂的；易消散的；转瞬即逝的
definition_en: lasting only a very short time and fading like vapour
core_image: 清晨窗上的一层白气，手指一划就留下痕迹，几分钟后连痕迹也没有了
scene: 烟花在半空炸开，亮了一下，随后只剩烟。The beauty of the evanescent flare outlived nothing but the memory of it.
sceneCN: 这里 evanescent 指转瞬即逝的（第 1 个义项：像雾一样迅速消散）；句意为那短暂的光华除了记忆什么也没留下。

pos.zh: 短暂的；易消散的；转瞬即逝的

senses.title: Fading like vapour
senses.definition: passing out of sight the way mist thins in the air
senses.definitionCN: 像雾在空气中变薄那样从视野中消失
senses.example: The evanescent flare left only smoke behind.
senses.exampleCN: 那转瞬即逝的闪光只留下了烟。
senses.why: The word's oldest picture is vapour: visible, weightless, and already going.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的画面是蒸汽：可见、无重，而且已经在走。

senses.title: Brief fame
senses.definition: attention that rises quickly and is gone before it settles
senses.definitionCN: 迅速升起、还未落定就消失的关注
senses.example: The singer enjoyed an evanescent fame of two seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 这位歌手享受了两个季度的短暂声名。
senses.why: Attention arrives faster than a career can be built, so it can leave before the work exists.
senses.whyCN: 关注来得比事业建成更快，因此它可能在工作成形之前就离开。

senses.title: Fleeting beauty
senses.definition: beauty whose value partly comes from how soon it ends
senses.definitionCN: 其价值部分来自结束之快的美
senses.example: The evanescent colours of the sunset drew a crowd to the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 日落那转瞬即逝的色彩把人群引到岸边。
senses.why: Some beauty is intensified by its own disappearance, and the word knows this.
senses.whyCN: 有些美因自身的消失而更强烈，这个词懂得这一点。

senses.title: A vanishing moment
senses.definition: a short interval that cannot be held or repeated
senses.definitionCN: 无法被握住或重复的短暂间隙
senses.example: For an evanescent moment the two rivals looked like friends.
senses.exampleCN: 有那么转瞬一刻，两个对手看起来像朋友。
senses.why: A moment can hold a whole possibility that the rest of the year does not allow.
senses.whyCN: 一个瞬间可以装下整年里其余时间都不允许的可能性。

senses.title: A faint trace
senses.definition: a mark so light that it is almost not there
senses.definitionCN: 轻到几乎不存在的痕迹
senses.example: Only an evanescent scent remained in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里只剩一缕快散尽的香气。
senses.why: A trace is what a disappearing thing leaves behind, and it fades at its own speed.
senses.whyCN: 痕迹是消失之物留下的东西，而它按自己的速度淡去。

senses.title: A passing fashion
senses.definition: a trend that burns bright and leaves no structure behind
senses.definitionCN: 烧得亮却不留结构的潮流
senses.example: The style was evanescent, gone before the shops stocked it.
senses.exampleCN: 这种风格转瞬即逝，商店还没进货它就没了。
senses.why: A trend lives on imitation, and imitation cannot keep up with a thing that is already leaving.
senses.whyCN: 潮流靠模仿存活，而模仿追不上一个已经在离开的东西。

senses.title: Evaporating scent
senses.definition: a smell that lifts away as soon as it is noticed
senses.definitionCN: 一被察觉就升走的味道
senses.example: The evanescent scent of cut grass filled the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 割草的香气在傍晚散开，又很快散去。
senses.why: Scent is the most honest test of the word: it is present only while it is leaving.
senses.whyCN: 香气是这个词最诚实的检验：它只在离开时才存在。

senses.title: A fading memory
senses.definition: a recollection that loses detail every time it is recalled
senses.definitionCN: 每次被回想都失去细节的记忆
senses.example: The face had become evanescent, more feeling than feature.
senses.exampleCN: 那张脸已渐渐淡去，更多是感觉而非五官。
senses.why: Memory behaves like vapour too: the more often it is handled, the thinner it gets.
senses.whyCN: 记忆也像蒸汽：被触碰得越多，它越薄。

intro.en: Evanescent comes from a Latin verb meaning to vanish, and it keeps the picture of something thinning into air.
intro.cn: evanescent 来自一个意为「消失」的拉丁动词，它保留着某物变薄、化入空气的画面。

items.en: English took the adjective in the 18c., often for colours, scents and pleasures.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入这个形容词，常用于色彩、香气与快乐。

items.en: Evanescere meant 'to vanish, to pass away', built from ex- and vanescere.
items.cn: evanescere 意为「消失、逝去」，由 ex- 与 vanescere 构成。

items.en: Vanus meant empty, hollow, and gives vain and vanish.
items.cn: vanus 意为空的、虚的，给出 vain 与 vanish。

items.en: Ex- means out; the movement is outward until nothing is left.
items.cn: ex- 意为出；动作向外，直到什么也不剩。

items.en: In poetry the word often carries a gentle grief rather than plain shortness.
items.cn: 在诗歌里，这个词常带一点轻柔的哀伤，而不只是短暂。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vanishing stem; the near-meaning group measures how long things last.
note.cn: 形近组共享「消失」词干；近义组衡量事物持续的时长。

entries.definition: the quality of fading away.
to fade from sight.
in a fleeting manner.
the act of avoiding something.
lasting only a moment.
staying only a short time.
lasting for a very short span, often by nature.
passing quickly or hard to hold.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速掠过或难以握住的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of breath on cold glass, wiped away and then gone.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「冷玻璃上的白气，被擦掉，然后彻底不见」的画面。

normal.en: Evanescent contains vanish: same empty root, same departure.
normal.cn: evanescent 里有 vanish：同一个「空」的词根，同一种离开。

normal.en: Think of steam over a cup, visible one second and gone the next.
normal.cn: 想象杯子上方的热气，一瞬可见，下一瞬就没了。

normal.en: Say ee-vuh-NESS-unt; the soft ending sounds like a sigh of leaving.
normal.cn: 读成 ee-vuh-NESS-unt，柔和的结尾像一声离去的叹息。

normal.en: Link with vain: both come from Latin vanus, empty.
normal.cn: 和 vain 联系：两者都出自拉丁语 vanus（空）。

normal.en: The word is long and the thing is short, which is its own joke.
normal.cn: 词很长，所指的是很短，这本身就是个笑话。

abstract.en: What lasts is not always what matters, and what fades is not always worthless.
abstract.cn: 持久的未必重要，消散的未必无价值。

abstract.en: Some beauty needs its disappearance to be seen at all.
abstract.cn: 有些美必须靠消失才能被看见。

abstract.en: A trace is proof that something was, even as it proves it is going.
abstract.cn: 痕迹既证明某物曾在，也证明它正在离开。

examples.en: The evanescent flare left only smoke behind.
examples.cn: 那转瞬即逝的闪光只留下了烟。

examples.en: The singer enjoyed an evanescent fame of two seasons.
examples.cn: 这位歌手享受了两个季度的短暂声名。

examples.en: Only an evanescent scent remained in the room.
examples.cn: 房间里只剩一缕快散尽的香气。

dict_mnemonic.text: e（出）+ van（空）+ escent（正在……的）：正在化为空，就是「转瞬即逝」。

root: 拉丁语 vanus（空）→ vanescere（消散），加前缀 ex-（出）→ evanescere

sensesIntro.en: Every sense has the same shape: something appears, is barely held, and leaves; only the thing that fades changes.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是同一个形状：某物出现、几乎握不住、然后离开；变的只是淡去之物。

branches.en: Vapour and scent, the word's oldest pictures.
branches.cn: 蒸汽与香气，这个词最古老的画面。

branches.en: Fame and fashion that leave no structure.
branches.cn: 不留下结构的声名与风尚。

branches.en: Beauty and moments valued for their brevity.
branches.cn: 因短暂而被珍视的美与瞬间。

branches.en: Traces and memories that thin with handling.
branches.cn: 因被触碰而变薄的痕迹与记忆。

branches.en: Fading can deepen as well as destroy.
branches.cn: 淡去既能加深，也能摧毁。

intro.en: The van family is about emptiness: evanescent thins to nothing, vain is hollow, and vanish is the plain verb.
intro.cn: van 词族与空有关：evanescent 薄到没有，vain 是空的，vanish 则是最朴素的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vanus means empty; the prefix ex- adds outward motion, so the word pictures emptiness spreading out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vanus 意为空；前缀 ex- 加上向外的运动，于是这个词描绘「空」向外铺开。

items.example: The evanescent mist cleared by noon.
The evanescence of the image surprised him.
The coin vanished from his hand.
A transient guest stayed one night.

definition_zh: 使无罪；开脱；证明清白
definition_en: to clear someone of blame or guilt, especially by evidence
core_image: 法庭上一个人从被告席站起来，手里的文件让指控者在半句上停住
scene: 档案室里翻出一张旧收据，日期证明他当时在另一座城。The receipt exculpated him after twenty years.
sceneCN: 这里 exculpate 指证明某人无罪（第 3 个义项：法律上的免责）；句意为这张收据在二十年后洗清了他。

senses.title: Clear someone of blame
senses.definition: to remove the charge of wrongdoing from a person
senses.definitionCN: 把做错事的指控从一个人身上移走
senses.example: The receipt exculpated him after twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这张收据在二十年后洗清了他。
senses.why: The word is a legal act in miniature: blame is a weight, and exculpating takes it off.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是一个缩小的法律行为：责任是重量，而开脱把它拿走。

senses.title: Evidence that excuses
senses.definition: to show by proof that a person could not have done the act
senses.definitionCN: 以证据表明某人不可能做出该行为
senses.example: A new witness exculpated the driver entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 一位新证人完全洗清了这位司机。
senses.why: Proof works by closing a possibility: if he was elsewhere, the act cannot attach to him.
senses.whyCN: 证据靠关闭一种可能来起作用：如果他人在别处，行为就附不到他身上。

senses.title: Legal exoneration
senses.definition: to establish in law that a person is not guilty
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上确认某人无罪
senses.example: The court exculpated the company of all charges.
senses.exampleCN: 法院免除了公司的一切指控。
senses.why: In law the word has a formal force: it changes the record, not only the mood.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，这个词有正式效力：它改变记录，而不只是气氛。

senses.title: Excuse a mistake
senses.definition: to explain a fault in a way that lessens responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 以减轻责任的方式解释一个过失
senses.example: He tried to exculpate himself by blaming the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 他试图把责任推给日程来为自己开脱。
senses.why: Blaming a circumstance is the cheapest form of self-defence, and the least convincing.
senses.whyCN: 把责任推给环境是最廉价的自辩，也最难令人信服。

senses.title: Clear a reputation
senses.definition: to restore the public name of someone wrongly suspected
senses.definitionCN: 恢复被错误怀疑者的公众名声
senses.example: The inquiry exculpated the teacher and apologised.
senses.exampleCN: 调查为这位教师洗清并致歉。
senses.why: Reputation is a social possession; clearing it returns what suspicion had taken.
senses.whyCN: 名誉是一种社会财产；洗清就是把怀疑拿走的东西还回去。

senses.title: Self-exculpation
senses.definition: to justify one's own conduct so as to escape blame
senses.definitionCN: 为自己的行为辩解以逃避责任
senses.example: His memoir is a long exercise in self-exculpation.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回忆录是一场漫长的自我开脱。
senses.why: When the accused explains, the explanation may be evidence or merely defence.
senses.whyCN: 当被指控者解释时，那解释可能是证据，也可能只是辩护。

senses.title: Exculpate an institution
senses.definition: to clear an organisation of responsibility for a failure
senses.definitionCN: 免除一个组织对某次失败的责任
senses.example: The report exculpated the agency and faulted the contractor.
senses.exampleCN: 报告免除了该机构的责任，把过错归于承包商。
senses.why: Institutions cannot feel blame, but their records can be cleared, which is why the word matters to them.
senses.whyCN: 机构不会感到羞耻，但它们的记录可以被洗清，这正是这个词对它们重要的原因。

senses.title: Moral clearing
senses.definition: to show that someone's intentions were not corrupt
senses.definitionCN: 表明某人的动机并不败坏
senses.example: The letters exculpated him morally, if not legally.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件在道德上为他洗清，尽管法律上未必。
senses.why: Being without guilt and being without blame are different rooms, and the word can open either.
senses.whyCN: 没有罪与没有责是两间不同的屋子，而这个词能打开其中任一。

intro.en: Exculpate is built from out of and blame, so it means exactly to take the blame out of someone.
intro.cn: exculpate 由「出」与「责」构成，意思正是把责任从某人身上取出来。

items.en: English formed the verb in the 17c. from Latin parts, mostly in legal writing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪用拉丁部件造出这个动词，多用于法律文字。

items.en: Ex- means out of, away from, and marks the direction blame is moved.
items.cn: ex- 意为出、离开，标记责任被移走的方向。

items.en: Culpa means fault, blame, guilt, and gives culpable and culprit.
items.cn: culpa 意为过失、责备、罪，给出 culpable 与 culprit。

items.en: Late Latin exculpare meant 'to free from blame', the direct ancestor of the verb.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 exculpare 意为「免于责备」，是这个动词的直系祖先。

items.en: Modern law pairs it with exculpatory evidence, the proof that clears.
items.cn: 现代法律把它与 exculpatory evidence 配对，即洗清罪责的证据。

note.en: The look-alike group sits on the blame root; the near-meaning group distinguishes ways of removing fault.
note.cn: 形近组坐在「责」的词根上；近义组区分移除过错的不同方式。

entries.definition: serving to clear a person of blame.
the act of clearing blame.
deserving blame.
to involve in blame.
to declare a person not guilty in court.
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上宣布某人无罪。

entries.definition: to show that someone or something was right.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某人或某物是正确的。

entries.definition: to free a person from guilt or punishment.
to forgive an offence and its punishment.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a document placed on a courtroom table, stopping an accusation mid-sentence.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一份文件放上法庭桌子，让指控说到一半就停住」的画面。

normal.en: Exculpate = ex + culpa: out of blame, exactly as spelled.
normal.cn: exculpate = ex + culpa：从责备中出来，正是字面的意思。

normal.en: Culpa also hides in culprit: the one held to blame.
normal.cn: culpa 也藏在 culprit 里：被认作有过错的人。

normal.en: Think of a heavy coat of blame being lifted off someone's shoulders.
normal.cn: 想象一件沉重的外套被从某人肩上提起来。

normal.en: Say iks-KUL-pate; the stress lands on the fault being moved.
normal.cn: 读成 iks-KUL-pate，重音落在被移走的那个过错上。

normal.en: Opposite in-culpate adds the blame; ex- takes it away.
normal.cn: 反义的 in-culpate 是加责，ex- 是去责。

abstract.en: Proof clears by closing possibilities, not by pleading.
abstract.cn: 证据靠关闭可能性来洗清，而不是靠哀求。

abstract.en: Being morally clean and being legally clean are different rooms.
abstract.cn: 道德上干净与法律上干净是不同的房间。

abstract.en: The first explanation after an accusation is always suspicious, even when it is true.
abstract.cn: 指控后的第一个解释总是可疑的，即使它是真的。

examples.en: The receipt exculpated him after twenty years.
examples.cn: 这张收据在二十年后洗清了他。

examples.en: A new witness exculpated the driver entirely.
examples.cn: 一位新证人完全洗清了这位司机。

examples.en: The inquiry exculpated the teacher and apologised.
examples.cn: 调查为这位教师洗清并致歉。

dict_mnemonic.text: ex（出）+ culp（责）+ ate（动词）：把责任拿出去，就是「开脱、洗清」。

root: 拉丁语 culpa（过失、责）加前缀 ex-（出）→ exculpare（免于责备）

sensesIntro.en: Exculpate always moves a weight off a person; the senses differ in whether the weight is legal guilt, public suspicion or moral doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: exculpate 总是把重量从人身上移开；各义项的差别在于这重量是法律责任、公众怀疑，还是道德疑云。

branches.en: The act of clearing and the proof that does it.
branches.cn: 洗清的行为，以及完成它的证据。

branches.en: Legal exoneration and the repair of a reputation.
branches.cn: 法律上的免责与名誉的修复。

branches.en: Explanations that try to shift fault away.
branches.cn: 试图把过错移开的解释。

branches.en: Institutions whose records can be cleared.
branches.cn: 记录可以被洗清的机构。

branches.en: The moral version: intentions shown to be sound.
branches.cn: 道德版本：动机被证明清白。

intro.en: The culp family is about blame: exculpate removes it, inculpate attaches it, and culpable means it fits.
intro.cn: culp 词族与责备有关：exculpate 移除，inculpate 附上，culpable 则是「合乎责备」。

latinIntro.en: Latin culpa is fault itself; the prefixes decide whether fault is being taken away or added.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 culpa 就是过错本身；前缀决定这过错是被拿走还是被加上。

items.exampleCN: 这部影片为飞行员洗清。
这盘录音带具有开脱性。
法院衡量他的责任程度。
这些信件使两名官员受责。

items.example: He offered a mea culpa in public.

definition_zh: 可能出错的；易犯错的；不可靠的
definition_en: capable of making mistakes or being wrong
core_image: 一把尺子的边缘有一道几乎看不见的弯，用久了才在长线上显出偏差
scene: 他在报告末尾写下一行小字，承认自己的估算可能偏差。The most careful method is still fallible at the edges.
sceneCN: 这里 fallible 指可能出错的（第 4 个义项：会出错的方法或系统）；句意为最细致的方法在边缘处仍会出错。

pos.zh: 可能出错的；易犯错的；不可靠的

senses.title: Capable of error
senses.definition: able to be mistaken, as every person is
senses.definitionCN: 可能判断错误，凡是人皆如此
senses.example: Any fallible reader can misread a single line.
senses.exampleCN: 任何会犯错的读者都可能看错一行。
senses.why: The word is not an insult; it states a condition shared by all thinking beings.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不是侮辱；它陈述一切思考者共有的条件。

senses.title: Fallible memory
senses.definition: a memory that changes or invents detail over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间改变或增添细节的记忆
senses.example: Her fallible memory turned three events into one.
senses.exampleCN: 她不可靠的记忆把三件事合为一件。
senses.why: Memory is not a recording but a reconstruction, and reconstruction can drift.
senses.whyCN: 记忆不是录音，而是重建，而重建会漂移。

senses.title: Fallible judgement
senses.definition: a decision that may be reasonable yet still wrong
senses.definitionCN: 可能合理却仍然错误的决定
senses.example: Even fallible judgement deserves to be heard.
senses.exampleCN: 即使可能出错的判断也值得被听见。
senses.why: A judgement that might be wrong still carries information that silence cannot.
senses.whyCN: 可能出错的判断仍携带沉默无法提供的信息。

senses.title: Fallible system
senses.definition: a method or machine that can fail at its limits
senses.definitionCN: 在极限处可能失效的方法或机器
senses.example: The most careful method is still fallible at the edges.
senses.exampleCN: 最细致的方法在边缘处仍会出错。
senses.why: A system is fallible not because it is badly built but because the world exceeds its rules.
senses.whyCN: 系统的易错不在于造得差，而在于世界超出了它的规则。

senses.title: Fallible authority
senses.definition: an expert or office whose word is not automatically true
senses.definitionCN: 其话并非自动为真的专家或机构
senses.example: Fallible authority still beats no authority at all.
senses.exampleCN: 会错的权威仍胜于完全没有权威。
senses.why: The word separates respect from surrender: an authority may be trusted without being treated as a god.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把尊重与投降分开：权威可以被信任，却不必被当作神。

senses.title: Human fallibility
senses.definition: the general condition that people can always be wrong
senses.definitionCN: 人总可能出错的普遍状况
senses.example: The design assumes human fallibility and adds a second check.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计预设人会出错，于是加了第二道检查。
senses.why: Good design does not deny the weakness; it plans for it.
senses.whyCN: 好的设计不否认弱点，而是为它作准备。

senses.title: Fallible proof
senses.definition: evidence that is strong but not beyond every doubt
senses.definitionCN: 有力却未超越一切怀疑的证据
senses.example: The case rested on fallible proof and a careful jury.
senses.exampleCN: 案子依靠不完美的证据与谨慎的陪审团。
senses.why: Most real proofs are strong without being airtight, and decisions must still be made.
senses.whyCN: 现实中的多数证明有力却不严密，而决定仍必须作出。

senses.title: Fallible but honest
senses.definition: a person who errs without intending to deceive
senses.definitionCN: 会出错却无意欺骗的人
senses.example: He was fallible but honest, and that was enough.
senses.exampleCN: 他会犯错，但诚实，这就够了。
senses.why: The word does not imply deceit; it only denies perfection.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不含欺骗之意；它只是否认完美。

intro.en: Fallible comes from a Latin verb meaning to deceive, so it names the capacity to be led astray.
intro.cn: fallible 来自一个意为「欺骗」的拉丁动词，因此它命名的是被引离正道的能力。

items.en: English took the adjective in the 17c., often in theology and law.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，常见于神学与法律。

items.en: Fallere meant 'to deceive, to trip up', the root of false and fail.
items.cn: fallere 意为「欺骗、使失足」，是 false 与 fail 的词根。

items.en: Fallibilis meant 'that can deceive or be deceived'.
items.cn: fallibilis 意为「能欺骗或能被欺骗的」。

items.en: Science adopted the word to state that all findings can be revised.
items.cn: 科学采用这个词，用来声明一切结论都可被修正。

items.en: Everyday English softened it: fallible now mostly means human, not deceitful.
items.cn: 日常英语把它软化：如今 fallible 多指「有人性的」，而非「欺骗的」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the false root; the near-meaning group names kinds of unreliability.
note.cn: 形近组共享「假」的词根；近义组列出不可靠的不同种类。

entries.definition: the capacity to be wrong.
incapable of error.
the state of being unable to err.
a mistaken belief or argument.
having faults or gaps.
cannot be trusted to work or tell truth.
based on error, factually incorrect.
entries.definitionCN: 基于错误、事实上不对的。

entries.definition: holding a wrong idea about something.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a ruler with a bend so slight that only a long line reveals it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一把尺子有一道极轻的弯，只有长线才显出它」的画面。

normal.en: Fallible shares a root with false and fail: all three are about coming off the true line.
normal.cn: fallible 与 false、fail 同根：三者都与偏离真线有关。

normal.en: Add in- and the word flips: infallible means cannot fall.
normal.cn: 加上 in- 词就翻转：infallible 意为「不会失足」。

normal.en: Think of a witness who is honest and still wrong.
normal.cn: 想象一个诚实却仍然记错的证人。

normal.en: Say FAL-uh-bl; the first syllable is the stumble itself.
normal.cn: 读成 FAL-uh-bl，第一个音节就是那一下踉跄。

normal.en: Link with default: both suggest a small built-in chance of failure.
normal.cn: 和 default 联系：两者都暗示内置的一点失败可能。

abstract.en: Admitting fallibility is the beginning of every reliable method.
abstract.cn: 承认易错，是一切可靠方法的开始。

abstract.en: The opposite of fallible is not wise; it is impossible.
abstract.cn: 易错的反面不是智慧，而是不可能。

abstract.en: Being wrong is not the same as being false; honest error still deserves respect.
abstract.cn: 出错不等于虚假；诚实的错误仍值得尊重。

examples.en: Any fallible reader can misread a single line.
examples.cn: 任何会犯错的读者都可能看错一行。

examples.en: The most careful method is still fallible at the edges.
examples.cn: 最细致的方法在边缘处仍会出错。

examples.en: He was fallible but honest, and that was enough.
examples.cn: 他会犯错，但诚实，这就够了。

dict_mnemonic.text: fall（跌、骗）+ ible（能……的）：能被绊倒的，就是「会出错的」。

root: 拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、使失足）→ fallibilis（可能被欺的）

sensesIntro.en: Fallible never means dishonest; it means able to come off the true line, and the senses differ in what may slip.
sensesIntro.cn: fallible 从不指不诚实；它指可能偏离真线，各义项的差别在于滑开的是什么。

core.en: ABLE TO COME OFF THE TRUE LINE

branches.en: The general human condition, without any hint of deceit.
branches.cn: 普遍的人类处境，不含欺骗之意。

branches.en: Memory and judgement that drift.
branches.cn: 会漂移的记忆与判断。

branches.en: Systems and proofs that fail at their limits.
branches.cn: 在极限处失效的系统与证明。

branches.en: Authorities that are respected but not worshipped.
branches.cn: 受尊重却不被崇拜的权威。

branches.en: Design that plans for the weakness instead of denying it.
branches.cn: 为弱点作准备而非否认它的设计。

intro.en: The fall family is about slipping: fallible can slip, infallible cannot, and fallacy is the slip itself.
intro.cn: fall 词族与滑倒有关：fallible 会滑，infallible 不会，fallacy 则是那一下滑。

latinIntro.en: Latin fallere means to deceive or trip; its family includes false, fail and fault, all forms of coming off the line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 意为欺骗或绊倒；其词族包括 false、fail 与 fault，都是偏离真线的形态。

items.exampleCN: 会犯错的法官仍在裁判。

items.example: Fallibility is part of the method.
items.exampleCN: 易错性是方法的一部分。

items.example: The argument rests on a fallacy.
items.exampleCN: 这个论证基于一个谬误。

items.example: The plan failed on day two.
The fault was in the seal.

definition_zh: 坚毅；刚毅；忍痛的力量
definition_en: strength of mind that lets a person endure pain or hardship calmly
core_image: 一个人拄着拐杖走过长长的雪地，每一步都很慢，却一步也没有停
scene: 手术后的第三周，他每天沿走廊走二十步，从不让人扶。The nurses admired his fortitude more than his recovery.
sceneCN: 这里 fortitude 指忍痛坚持的坚毅（第 1 个义项：在痛苦中保持的力量）；句意为护士们更佩服他的坚毅，而不是他的康复。

senses.title: Courage in pain
senses.definition: the strength to bear physical pain without giving way
senses.definitionCN: 承受身体痛苦而不垮掉的力量
senses.example: The nurses admired his fortitude more than his recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们更佩服他的坚毅，而不是他的康复。
senses.why: This sense is about holding still under pain, not about fighting it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项讲的是在痛苦下稳住，而不是与痛苦搏斗。

senses.title: Courage over years
senses.definition: the courage that lasts through long hardship rather than one crisis
senses.definitionCN: 穿过漫长困苦、而非一次危机的勇气
senses.example: She raised three children alone with unbroken fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 她以不曾中断的坚毅独自养大三个孩子。
senses.why: A single hard hour needs nerve; a decade needs fortitude.
senses.whyCN: 艰难的一小时需要胆量；十年需要坚毅。

senses.title: Moral strength
senses.definition: the strength to keep to one's principles under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下守住原则的力量
senses.example: He refused the bribe with quiet fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 他以沉静的刚毅拒绝了贿赂。
senses.why: Here the pain is not bodily but social: the cost is being disliked.
senses.whyCN: 这里的痛苦不是身体的，而是社会的：代价是被讨厌。

senses.title: Calm endurance
senses.definition: endurance without drama or complaint
senses.definitionCN: 不带戏剧性、也不抱怨的忍耐
senses.example: Her fortitude showed in what she never said.
senses.exampleCN: 她的坚忍体现在她从不说的那些话里。
senses.why: Endurance without complaint is the form strength takes when no one is watching.
senses.whyCN: 无人注视时，力量就表现为不抱怨的忍耐。

senses.title: Courage without display
senses.definition: strength that does not need to be seen to exist
senses.definitionCN: 无需被看见也存在的力量
senses.example: There was no speech, only fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 没有演说，只有坚毅。
senses.why: The word prefers the quiet form: it describes a state, not a performance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词偏爱安静的形式：它描述状态，而非表演。

senses.title: Fortitude in adversity
senses.definition: the quality that keeps a person upright when circumstances turn bad
senses.definitionCN: 境况转坏时使人不倒的品质
senses.example: The town met the flood with stubborn fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇以倔强的坚毅面对洪水。
senses.why: Bad circumstances are the test that turns a capacity into a habit.
senses.whyCN: 恶劣境况是把能力变成习惯的检验。

senses.title: Fortitude of belief
senses.definition: the strength to hold a faith or conviction against opposition
senses.definitionCN: 在反对中守住信仰或信念的力量
senses.example: The small congregation kept its fortitude through years of pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小教会在多年压力中保持坚贞。
senses.why: Faith under pressure is held by the same muscle that holds a body upright.
senses.whyCN: 压力下的信念，由撑住身体的同一块肌肉撑着。

senses.title: Physical stamina
senses.definition: the bodily strength to keep going when tired
senses.definitionCN: 疲倦时仍能继续的身体力量
senses.example: Long marches test fortitude more than courage.
senses.exampleCN: 长途行军考验的更多是耐久，而不是勇气。
senses.why: The word can lean toward the body, though its usual home is the mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以偏向身体，尽管它通常住在心智里。

intro.en: Fortitude comes from a Latin word for strength, and it is strength thought of as a thing a person can hold.
intro.cn: fortitude 来自一个意为「力量」的拉丁词，它是被当作人所能持有之物来想的力量。

items.en: English took the noun in the 12c. through French, first as a general word for strength.
items.cn: 英语在十二世纪经法语借入这个名词，最初泛指力量。

items.en: Fortitudo meant 'strength, courage', and was one of the four classical virtues.
items.cn: fortitudo 意为「力量、勇气」，是四种古典美德之一。

items.en: Fortis means strong, brave, and gives fortify and fortress.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮、勇敢，给出 fortify 与 fortress。

items.en: Medieval writers ranked fortitude as the virtue that holds the other virtues steady under attack.
items.cn: 中世纪作者把坚毅列为在攻击下稳住其它美德的美德。

items.en: Modern English narrowed it to quiet endurance, especially under pain or long hardship.
items.cn: 现代英语把它收窄为安静的忍耐，尤其在痛苦或长期困苦之下。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the strong root; the near-meaning group separates kinds of courage.
note.cn: 形近组共享「强」的词根；近义组区分不同种类的勇气。

entries.definition: to make stronger or better defended.
a defensive work or the act of strengthening.
a heavily defended stronghold.
showing quiet strength.
the ability to recover after difficulty.
the power to keep going through fatigue.
firm determination to do something.
enduring pain or loss without complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 不抱怨地忍受痛苦或损失。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of slow steps across a long field of snow.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「在长长的雪地里一步一步慢慢走」的画面。

normal.en: Fortitude contains fort: a fort stands because it is built to take hits.
normal.cn: fortitude 里有 fort（堡垒）：堡垒能立住，是因为它造来承受打击。

normal.en: Link with fortify and fortress: one makes strong, one is strong.
normal.cn: 和 fortify、fortress 联系：一个加固，一个坚固。

normal.en: Think of a long walk rather than a single leap.
normal.cn: 想象一段长走，而不是一次跳跃。

normal.en: Say FOR-ti-tood; the heavy first syllable sounds like a planted foot.
normal.cn: 读成 FOR-ti-tood，沉甸甸的第一个音节像一只踏稳的脚。

normal.en: Shop it with patience: patience waits, fortitude holds.
normal.cn: 和 patience 一起记：patience 是等，fortitude 是撑住。

abstract.en: Courage meets a moment; fortitude meets a season.
abstract.cn: 勇气面对一个时刻，坚毅面对一个季节。

abstract.en: The strongest thing in a room is often the person saying nothing.
abstract.cn: 屋里最强的，常常是一言不发的那个人。

abstract.en: Strength held quietly does not need an audience to be real.
abstract.cn: 安静持有的力量，不需要观众才算真实。

examples.en: The nurses admired his fortitude more than his recovery.
examples.cn: 护士们更佩服他的坚毅，而不是他的康复。

examples.en: She raised three children alone with unbroken fortitude.
examples.cn: 她以不曾中断的坚毅独自养大三个孩子。

examples.en: He refused the bribe with quiet fortitude.
examples.cn: 他以沉静的刚毅拒绝了贿赂。

dict_mnemonic.text: fort（强）+ itude（名词）：一直强着的状态，就是「坚毅」。

root: 拉丁语 fortis（强、勇）→ fortitudo（力量、勇气）

sensesIntro.en: Fortitude is strength that holds rather than strikes; the senses differ in what is being held against, pain, time, pressure or fatigue.
sensesIntro.cn: fortitude 是「撑住」而非「出击」的力量；各义项的差别在于所抵抗的是痛苦、时间、压力，还是疲惫。

branches.en: Pain and its quiet bearing.
branches.cn: 痛苦与对其安静的承受。

branches.en: Long hardship and bad circumstances.
branches.cn: 长期困苦与恶劣境况。

branches.en: Principles and faith held under pressure.
branches.cn: 压力下守住的准则与信念。

branches.en: The unshown form: strength without performance.
branches.cn: 不展示的形态：没有表演的力量。

branches.en: The bodily version, stamina under fatigue.
branches.cn: 身体版本：疲惫中的耐久。

intro.en: The fort family is about making and being strong: fortify strengthens, fortress defends, fortitude endures.
intro.cn: fort 词族与「使强」和「强」有关：fortify 加固，fortress 防御，fortitude 忍耐。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis is the adjective strong; fortitudo turns it into a quality a person can possess.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 是形容词「强」；fortitudo 把它变成一种人可以拥有的品质。

items.meaning: a making strong, or the work built

items.example: The fortress held for a month.
The force of the wave broke the door.

definition_zh: 徒劳；无用；无意义
definition_en: the quality of being useless or of having no effect
core_image: 一个人反复把水倒进一只底部有洞的桶，水线始终不升
scene: 第八次修改之后，评审仍然给出同样的意见。The futility of the process was plain to everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 futility 指过程的徒劳（第 1 个义项：努力没有效果）；句意为这个流程的徒劳人人可见。

senses.title: Pointlessness of effort
senses.definition: the state of working hard with no possible result
senses.definitionCN: 努力却不可能有结果的状态
senses.example: The futility of the process was plain to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流程的徒劳人人可见。
senses.why: Futility measures effort against outcome; when the second cannot come, the first empties.
senses.whyCN: 徒劳用结果衡量努力；当结果不可能来，努力就空了。

senses.title: A futile act
senses.definition: a single action that cannot change anything
senses.definitionCN: 无法改变任何事的单个行为
senses.example: Shouting at the locked door was a futility he kept repeating.
senses.exampleCN: 对着锁住的门喊，是他一再重复的无用举动。
senses.why: One act can fail alone without proving that every act must fail.
senses.whyCN: 单个行为的失败，并不证明所有行为都会失败。

senses.title: Futility of war
senses.definition: the sense that a conflict destroys more than it can settle
senses.definitionCN: 冲突摧毁的多于它能解决的那种感受
senses.example: The poem is famous for its quiet statement of war's futility.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗以对战争无意义的平静陈述而闻名。
senses.why: The word can turn political: it questions whether the cost has any matching result.
senses.whyCN: 这个词会转为政治判断：它质疑代价是否有相称的结果。

senses.title: Futility of words
senses.definition: the feeling that speaking cannot reach the person addressed
senses.definitionCN: 觉得说话无法抵达对方的那种感受
senses.example: After the third apology she felt the futility of words.
senses.exampleCN: 第三次道歉之后，她感到了言语的无力。
senses.why: When speech cannot reach, silence is not the only other option; timing may be.
senses.whyCN: 当言语抵达不了，沉默不是唯一的另一选项，时机也许是。

senses.title: A sense of futility
senses.definition: a mood in which all action seems pointless
senses.definitionCN: 觉得一切行动都无意义的心境
senses.example: A vague sense of futility settled over the office.
senses.exampleCN: 一种模糊的徒劳感笼住了办公室。
senses.why: This is the emotional form: not a judgement about one act but a weather over everything.
senses.whyCN: 这是情感形态：不是对某个行为的判断，而是笼罩一切的气候。

senses.title: Futility of resistance
senses.definition: the recognition that opposition cannot succeed
senses.definitionCN: 认识到反抗不可能成功
senses.example: They fought on despite the futility of resistance.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管抵抗已无望，他们仍继续战斗。
senses.why: Recognising that resistance cannot win is different from agreeing with the power that won.
senses.whyCN: 承认抵抗无法获胜，与认同获胜的权力是两回事。

senses.title: Futility in art
senses.definition: a theme in art about effort that consumes itself
senses.definitionCN: 艺术中关于自我消耗的努力的主题
senses.example: The painter made futility beautiful without making it false.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家让徒劳变得美，却没有让它变成假。
senses.why: Art can hold a useless thing long enough for us to see why it was done.
senses.whyCN: 艺术能把无用之物举得够久，让我们看清它为何被做。

senses.title: Futility admitted
senses.definition: the honest admission that a plan has no future
senses.definitionCN: 诚实承认某个计划没有未来
senses.example: Admitting futility was the first useful step.
senses.exampleCN: 承认徒劳是第一个有用的步骤。
senses.why: The word can be a clearing, not only a defeat: what is futile can be released.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以是一次清理，而不只是失败：徒劳之物可以被放下。

intro.en: Futility comes from a Latin adjective for a leaky vessel, something that cannot hold what is poured in.
intro.cn: futility 来自一个意为「漏的器皿」的拉丁形容词，装不住倒进去的东西。

items.en: English took the noun in the 17c., at first for speech that could not persuade.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，最初指无法说服人的言辞。

items.en: Futilis meant 'that easily pours out, leaky', and so 'vain, worthless'.
items.cn: futilis 意为「容易漏出的、漏的」，因此也指「空的、无价值的」。

items.en: Fundere 'to pour' is the base, and it also gives fuse and profuse.
items.cn: fundere「倒」是词基，也给出 fuse 与 profuse。

items.en: Futilitas meant 'worthlessness, vanity', the abstract quality of the leaky thing.
items.cn: futilitas 意为「无价值、虚妄」，即漏器之物抽象出来的性质。

items.en: Modern English applies it to efforts, wars, speeches and whole lives.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于努力、战争、演说乃至整个人生。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the futile stem; the near-meaning group names kinds of pointlessness.
note.cn: 形近组保留 futile 词干；近义组列出无意义的不同种类。

entries.definition: producing no useful result.
in a way that cannot succeed.
the quality of being useless.
able to produce abundantly.
the quality of having no aim or use.
entries.definitionCN: 没有目标或用途的性质。

entries.definition: the state of being unable to serve a purpose.
futility or emptiness of effort or ambition.
a complete and humiliating failure.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of water poured into a bucket with a hole in the bottom.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「水倒进一只底部有洞的桶」的画面。

normal.en: Futility shares a root with fuse: both come from pouring, and what pours out cannot be kept.
normal.cn: futility 与 fuse 同根：都出自「倒」，倒出去的东西留不住。

normal.en: Futile and fertile differ by two letters and by everything that can grow.
normal.cn: futile 与 fertile 只差两个字母，却隔着一整个能生长与不能生长的世界。

normal.en: Think of a bucket with a hole, held over dry ground.
normal.cn: 想象一只带洞的桶，举在干地上。

normal.en: Say fyoo-TIL-uh-tee; the light first syllable sounds like something draining away.
normal.cn: 读成 fyoo-TIL-uh-tee，轻飘的第一个音节像有东西漏走。

normal.en: Pair it with effort: futility is effort with no door to go through.
normal.cn: 和 effort 配对：徒劳是没有门可穿的努力。

abstract.en: A leaky vessel is not evil; it simply cannot be filled.
abstract.cn: 漏器不是恶的；它只是装不满。

abstract.en: Knowing something is futile can free the energy that was wasted on it.
abstract.cn: 知道某事徒劳，可以释放曾被浪费在它上面的能量。

abstract.en: The word describes the container, not the person who pours.
abstract.cn: 这个词描述的是容器，而不是倒水的人。

examples.en: The futility of the process was plain to everyone.
examples.cn: 这个流程的徒劳人人可见。

examples.en: After the third apology she felt the futility of words.
examples.cn: 第三次道歉之后，她感到了言语的无力。

examples.en: Admitting futility was the first useful step.
examples.cn: 承认徒劳是第一个有用的步骤。

dict_mnemonic.text: fut（倒、漏）+ ility（名词）：像漏桶装水，倒多少都留不住，就是「徒劳」。

root: 拉丁语 futilis（漏的、装不住的）→ futilitas（无价值）

sensesIntro.en: Futility is always a relation between effort and vessel; the senses differ in what is being poured into what.
sensesIntro.cn: futility 始终是努力与容器之间的关系；各义项的差别在于倒进去的是什么，容器又是什么。

core.en: A LEAKY VESSEL CANNOT BE FILLED

branches.en: Effort and single acts that cannot produce a result.
branches.cn: 无法产生结果的努力与单个行为。

branches.en: Political and military versions: wars and resistance.
branches.cn: 政治与军事版本：战争与抵抗。

branches.en: Speech that cannot reach, and the mood it leaves.
branches.cn: 无法抵达的言语，以及它留下的心境。

branches.en: Art that makes the theme visible without endorsing it.
branches.cn: 让主题可见却并不赞成的艺术。

branches.en: The release that comes with honest admission.
branches.cn: 诚实承认后带来的放下。

intro.en: The fut family is about pouring and leaking: futile cannot hold, and the noun names that inability.
intro.cn: fut 词族与倒、漏有关：futile 装不住，名词则命名这种装不住。

latinIntro.en: Latin fundere means to pour; futilis describes the vessel that lets everything run out again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fundere 意为倒；futilis 描述那只让一切又流走的容器。

items.meaning: the quality of being in vain
items.example: The futileness of the plan showed early.
items.exampleCN: 计划的徒劳很早就显出。
标签把所有人弄糊涂了。

definition_zh: 全部范围；全音域；色域
definition_en: the complete range of something, from one end to the other
core_image: 一整排色卡从最浅的白排到最深的黑，手指从一端滑到另一端
scene: 他的演讲从玩笑一路走到悼词，中间没有一处停顿。The speech ran the gamut from laughter to grief.
sceneCN: 这里 gamut 指完整的情感范围（第 3 个义项：情感的幅度）；句意为演讲从笑声一路走到悲伤。

senses.title: Full range
senses.definition: the whole extent of something, with nothing left out
senses.definitionCN: 某物的全部幅度，无所遗漏
senses.example: The report covers the gamut of local concerns.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告覆盖了当地关切的全范围。
senses.why: The word insists on completeness: not many examples, but the whole set from edge to edge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词坚持完整性：不是许多例子，而是从一端到另一端的整副集合。

senses.title: Range of colours
senses.definition: the full set of colours a system can show or a palette contains
senses.definitionCN: 系统能显示或调色板所含的全部色彩
senses.example: The screen reproduces a wide gamut of colours.
senses.exampleCN: 这块屏幕再现了很宽的色域。
senses.why: This is the sense most alive in technology: gamut is a measurable span, not a mood.
senses.whyCN: 这是技术在用的义项：色域是可测量的跨度，不是情绪。

senses.title: Range of emotions
senses.definition: the whole stretch of feeling from one extreme to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一端极端到另一端极端的全部感受
senses.example: The speech ran the gamut from laughter to grief.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲从笑声一路走到悲伤。
senses.why: Feelings are described as a scale because they can be arranged by intensity.
senses.whyCN: 情感被描述成刻度，因为它们可以按强度排列。

senses.title: Range of notes
senses.definition: the notes a voice or instrument can produce, low to high
senses.definitionCN: 嗓音或乐器能发出的由低到高的音
senses.example: Her voice covers the gamut of the alto line.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音覆盖了中音声部的全部音域。
senses.why: This is the word's origin: a scale named by its lowest note.
senses.whyCN: 这是词的起源：以最低音命名的一套音阶。

senses.title: Range of options
senses.definition: all the choices available between two limits
senses.definitionCN: 两个界限之间所有可选项
senses.example: The proposal offers the gamut of options, from delay to cancellation.
senses.exampleCN: 提案给出了从延期到取消的全部选项。
senses.why: A range is useful only when both ends are really available.
senses.whyCN: 只有当两端都真的可选，范围才有用。

senses.title: Whole gamut of experience
senses.definition: every kind of experience a life or a field contains
senses.definitionCN: 一种生活或领域所含的每一种经验
senses.example: A long marriage runs the gamut of weather.
senses.exampleCN: 一段长久的婚姻会经历各种天气。
senses.why: A life is measured less by its peaks than by how much of the span it actually visits.
senses.whyCN: 衡量一生，与其看高峰，不如看它真正走过多少跨度。

senses.title: Gamut of expression
senses.definition: the full spread of ways a medium can express something
senses.definitionCN: 一种媒介表达某物的全部手法
senses.example: Film has a gamut of expression that prose must borrow.
senses.exampleCN: 电影有整套表达幅度，散文只能借用。
senses.why: A medium reach is defined by the effects it can produce, not by the ones it prefers.
senses.whyCN: 媒介的幅度由它能产生的效果界定，而不是由它偏爱的效果界定。

senses.title: Running the gamut
senses.definition: the act of moving through every point of a range in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序穿过一个范围的每一点
senses.example: The audition made each singer run the gamut of keys.
senses.exampleCN: 试唱让每位歌手都过了一遍全部调性。
senses.why: The phrase turns the noun into an action: a range is something one can travel.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把名词变成动作：范围是可以走过的。

intro.en: Gamut began as the name of a musical scale, made from the Greek letter gamma plus the note ut.
intro.cn: gamut 最初是一套音阶的名字，由希腊字母 gamma 加上音名 ut 构成。

items.en: Guido of Arezzo named the scale gamma ut, running from the lowest note upward.
items.cn: 阿雷佐的圭多把这套音阶命名为 gamma ut，从最低音向上排列。

items.en: The two words fused into gamut, and English borrowed it through French.
items.cn: 两个词合成 gamut，英语再经法语借入。

items.en: For centuries gamut meant the whole recognized range of notes.
items.cn: 数百年间，gamut 指全部被承认的音域。

items.en: By the 17c. the word extended to any complete range, colours and feelings included.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词扩展到任何完整范围，包括色彩与情感。

items.en: Modern English keeps the phrase run the gamut and the technical sense in printing.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 run the gamut 这一短语，以及印刷中的技术义。

note.en: The look-alike group sounds like gamut but is unrelated; the near-meaning group names spans and sets.
note.cn: 形近组听起来像 gamut，却并无关系；近义组列出跨度与集合。

entries.definition: the third Greek letter, a source of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊第三个字母，词的来源之一。

entries.definition: an opening move or a calculated stratagem.
entries.definitionCN: 开局着法或计算过的策略。

entries.definition: a reproductive cell that fuses with another.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一个融合的生殖细胞。

entries.definition: talking too much about small things.
the limits within which something varies.
a full band of colours or positions.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的一段色彩或立场。

entries.definition: the full scope or reach of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的全部范围或触及。

entries.definition: the full set of works or skills one commands.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人掌握的全部作品或技能。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a colour chart, one hand sliding from white to black.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一张色卡，一只手从白滑到黑」的画面。

normal.en: Gamut is gamma plus ut, the lowest note of an old scale.
normal.cn: gamut 是 gamma 加 ut，旧音阶的最低音。

normal.en: Think of a full keyboard, every key pressed once.
normal.cn: 想象一整排琴键，每个键都被按过一次。

normal.en: The phrase is run the gamut, not walk the gamut.
normal.cn: 搭配是 run the gamut，不是 walk the gamut。

normal.en: Say GAM-ut; the flat a sounds like a scale being read off.
normal.cn: 读成 GAM-ut，平直的 a 音像在念一排刻度。

normal.en: Link with range and spectrum: both are borrowed words for a complete span.
normal.cn: 和 range、spectrum 联系：两者都是表示完整跨度的借词。

abstract.en: A range is complete only when both ends are included.
abstract.cn: 只有两端都被包含，范围才算完整。

abstract.en: The whole gamut is not the same as many examples.
abstract.cn: 全部范围不等于许多例子。

abstract.en: What can be measured can be travelled; that is why the phrase uses run.
abstract.cn: 可测量的东西可以被走遍；所以这个短语用 run。

examples.en: The speech ran the gamut from laughter to grief.
examples.cn: 演讲从笑声一路走到悲伤。

examples.en: The report covers the gamut of local concerns.
examples.cn: 这份报告覆盖了当地关切的全范围。

examples.en: The screen reproduces a wide gamut of colours.
examples.cn: 这块屏幕再现了很宽的色域。

dict_mnemonic.text: gamma（希腊字母）+ ut（最低音）：从最低音到最高音的一整排，就是「全部范围」。

root: 中世纪音乐术语 gamma ut（音阶名），由希腊字母 gamma 与音名 ut 合成

sensesIntro.en: Gamut always means the whole span with both ends included; the senses differ in what is arranged along that span.
sensesIntro.cn: gamut 始终指包含两端的完整跨度；各义项的差别在于沿这跨度排列的是什么。

core.en: THE WHOLE SPAN, BOTH ENDS INCLUDED

branches.en: The original sense: notes from the lowest upward.
branches.cn: 本义：从最低音向上的音。

branches.en: Colours as a measurable span.
branches.cn: 作为可测量跨度的色彩。

branches.en: Feeling and experience arranged by intensity.
branches.cn: 按强度排列的情感与经验。

branches.en: Options and expressive means, edge to edge.
branches.cn: 从一端到另一端的选项与表达手段。

branches.en: The general sense and the act of travelling it.
branches.cn: 一般意义，以及走遍它的动作。

intro.en: The gamut family is small, but it reaches into music, printing and ordinary speech about ranges.
intro.cn: gamut 词族很小，却伸进音乐、印刷，以及日常谈论范围的言语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here: the word is a medieval music term, and its parts are a Greek letter and a sung syllable.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根：这个词是中世纪音乐术语，部件是一个希腊字母与一个唱名音节。

items.meaning: the named scale, hence a full range
items.meaningCN: 被命名的音阶，引申为完整范围
items.example: The gamut of colours filled the wall.
items.exampleCN: 整面墙铺满了全套色彩。

items.meaning: a ladder of notes or values
an image of a full band
items.example: The spectrum ran from red to violet.

items.meaning: a row or line of limits
items.example: The range of prices was wide.
The pianist has a large repertoire.

latinEntries.meaning: the old name of the note do
an appearance, a band of colour

definition_zh: 反传统者；抨击偶像者；破坏圣像者
definition_en: a person who attacks established beliefs, images or customs
core_image: 一个人站在挂满画像的墙前，伸手把最中央那幅取下来，放到地上
scene: 所有人都在称赞那套流程，只有他站起来问了一句最基础的问题。The iconoclast was invited back every year.
sceneCN: 这里 iconoclast 指挑战既有信条的人（第 2 个义项：抨击信条者）；句意为这位反传统者每年都被请回来。

pos.zh: 反传统者；抨击偶像者；破坏圣像者

collocations.zh: 无所畏惧的偶像破坏者

senses.title: Breaker of images
senses.definition: a person who destroys religious images as idolatrous
senses.definitionCN: 以偶像崇拜为由毁坏宗教圣像的人
senses.example: In the eighth century the iconoclast removed every painted face from the church.
senses.exampleCN: 八世纪时，破坏圣像者把教堂里每一张绘出的面容都取了下来。
senses.why: This is the historical sense: the word was born in a war over whether images may be worshipped.
senses.whyCN: 这是历史义：这个词诞生于一场关于图像能否被崇拜的战争。

senses.title: Attacker of beliefs
senses.definition: a person who challenges accepted doctrines held as sacred
senses.definitionCN: 挑战被视为神圣的既定信条的人
senses.example: The iconoclast was invited back every year.
senses.exampleCN: 这位反传统者每年都被请回来。
senses.why: Once images became ideas, breaking them became argument rather than demolition.
senses.whyCN: 当图像变成观念，破坏它就从拆毁变成了论证。

senses.title: Challenger of tradition
senses.definition: someone who questions customs simply because they are old
senses.definitionCN: 仅仅因为习俗古老就加以质疑的人
senses.example: Every tradition needs at least one iconoclast to stay honest.
senses.exampleCN: 每种传统都至少需要一个反传统者来保持诚实。
senses.why: Age alone is not an argument, and the challenger is right to say so once.
senses.whyCN: 年岁本身不是论据，挑战者说一次这话是对的。

senses.title: Reformer in an institution
senses.definition: a member who attacks the habits of their own organisation
senses.definitionCN: 攻击自己组织习惯的成员
senses.example: As an iconoclast inside the bank, she abolished three rituals.
senses.exampleCN: 作为银行里的破规者，她废掉了三项仪式。
senses.why: Reform from inside is slower and more effective, because the critic knows which wall bears weight.
senses.whyCN: 内部改革更慢也更有效，因为批评者知道哪堵墙承重。

senses.title: Critic of heroes
senses.definition: a person who refuses to treat admired figures as flawless
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝把受敬仰者当作无瑕之人的人
senses.example: The biography was written by an iconoclast who loved its subject.
senses.exampleCN: 这本传记出自一位爱传主的反偶像者。
senses.why: A hero treated as flawless stops being a model and becomes a fence.
senses.whyCN: 被当作无瑕的英雄不再是榜样，而成了一道围栏。

senses.title: Artistic rule-breaker
senses.definition: an artist who abandons the accepted forms of the day
senses.definitionCN: 抛弃当时通行形式的艺术家
senses.example: The iconoclast hung the painting upside down and changed the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这位破规者把画倒挂，改变了整个房间。
senses.why: Forms are tools; when a tool hides the thing it should show, breaking it is reasonable.
senses.whyCN: 形式是工具；当工具遮住了它该显示的东西，打破它就是合理的。

senses.title: The needed voice
senses.definition: the dissent that keeps a group from repeating its mistakes
senses.definitionCN: 使团体不再重复错误的异议
senses.example: They kept one iconoclast on every committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在每个委员会里都留一位异声。
senses.why: A group without dissent cannot tell the difference between agreement and silence.
senses.whyCN: 没有异议的团体分不清同意与沉默。

senses.title: Iconoclasm as habit
senses.definition: a standing habit of attacking whatever is respected
senses.definitionCN: 攻击一切受敬之物的固定习气
senses.example: His iconoclasm had become a reflex, not a position.
senses.exampleCN: 他的反偶像已成条件反射，而不是立场。
senses.why: The same impulse that clears dead forms can also break what is still alive.
senses.whyCN: 清除死形式的同一冲动，也会打破仍然活着的东西。

intro.en: Iconoclast joins two Greek words, image and breaker, and its history begins in a church dispute over pictures.
intro.cn: iconoclast 把两个希腊词「图像」与「破坏者」接在一起，历史始于教会关于图像的争论。

items.en: Eikon meant 'image, likeness', especially a painted holy figure.
items.cn: eikon 意为「图像、相似物」，尤指绘制的圣像。

items.en: Klastes meant 'breaker', from klan 'to break', the source of clastic.
items.cn: klastes 意为「破坏者」，出自 klan「打破」，是 clastic 的来源。

items.en: Iconoclasts destroyed images in the 8c. on the grounds that worship of them was idolatry.
items.cn: 八世纪的破坏圣像者以崇拜图像属偶像崇拜为由毁坏图像。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the 16c., first for the historical party.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个词，最初指那个历史派别。

items.en: By the 19c. any attacker of accepted beliefs could be called an iconoclast.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，任何攻击既定信念的人都能被称为 iconoclast。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the image-breaking pieces; the near-meaning group names kinds of challengers.
note.cn: 形近组共享「破像」的部件；近义组列出不同种类的挑战者。

entries.definition: the attacking of images or beliefs.
breaking accepted images or rules.
entries.definitionCN: 打破既定形象或规则的。

entries.definition: the study or system of images.
a venerated image or symbol.
a person who fights against established power.
one who disagrees with an official view.
a person who wants deep change of the system.
entries.definitionCN: 主张制度深层改变的人。

entries.definition: one who holds a belief condemned as false.
entries.definitionCN: 持被斥为虚假信念的人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a painting being taken down from the centre of the wall.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一幅画被人从墙的正中央取下来」的画面。

normal.en: Iconoclast = icon + clast: an image breaker, exactly as spelled.
normal.cn: iconoclast = icon + clast：破坏图像的人，正是字面意思。

normal.en: Clast also hides in clastic rock: broken pieces pressed together.
normal.cn: clast 也藏在 clastic rock（碎屑岩）里：碎块被压在一起。

normal.en: Think of someone asking the question everyone has agreed not to ask.
normal.cn: 想象有人问出大家都默契地不问的那个问题。

normal.en: Say eye-KON-uh-klast; the eye at the start sounds like an eye looking at an image.
normal.cn: 读成 eye-KON-uh-klast，开头的 eye 像一只眼睛在看图像。

normal.en: Link with icon: every iconoclast needs an icon first.
normal.cn: 和 icon 联系：每个反偶像者都得先有一个偶像。

abstract.en: Breaking an image is easy; replacing the need for it is the real work.
abstract.cn: 打破图像容易；替代对它的需要才是真正的工作。

abstract.en: A healthy tradition keeps one person who is allowed to be rude to it.
abstract.cn: 健康的传统会留一个被允许对它无礼的人。

abstract.en: The habit of attack can clear dead wood or cut living branches.
abstract.cn: 攻击的习气既能清掉枯枝，也能砍断活枝。

examples.en: The iconoclast was invited back every year.
examples.cn: 这位反传统者每年都被请回来。

examples.en: Every tradition needs at least one iconoclast to stay honest.
examples.cn: 每种传统都至少需要一个反传统者来保持诚实。

examples.en: As an iconoclast inside the bank, she abolished three rituals.
examples.cn: 作为银行里的破规者，她废掉了三项仪式。

dict_mnemonic.text: icon（圣像）+ clast（打破的人）：打破圣像的人，就是「反传统者」。

root: 希腊语 eikon（图像）+ klastes（破坏者）

sensesIntro.en: An iconoclast breaks something treated as untouchable; the senses differ in whether the target is an image, a doctrine, a custom or a hero.
sensesIntro.cn: iconoclast 打碎被当作不可触碰之物；各义项的差别在于对象是图像、教义、习俗，还是英雄。

core.en: BREAKING WHAT IS TREATED AS UNTOUCHABLE

branches.en: The historical breaking of religious images.
branches.cn: 历史上对宗教图像的破坏。

branches.en: Doctrines and customs attacked by argument.
branches.cn: 以论证攻击的教义与习俗。

branches.en: The internal reformer and the useful dissenting voice.
branches.cn: 内部改革者与有用的异声。

branches.en: Heroes questioned and forms abandoned.
branches.cn: 被质疑的英雄与被抛弃的形式。

branches.en: The habit of attack, which can outlive its purpose.
branches.cn: 攻击的习气，可能活得比它的目的更久。

intro.en: The icon family is about images and their authority: an icon is honoured, iconography studies them, iconoclasm breaks them.
intro.cn: icon 词族与图像及其权威有关：icon 受敬奉，iconography 研究它们，iconoclasm 打破它们。

latinIntro.en: Greek eikon and klastes are the two halves; the first gives the target, the second the act, and the compound is a small programme.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 eikon 与 klastes 是两半：前者给对象，后者给动作，这个复合词本身就是一个小纲领。

items.exampleCN: 破坏圣像之风扫过该省。
他那篇破规文章传得很快。

items.example: The icon hung above the door.

items.meaning: the writing or study of images
items.example: The iconography of the period is rich.
items.exampleCN: 这一时期的图像体系很丰富。
每一块碎屑都有一段故事。

items.meaning: the study of images and symbols
items.example: Iconology reads the room, not the frame.
items.exampleCN: 图像学读的是房间，而不是画框。

definition_zh: 即兴的；即席的；临时的
definition_en: done or said without preparation, on the spur of the moment
core_image: 一个人被推上台，手里没有稿子，只把口袋里的笔往桌上一放就开口
scene: 主持人临时请他讲两句，他站起来就说了五分钟。The impromptu toast turned out better than the planned one.
sceneCN: 这里 impromptu 指即席的（第 1 个义项：未经准备的发言）；句意为这段即兴祝酒比准备好的那段更好。

senses.title: Speech without preparation
senses.definition: words spoken to an audience without notes or rehearsal
senses.definitionCN: 没有稿子或排练就对听众说的话
senses.example: The impromptu toast turned out better than the planned one.
senses.exampleCN: 这段即兴祝酒比准备好的那段更好。
senses.why: The word puts readiness where preparation usually sits, and the result can surprise even the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「有准备」的位置换成「随时待命」，结果连说话者自己都可能意外。

senses.title: Performance on the spot
senses.definition: music or acting made up as it is performed
senses.definitionCN: 边演边编的音乐或表演
senses.example: The pianist gave an impromptu encore that nobody had rehearsed.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家加演了一段没人排练过的即兴曲。
senses.why: Improvisation works because the performer trusts trained reflexes more than a plan.
senses.whyCN: 即兴之所以可行，是因为表演者更信任训练出来的反射，而不是计划。

senses.title: An improvised meal
senses.definition: a meal assembled from whatever happens to be at hand
senses.definitionCN: 用手边现成的东西拼成的一餐
senses.example: They made an impromptu dinner from bread, cheese and one tomato.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用面包、奶酪和一个番茄凑成了晚餐。
senses.why: This sense extends the word from speech to things, as long as the thing is made on the spot.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把词从言语扩展到物品，只要东西是当场做成的。

senses.title: An unrehearsed remark
senses.definition: a comment that escapes before it has been shaped
senses.definitionCN: 还没被修饰就说出口的评论
senses.example: His impromptu remark was the most honest thing said all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句脱口而出的话是整晚最诚实的一句。
senses.why: What is unpolished is not always worse; polish can hide the actual thought.
senses.whyCN: 未经打磨的未必更差；打磨有时会遮住真正的想法。

senses.title: An ad hoc arrangement
senses.definition: a plan put together quickly to meet an immediate need
senses.definitionCN: 为应付眼前需要而快速拼成的安排
senses.example: The impromptu schedule worked for one week and then collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个临时日程撑了一周就崩了。
senses.why: Quick plans buy time; the question is whether the time is used to build something sturdier.
senses.whyCN: 快速的安排买来时间；问题在于这时间是否被用来造更牢的东西。

senses.title: An impromptu gathering
senses.definition: a meeting of people arranged with almost no notice
senses.definitionCN: 几乎没提前通知就聚起来的一群人
senses.example: The impromptu gathering in the hallway lasted until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 走廊里的临时聚会一直延续到午夜。
senses.why: Some of the best gatherings happen because nobody had time to plan them badly.
senses.whyCN: 有些最好的聚会之所以发生，是因为没人有时间把它计划坏。

senses.title: An improvised solution
senses.definition: a fix invented in the moment with limited materials
senses.definitionCN: 在当下用有限材料想出的解决办法
senses.example: The impromptu repair held the bridge for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 这个临场修补让桥撑了两天。
senses.why: A fix made from what is at hand reveals how much of engineering is invention.
senses.whyCN: 用手边之物做成的修补，显出工程里有多少是临场发明。

senses.title: The charm of the unprepared
senses.definition: the liveliness that comes from having no script to follow
senses.definitionCN: 没有脚本可循而带来的生气
senses.example: What the audience loved was the impromptu quality, not the content.
senses.exampleCN: 观众喜欢的是那种即兴劲儿，而不是内容。
senses.why: The word can praise as easily as it can excuse; context decides which.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既能称赞，也能当借口；语境决定是哪一种。

intro.en: Impromptu comes from Latin for in readiness, meaning a thing available at the very moment it is needed.
intro.cn: impromptu 来自拉丁语「处于准备状态」，指在需要的那一刻正好可用的东西。

items.en: In promptu meant 'in readiness, at hand', said of troops and supplies.
items.cn: in promptu 意为「在准备中、在手边」，用于军队与补给。

items.en: Promptus meant 'brought out, ready', the participle behind prompt.
items.cn: promptus 意为「被取出、准备好的」，是 prompt 的源头。

items.en: French borrowed the phrase and used it for a short piece made on the spot.
items.cn: 法语借入这个短语，用来指当场写成的短作品。

items.en: English took it in the 17c. as both adjective and noun, including a kind of piano piece.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入，既作形容词也作名词，包括一种钢琴曲。

items.en: Modern English applies it to speeches, meals, visits and anything made without preparation.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于发言、餐食、造访，以及任何未经准备而做成的事。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the prompt root; the near-meaning group names kinds of unprepared action.
note.cn: 形近组共享 prompt 词根；近义组列出未准备行为的不同种类。

entries.definition: quick and without delay.
at once, without waiting.
the quality of being quick.
readiness and speed of action.
arising from one's own impulse, not outside pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 出于自身冲动而非外部压力的。

entries.definition: not prepared or practised beforehand.
arranged for one particular purpose only.
entries.definitionCN: 仅为某一特定目的而安排的。

entries.definition: said without preparation or care.
entries.definitionCN: 未经准备或不经心说出的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a speaker standing up with empty hands and a full mind.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一个人两手空空、脑子满满地站起来」的画面。

normal.en: Impromptu hides prompt: readiness is the whole trick.
normal.cn: impromptu 里藏着 prompt：有准备状态就是全部诀窍。

normal.en: The word has no -ed and no -ly; it works as adjective, adverb and noun alike.
normal.cn: 这个词没有 -ed 也没有 -ly；它可作形容词、副词与名词。

normal.en: Think of a jazz pianist who never looks at the sheet.
normal.cn: 想象一位从不看谱的爵士钢琴家。

normal.en: Say im-PROMP-too; the stressed syllable is the moment of deciding.
normal.cn: 读成 im-PROMP-too，重读音节就是决定的那一瞬。

normal.en: Link with prompt: something prompt is ready, and impromptu is ready without prior work.
normal.cn: 和 prompt 联系：prompt 是准备好的，impromptu 是没提前准备却随时可用。

abstract.en: Preparation and improvisation are not opposites; training is what makes improvisation possible.
abstract.cn: 准备与即兴并不相反；训练才让即兴成为可能。

abstract.en: What is made on the spot carries the risk and the life of that spot.
abstract.cn: 当场做成的东西，带着那个现场的风险与生气。

abstract.en: A good improviser has practised enough to forget the practice.
abstract.cn: 好的即兴者练得足够多，才能忘掉练习。

examples.en: The impromptu toast turned out better than the planned one.
examples.cn: 这段即兴祝酒比准备好的那段更好。

examples.en: The pianist gave an impromptu encore that nobody had rehearsed.
examples.cn: 钢琴家加演了一段没人排练过的即兴曲。

examples.en: They made an impromptu dinner from bread, cheese and one tomato.
examples.cn: 他们用面包、奶酪和一个番茄凑成了晚餐。

dict_mnemonic.text: im（在）+ prompt（准备好的）+ u：处在随时可用的状态，就是「即兴」。

root: 拉丁语 in promptu（在手边、已备好），源自 promptus（准备好的）

sensesIntro.en: Impromptu always means made at the moment of use; the senses differ only in what is made, words, music, meals or gatherings.
sensesIntro.cn: impromptu 始终指在使用那一刻做成；各义项的差别只在做成了什么，言语、音乐、餐食还是聚会。

core.en: MADE AT THE MOMENT OF USE

branches.en: Words that come out already formed.
branches.cn: 一出口就已成形的话。

branches.en: Music and performance invented while played.
branches.cn: 边演边编的音乐与表演。

branches.en: Meals, gatherings and fixes assembled from what is at hand.
branches.cn: 用手边之物拼成的餐食、聚会与修补。

branches.en: Plans made quickly for immediate needs.
branches.cn: 为眼前需要快速作出的安排。

branches.en: The liveliness that comes from having no script.
branches.cn: 没有脚本带来的生气。

intro.en: The prompt family is about readiness: prompt is ready, promptly is at once, and impromptu is ready without preparation.
intro.cn: prompt 词族与准备状态有关：prompt 是准备好的，promptly 是立刻，impromptu 是没准备也随时可用。

latinIntro.en: Latin promptus means brought out and ready; the phrase in promptu places that readiness at hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 promptus 意为被取出、已备好；短语 in promptu 把这种准备放在手边。

items.exampleCN: 她迅速的回答让我们意外。

items.example: The promptness of the staff helped.

items.meaning: the copy used to cue a play
items.example: The prompt book was full of notes.

definition_zh: 反复灌输；谆谆教诲；使养成
definition_en: to fix an idea or habit in someone's mind by constant repetition
core_image: 一个人一次又一次把同一句话写在同一块湿泥上，直到字迹再也抹不掉
scene: 祖父每晚讲同一个故事，讲到最后孩子自己会背了。Years of inculcating caution had made her careful without thinking.
sceneCN: 这里 inculcate 指反复灌输（第 1 个义项：靠重复把观念植入心中）；句意为多年灌输谨慎，让她不假思索就小心。

pos.zh: 反复灌输；谆谆教诲；使养成

senses.title: Teach by repetition
senses.definition: to make an idea stick by saying or showing it again and again
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复说或反复示范使一个观念扎下根
senses.example: Years of inculcating caution had made her careful without thinking.
senses.exampleCN: 多年灌输谨慎，让她不假思索就小心。
senses.why: The word assumes that repetition does the work that argument cannot.
senses.whyCN: 这个词假定，重复能做成论证做不到的事。

senses.title: Instil values
senses.definition: to plant moral beliefs so deep that they guide behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 把道德信念植得足够深以指导行为
senses.example: The school set out to inculcate honesty rather than merely to punish lying.
senses.exampleCN: 学校要灌输诚实，而不只是惩罚说谎。
senses.why: A value that is only known is weak; one that is inculcated acts before it is examined.
senses.whyCN: 只是被知道的价值观很弱；被灌输的那一个在受检验之前就已行动。

senses.title: Implant a habit
senses.definition: to train a behaviour until it needs no conscious decision
senses.definitionCN: 把一个行为训练到不需要有意识决定
senses.example: She inculcated the habit of checking the locks twice.
senses.exampleCN: 她养成了检查两遍门锁的习惯。
senses.why: A habit is a decision that has been handed over to the body.
senses.whyCN: 习惯是被交给身体去执行的决定。

senses.title: Drill a rule
senses.definition: to teach a rule through repeated practice and correction
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复练习与纠正来教一条规则
senses.example: The coach inculcated one rule at a time and would not move on early.
senses.exampleCN: 教练一次只灌输一条规则，不肯提前推进。
senses.why: Drilling works because the body remembers what the mind forgets.
senses.whyCN: 训练之所以有效，是因为身体记得心智所忘的。

senses.title: Inculcate obedience
senses.definition: to train a person to comply without questioning
senses.definitionCN: 把一个人训练到不加质疑地顺从
senses.example: The regime inculcated obedience through daily ritual.
senses.exampleCN: 该政权通过每日仪式灌输服从。
senses.why: Here the word turns critical: repetition can install compliance as easily as virtue.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词转为批评：重复既能装进美德，也能装进顺从。

senses.title: Inculcate caution
senses.definition: to make someone habitually careful about risk
senses.definitionCN: 使某人习惯性地对风险保持小心
senses.example: His parents inculcated caution with stories of near misses.
senses.exampleCN: 他的父母用险些出事的经历灌输谨慎。
senses.why: Caution taught through story arrives with feeling attached, which is why it lasts.
senses.whyCN: 借故事教来的谨慎带着情感，因此能留下来。

senses.title: Inculcate through example
senses.definition: to transmit a belief by consistently acting it out
senses.definitionCN: 通过一贯地做出某种行为来传递信念
senses.example: She inculcated fairness less by speech than by how she divided the work.
senses.exampleCN: 她灌输公平，与其说靠言语，不如说靠如何分派工作。
senses.why: Example is the strongest form of repetition, because it shows the belief in use.
senses.whyCN: 榜样是最强的重复形式，因为它展示了信念在使用中的样子。

senses.title: Inculcation resisted
senses.definition: the process by which a taught belief is finally refused
senses.definitionCN: 被教导的信念最终被拒绝的过程
senses.example: The students endured years of inculcation and then rejected most of it.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们忍受了多年灌输，然后拒绝了其中大部分。
senses.why: What is implanted can also be dug out, though the roots usually remain.
senses.whyCN: 被植入的东西也能被挖出来，尽管根通常还在。

intro.en: Inculcate comes from Latin for trampling in, the picture of a heel pressing an idea into soft ground.
intro.cn: inculcate 来自拉丁语「踩进去」，画面是脚跟把一个观念压进松软的地面。

items.en: Inculcare meant 'to trample in, to force upon', built from in- and calcare.
items.cn: inculcare 意为「踩进去、强加」，由 in- 与 calcare 构成。

items.en: Calcare 'to tread' comes from calx, the heel, and gives the sense of pressure from above.
items.cn: calcare「踩踏」出自 calx（脚跟），带来自上而下的压力感。

items.en: Calx meant heel; Roman soldiers and farmers both knew the weight of one.
items.cn: calx 意为脚跟；罗马士兵与农夫都懂得一只脚跟的重量。

items.en: English took the verb in the 16c., at first for teaching by forceful repetition.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，最初指靠强力重复来教。

items.en: Modern English keeps the tone: the word is neutral in education and critical in politics.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这种语气：在教育中中性，在政治中带批评。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tread root; the near-meaning group names ways of implanting ideas.
note.cn: 形近组共享「踩」的词根；近义组列出植入观念的不同方式。

entries.definition: the act of driving an idea in by repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 靠重复把观念打入的行为。

entries.definition: one who drills ideas into others.
entries.definitionCN: 把观念灌输给他人的人。

entries.definition: tending to implant by repetition.
to keep eggs warm until they hatch.
to put a feeling or idea in gradually.
to fix an idea firmly in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 把观念牢牢固定于心中。

entries.definition: to teach beliefs that must not be questioned.
to train by repeated exercise.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a heel pressing letters into wet clay until they cannot be wiped out.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「脚跟把字压进湿泥、直到抹不掉」的画面。

normal.en: Inculcate contains calx, the heel: the idea is stepped into the mind.
normal.cn: inculcate 含 calx（脚跟）：观念是被踩进心里的。

normal.en: Think of a path worn into grass by the same pair of shoes.
normal.cn: 想象同双鞋在草地上踩出一条路。

normal.en: Say in-KUL-kate; the middle sounds like a firm press downward.
normal.cn: 读成 in-KUL-kate，中间音像一次坚定的下压。

normal.en: Link with calc, heel: pressure from above is the whole image.
normal.cn: 和 calc（脚跟）联系：自上而下的压力就是整个画面。

normal.en: Pair it with repetition: inculcation is repetition with a destination.
normal.cn: 和 repetition 配对：灌输是有目的地的重复。

abstract.en: Repetition can build a virtue or a cage, and it does not ask which.
abstract.cn: 重复既能造美德，也能造笼子，而它不问是哪一种。

abstract.en: What is pressed in deeply is hard to remove, even after it is rejected.
abstract.cn: 被压得很深的东西很难移除，即使被拒绝之后。

abstract.en: Example teaches faster than instruction because it shows the idea working.
abstract.cn: 榜样比训导教得快，因为它展示观念在运作。

examples.en: Years of inculcating caution had made her careful without thinking.
examples.cn: 多年灌输谨慎，让她不假思索就小心。

examples.en: The school set out to inculcate honesty rather than merely to punish lying.
examples.cn: 学校要灌输诚实，而不只是惩罚说谎。

examples.en: The coach inculcated one rule at a time and would not move on early.
examples.cn: 教练一次只灌输一条规则，不肯提前推进。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进）+ culc（踩）+ ate（动词）：把观念踩进心里，就是「灌输」。

root: 拉丁语 calx（脚跟）→ calcare（踩踏），加 in-（向内）→ inculcare

sensesIntro.en: Inculcate always involves pressure and repetition; the senses differ in what is being pressed in and who is holding the heel.
sensesIntro.cn: inculcate 始终包含压力与重复；各义项的差别在于压进去的是什么，以及谁握着脚跟。

core.en: PRESSING AN IDEA INTO THE MIND

branches.en: Repetition, habit and drill, the mechanics of the word.
branches.cn: 重复、习惯与训练，这个词的机制。

branches.en: Values and caution planted as guiding instincts.
branches.cn: 作为指导本能被植下的价值观与谨慎。

branches.en: The political danger: compliance installed without question.
branches.cn: 政治上的危险：不加质疑地装进顺从。

branches.en: Example as the strongest repetition.
branches.cn: 作为最强重复的榜样。

branches.en: What is implanted can later be dug out.
branches.cn: 被植入之物后来也能被挖出。

intro.en: The culc family is about treading: inculcate presses in, and the Latin heel is never far from the meaning.
intro.cn: culc 词族与踩踏有关：inculcate 往里压，而拉丁语的脚跟从未离这个词义太远。

latinIntro.en: Latin calx means heel and calcare means to tread; in- adds direction, and direction here is inward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 calx 意为脚跟，calcare 意为踩；in- 加上方向，而这里的方向是向内。

items.exampleCN: 他们很早就灌输了这条规则。

items.example: The old coach was a patient inculcator.
items.exampleCN: 老教练是个有耐心的灌输者。

items.example: The book has an inculcative tone.

items.exampleCN: 被灌输的习惯留了下来。

items.example: He trod the same path daily.
The bird has a sharp calcar.

definition_zh: 淡而无味的；乏味的；无生气的
definition_en: lacking taste, interest or liveliness
core_image: 一碗汤颜色正常，喝下去却什么也说不出，只像温水
scene: 餐厅里灯光很好，菜却全是同一个味道。The insipid soup needed salt, pepper and a reason to exist.
sceneCN: 这里 insipid 指淡而无味（第 1 个义项：食物缺乏味道）；句意为这碗汤既缺盐也缺存在的理由。

pos.zh: 淡而无味的；乏味的；无生气的

senses.title: Tasteless food
senses.definition: food or drink that gives the tongue almost nothing
senses.definitionCN: 给舌头几乎没有信息量的食物或饮料
senses.example: The insipid soup needed salt, pepper and a reason to exist.
senses.exampleCN: 这碗汤既缺盐也缺存在的理由。
senses.why: The word began in the mouth; taste is the first test of whether something has a self.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从嘴里开始；味道是检验某物「有没有自我」的第一关。

senses.title: Dull conversation
senses.definition: talk that fills time without giving anything to hold on to
senses.definitionCN: 填满时间却不给人任何抓手的谈话
senses.example: The reception was full of insipid conversation about weather.
senses.exampleCN: 招待会上全是关于天气的乏味谈话。
senses.why: Talk without substance still occupies the only resource nobody can save, which is time.
senses.whyCN: 没有实质的谈话仍占用了谁也省不下的资源，那就是时间。

senses.title: Colourless style
senses.definition: writing that avoids risk and therefore avoids impression
senses.definitionCN: 回避风险、因而回避印象的写作
senses.example: The report was correct, thorough and insipid.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告正确、详尽，也毫无生气。
senses.why: Style becomes insipid when every sentence could be swapped for another without loss.
senses.whyCN: 当每个句子都能被另一句无损替换时，文风就变得乏味。

senses.title: Insipid personality
senses.definition: a person who offers little that is distinct or memorable
senses.definitionCN: 给不出什么独特或难忘之处的人
senses.example: The character was written as insipid on purpose.
senses.exampleCN: 这个角色是刻意写成平淡的。
senses.why: A character can be quiet and still vivid; the word targets not volume but emptiness.
senses.whyCN: 角色可以安静而仍鲜明；这个词针对的不是音量，而是空。

senses.title: Insipid compromise
senses.definition: a settlement that satisfies nobody and stands for nothing
senses.definitionCN: 谁都不满意、也不代表任何东西的妥协
senses.example: The insipid compromise pleased the chair and no one else.
senses.exampleCN: 这个无味的折中只让主席满意。
senses.why: Compromise can be wisdom or mush, and the word marks the mush.
senses.whyCN: 妥协可以是智慧，也可以是糊状物，而这个词标记的是糊状物。

senses.title: Insipid sentiment
senses.definition: feeling expressed so safely that it costs the speaker nothing
senses.definitionCN: 表达得过于安全、说话者毫无代价的情感
senses.example: The film's insipid sentimentality aged badly.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影浅薄的感伤很快过时了。
senses.why: Feeling that costs the speaker nothing asks the listener to pay for it.
senses.whyCN: 说话者毫无代价的情感，是要求听者替它付账。

senses.title: Insipid routine
senses.definition: a daily round that repeats without variation or texture
senses.definitionCN: 毫无变化与质地的日常循环
senses.example: Life in the suburb had become insipid but comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 郊区生活变得枯燥，却也舒适。
senses.why: Comfort and dullness often arrive together, and one pays for the other.
senses.whyCN: 舒适与枯燥常常同来，一个的账由另一个付。

senses.title: The insipid as safe
senses.definition: the quality of being unobjectionable precisely because nothing is risked
senses.definitionCN: 正因为不冒任何风险而无可指摘的性质
senses.example: The insipid choice was the one the committee could defend.
senses.exampleCN: 那个平淡的选择是委员会唯一能为之辩护的。
senses.why: The word often criticises what a cautious institution rewards, which is the point of using it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常批评谨慎机构所奖励的东西，而这正是使用它的用意。

intro.en: Insipid is built from not and taste, so it says simply that something has no savour.
intro.cn: insipid 由「不」与「味」构成，它只说明某物没有滋味。

items.en: Insipidus meant 'tasteless, without savour', built from in- and sapidus.
items.cn: insipidus 意为「无味的、没有滋味的」，由 in- 与 sapidus 构成。

items.en: Sapidus meant 'savoury, wise', from sapere, to taste and to know.
items.cn: sapidus 意为「有味的、明智的」，出自 sapere（尝，也指知）。

items.en: Sapere 'to taste' also gives sapient and sage; knowing and tasting were once one act.
items.cn: sapere「尝」也给出 sapient 与 sage；知与尝曾经是同一个动作。

items.en: English took the adjective in the 17c., first for food and then for talk.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，先用于食物，后用于言谈。

items.en: Modern English uses it for anything that fails to register, from soup to policy.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于任何留不下印象的东西，从汤到政策。

note.en: The look-alike group turns on taste and wisdom; the near-meaning group shades the word's dullness.
note.cn: 形近组围绕「味」与「智」；近义组给出乏味的不同层次。

entries.definition: the quality of being tasteless or dull.
in a dull, flavourless way.
having a strong, pleasant taste.
wise, full of discernment.
tasteless or uninterestingly mild.
not interesting or sharp.
lifeless and offering nothing.
so ordinary that it has lost all force.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a warm bowl of liquid that could be anything and is nothing.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一碗温热的液体，可能是任何东西，却又什么都不是」的画面。

normal.en: Insipid is in + sapid; sapid comes from sapere, to taste.
normal.cn: insipid 是 in + sapid；sapid 出自 sapere（尝）。

normal.en: Think of a soup that has colour but no information.
normal.cn: 想象一碗有颜色却没有信息的汤。

normal.en: Say in-SIP-id; the small i sounds like a flat, weak taste.
normal.cn: 读成 in-SIP-id，短小的 i 音像寡淡的味道。

normal.en: Link with sapient: the wise word and the tasty word share a root.
normal.cn: 和 sapient 联系：智慧之词与有味之词同根。

normal.en: Pair it with vivid: insipid is vivid with the lights off.
normal.cn: 和 vivid 配对：insipid 是关了灯的 vivid。

abstract.en: What aims to offend nobody usually ends by moving nobody.
abstract.cn: 想不得罪任何人的东西，通常也打动不了任何人。

abstract.en: Taste is information; a thing without taste gives the mind nothing to hold.
abstract.cn: 味道是信息；没有味道的东西不给心智任何抓手。

abstract.en: The safest sentence is often the one nobody remembers.
abstract.cn: 最安全的句子，常常是没人记得的句子。

examples.en: The insipid soup needed salt, pepper and a reason to exist.
examples.cn: 这碗汤既缺盐也缺存在的理由。

examples.en: The reception was full of insipid conversation about weather.
examples.cn: 招待会上全是关于天气的乏味谈话。

examples.en: The report was correct, thorough and insipid.
examples.cn: 这份报告正确、详尽，也毫无生气。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（不）+ sip（味）+ id：没有味道，就是「淡而无味、乏味」。

root: 拉丁语 sapere（尝、知）→ sapidus（有味的），加否定前缀 in-

sensesIntro.en: Insipid begins with the tongue and spreads to everything that fails to register; the senses differ in what is being tasted.
sensesIntro.cn: insipid 从舌头开始，扩到一切留不下印象之物；各义项的差别在于被尝的是什么。

core.cn: 给不出任何东西的某物

branches.en: The bodily origin: food and drink without savour.
branches.cn: 身体本源：没有滋味的食物与饮料。

branches.en: People and talk that offer nothing to hold.
branches.cn: 给不出抓手的谈话与人。

branches.en: Style and feeling that take no risk.
branches.cn: 不冒风险的文风与情感。

branches.en: Compromises and routines that repeat without texture.
branches.cn: 没有质地的折中与循环日常。

branches.en: The reason it survives: safety.
branches.cn: 它得以存活的原因：安全。

intro.en: The sap family joins taste and knowledge: sapid is savoury, sapient is wise, and insipid has neither.
intro.cn: sap 词族把味与知接在一起：sapid 是有味的，sapient 是明智的，而 insipid 两者皆无。

latinIntro.en: Latin sapere means both to taste and to know; the negative prefix in- empties the word of both.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sapere 既指尝也指知；否定前缀 in- 把两者都从词里清空。

items.meaning: the state of having no taste
items.example: The insipidity of the film was total.
The sapidity of the broth surprised her.

items.exampleCN: 那位明智的老法官听着。

items.meaning: wise, as one who has tasted life

definition_zh: 并置；并列；把……放在一起对照
definition_en: to place two things side by side, especially to show a contrast
core_image: 两幅画挂在同一面墙上，一幅是废墟，一幅是花园，中间只隔一掌宽
scene: 编辑把两张照片放在同一页，左边是婚礼，右边是空椅子。The layout juxtaposes celebration and absence.
sceneCN: 这里 juxtapose 指把两者并置以显示对照（第 2 个义项：通过并置比较）；句意为版面把庆祝与缺席并置。

senses.title: Place side by side
senses.definition: to set two things next to each other in space
