senses.definitionCN: 把两个事物在空间上放到彼此旁边
senses.example: The curator juxtaposed the two portraits on one wall.
senses.exampleCN: 策展人把两幅肖像并置在同一面墙上。
senses.why: The word is first about position, not meaning; contrast is what position can produce.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先关乎位置，而非意义；对照是位置可能产生的结果。

senses.title: Compare by contrast
senses.definition: to put things together so that the difference between them speaks
senses.definitionCN: 把事物放在一起，让它们之间的差异自己说话
senses.example: The layout juxtaposes celebration and absence.
senses.exampleCN: 版面把庆祝与缺席并置。
senses.why: Proximity is an argument: what sits beside what tells the viewer how to read both.
senses.whyCN: 邻近本身就是论证：谁挨着谁，告诉观者如何读这两者。

senses.title: Contrast in art
senses.definition: a compositional act that creates meaning through adjacency
senses.definitionCN: 通过相邻关系创造意义的构图行为
senses.example: The film juxtaposes a lullaby with a factory floor.
senses.exampleCN: 影片把摇篮曲与厂房并置。
senses.why: Adjacency is the cheapest tool a composition has and the most persuasive.
senses.whyCN: 相邻是构图最便宜也最有说服力的工具。

senses.title: Set old against new
senses.definition: to place a tradition beside its replacement
senses.definitionCN: 把一种传统放到它的替代物旁边
senses.example: The museum juxtaposes a hand loom and a robot arm.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把手工织机与机械臂并置。
senses.why: History becomes legible when two moments share a frame.
senses.whyCN: 当两个时刻共享一个框，历史就变得可读。

senses.title: Juxtapose images
senses.definition: to arrange pictures so that they comment on each other
senses.definitionCN: 排列图像，使它们互相评说
senses.example: The photographer juxtaposed a full table and an empty street.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师把满桌与空街并置。
senses.why: Two pictures side by side can say what neither says alone.
senses.whyCN: 两张并排的画能说出任何一张单独说不出的话。

senses.title: Juxtapose arguments
senses.definition: to set two claims beside each other for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 把两个主张放在一起供比较
senses.example: The essay juxtaposes the two theories without choosing between them.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把两种理论并置，却不作取舍。
senses.why: Neutral placement is a form of respect: both get the same light before judgement.
senses.whyCN: 中立的并置是一种尊重：在判断之前，两者得到同样的光。

senses.title: Juxtaposition as irony
senses.definition: the ironic effect produced by putting mismatched things together
senses.definitionCN: 把不匹配之物放在一起产生的反讽效果
senses.example: The juxtaposition of a slogan and a broken window was not accidental.
senses.exampleCN: 标语与破窗的并置并非偶然。
senses.why: Irony here is structural: the arrangement does the mocking, not the words.
senses.whyCN: 这里的反讽是结构性的：嘲讽由安排完成，而不是由文字。

senses.title: Juxtapose lives
senses.definition: to place two life stories together so that each reveals the other
senses.definitionCN: 把两个人生故事放在一起，使彼此显出对方
senses.example: The novel juxtaposes two brothers across forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说把两兄弟并置，跨越四十年。
senses.why: A life is hard to see from inside; another life beside it works as a lamp.
senses.whyCN: 人生从内部很难看清；旁边另一个人生就像一盏灯。

intro.en: Juxtapose joins a Latin word for near with a French word for place: to place near.
intro.cn: juxtapose 把拉丁语「近」与法语「放置」接在一起：放到近处。

items.en: French juxtaposer appeared in the 19c., built from Latin juxta and French poser.
items.cn: 法语 juxtaposer 出现在十九世纪，由拉丁语 juxta 与法语 poser 构成。

items.en: Juxta meant 'beside, close to', and survives in the legal phrase juxta modum.
items.cn: juxta 意为「在旁边、靠近」，至今存于法律短语 juxta modum。

items.en: Poser 'to place' comes from Latin ponere, also behind position and compose.
items.cn: poser「放置」出自拉丁语 ponere，也是 position 与 compose 的来源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 19c., along with the noun juxtaposition.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入这个动词，连同名词 juxtaposition。

items.en: Modern criticism uses it for layout, film editing and argument alike.
items.cn: 现代批评把它用于版面、剪辑与论证。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the placing root; the near-meaning group names ways of putting things together.
note.cn: 形近组共享「放置」词根；近义组列出把事物放在一起的方式。

entries.definition: the act or result of placing side by side.
placed next to each other.
in the act of setting side by side.
to lay one thing over another.
to examine two things for similarities and differences.
to set things so that their differences stand out.
to put two things together as a set.
to collect and arrange items for comparison.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of two unlike paintings hanging a hand's width apart.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「两幅不相像的画只隔一掌宽挂在墙上」的画面。

normal.en: Juxta means near, and pose means place: near-place, exactly as spelled.
normal.cn: juxta 意为近，pose 意为放：近处放置，正是字面。

normal.en: Juxtapose is not compare; it only arranges, and the viewer compares.
normal.cn: juxtapose 不是 compare；它只负责排列，比较由观者完成。

normal.en: Think of a magazine spread with two photos facing each other.
normal.cn: 想象杂志跨页上两张照片面对面。

normal.en: Say juk-stuh-POZE; the ending sounds like placing something down.
normal.cn: 读成 juk-stuh-POZE，结尾像把东西放下。

normal.en: Link with position: both come from ponere, to place.
normal.cn: 和 position 联系：两者都出自 ponere（放置）。

abstract.en: Meaning can be made by adjacency alone, without a single sentence.
abstract.cn: 仅靠相邻就能制造意义，不需要一句话。

abstract.en: What you place beside a thing tells people how to feel about it.
abstract.cn: 你把什么放在某物旁边，就告诉了人们该如何感觉它。

abstract.en: Fair comparison gives both objects the same light before judging.
abstract.cn: 公平的比较在判断前给两个对象同样的光。

examples.en: The layout juxtaposes celebration and absence.
examples.cn: 版面把庆祝与缺席并置。

examples.en: The curator juxtaposed the two portraits on one wall.
examples.cn: 策展人把两幅肖像并置在同一面墙上。

examples.en: The museum juxtaposes a hand loom and a robot arm.
examples.cn: 博物馆把手工织机与机械臂并置。

dict_mnemonic.text: juxta（旁边）+ pose（放）：放在旁边，就是「并置」。

root: 拉丁语 juxta（靠近）+ 法语 poser（放置，源自拉丁语 ponere）

sensesIntro.en: Juxtapose is a spatial act that produces meaning; the senses differ in whether the effect is comparison, history, irony or revelation.
sensesIntro.cn: juxtapose 是产生意义的空间行为；各义项的差别在于效果是对照、历史、反讽，还是揭示。

core.en: PLACING NEAR SO THAT MEANING APPEARS

branches.en: Pure arrangement, in space or on a page.
branches.cn: 空间或页面上的纯排列。

branches.en: Comparison produced by a neutral frame.
branches.cn: 由中立框架产生的比较。

branches.en: Art and history arranged for contrast.
branches.cn: 为对照而安排的艺术与历史。

branches.en: Irony created by mismatch in the frame.
branches.cn: 由框内不匹配造成的反讽。

branches.en: Two lives lit by each other.
branches.cn: 两个人被彼此照亮。

intro.en: The pose family is all about placing: juxtapose puts beside, compose puts together, impose puts upon.
intro.cn: pose 词族全与放置有关：juxtapose 放旁边，compose 放一起，impose 放上面。

latinIntro.en: Latin juxta supplies nearness and ponere supplies placement; the compound is a small instruction to the eye.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 juxta 提供「近」，ponere 提供「放」；这个复合词是给眼睛的一条小指令。

items.example: He composed the page by hand.
The position of the text matters.

definition_zh: 言简意赅的；寡言的；简短有力的
definition_en: using very few words, often with a dry or abrupt force
core_image: 一个斯巴达士兵听完长长的劝降，只回了一个字，然后转身继续磨刀
scene: 记者问了七个问题，他答了十四个字，会议就结束了。His laconic reply ended the argument faster than a speech would have.
sceneCN: 这里 laconic 指言简意赅（第 1 个义项：用极少的词表达）；句意为他的简短回答比一场演说更快结束了争论。

derivatives.zh: 拉科尼亚（斯巴达所在地区）

senses.title: Few words, full weight
senses.definition: expressing much in very few words
senses.definitionCN: 用极少的词表达很多
senses.example: His laconic reply ended the argument faster than a speech would have.
senses.exampleCN: 他的简短回答比一场演说更快结束了争论。
senses.why: The word values density, not silence: a few words that carry everything they need.
senses.whyCN: 这个词看重密度，而不是沉默：几个字扛起它们所需的全部重量。

senses.title: A short answer
senses.definition: a reply so brief that it refuses further discussion
senses.definitionCN: 短到拒绝继续讨论的回答
senses.example: Asked whether he agreed, he gave a laconic yes.
senses.exampleCN: 被问是否同意时，他只给了一个「是」。
senses.why: Brevity can be a door closing politely, which is why the word often feels final.
senses.whyCN: 简短可以是一扇礼貌关上的门，因此这个词常显得终局。

senses.title: A compressed style
senses.definition: writing that removes every word the meaning does not need
senses.definitionCN: 删去一切意义所不需的字句的写作
senses.example: The report was laconic to the point of coldness.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告简练到近乎冷淡。
senses.why: A style becomes laconic when nothing in it could be removed without loss.
senses.whyCN: 当文中的任何东西都不能被无损删去时，文风就变得简练。

senses.title: A brief warning
senses.definition: a warning delivered in so few words that it cannot be softened
senses.definitionCN: 短到无法被软化的警告
senses.example: The laconic note said only: do not go past the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 那张简短的纸条只写着：不要越过围栏。
senses.why: When a warning is shortened, nothing is left for argument to hold on to.
senses.whyCN: 警告被缩短后，论证就没有可以抓的地方。

senses.title: Laconic humour
senses.definition: dry humour that lets a short phrase carry the joke
senses.definitionCN: 让短短一句承担笑点的冷幽默
senses.example: His laconic remark got the laugh that the long joke had missed.
senses.exampleCN: 他的简短一句赢得了那个长笑话没赢到的笑。
senses.why: Dry humour works by withholding the tone that would explain it.
senses.whyCN: 冷幽默靠扣下那个本可解释它的语气来起作用。

senses.title: Restraint under emotion
senses.definition: saying little when feeling would justify much
senses.definitionCN: 在情感本可容许多说时说得很少
senses.example: After the news he was laconic, and everyone understood more from that.
senses.exampleCN: 消息之后他很少说话，而大家反而从中懂了更多。
senses.why: Restraint can transmit feeling more accurately than elaboration.
senses.whyCN: 克制有时比铺陈更准确地传递情感。

senses.title: The laconic commander
senses.definition: the style of a leader who gives orders without explanation
senses.definitionCN: 不作解释就下命令的领导者风格
senses.example: The laconic captain said one word and the crew moved.
senses.exampleCN: 寡言的船长说了一个词，船员就动了起来。
senses.why: In command, extra words create doubt; a short order sounds like a settled fact.
senses.whyCN: 在指挥中，多余的话制造怀疑；简短的命令听起来像既定事实。

senses.title: The risk of the laconic
senses.definition: the failure that comes when brevity withholds too much
senses.definitionCN: 简短扣下太多信息而造成的失误
senses.example: The laconic email read as rude to the new client.
senses.exampleCN: 这封简短的邮件在新客户看来很无礼。
senses.why: The same economy that saves words can save too few.
senses.whyCN: 省字的同一种经济，也可能省得太少。

intro.en: Laconic comes from Laconia, the region of Sparta, whose citizens were famous for saying a great deal in almost no words.
intro.cn: laconic 来自拉科尼亚，即斯巴达所在的地区，那里的人以用极少的字说很多话而闻名。

items.en: Lakonikos meant of Laconia, the region around Sparta.
items.cn: Lakonikos 意为「拉科尼亚的」，即斯巴达周边地区。

items.en: Spartans were known for terse answers; Philip of Macedon was told simply no to his demand.
items.cn: 斯巴达人以简短回答著称；马其顿的腓力得到的只是一个「不」。

items.en: Latin borrowed the adjective to describe that style of speech.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个形容词，用来描述那种说话风格。

items.en: English took it in the 16c., first as a comment on Spartan brevity.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，最初是对斯巴达式简短的评价。

items.en: Modern English applies it to any brief, dry, forceful utterance.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于任何简短、干燥、有力的话。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Laconia stem; the near-meaning group measures brevity.
note.cn: 形近组共享 Laconia 词干；近义组衡量简短的各个层次。

entries.definition: in a brief, dry manner.
the habit of speaking briefly.
a short, pointed saying.
the region of Sparta.
using few words that are neat and pointed.
giving much information in few words.
rudely brief.
saying very little by nature.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a Spartan soldier answering a long demand with one syllable.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「斯巴达士兵用一个音节回答冗长要求」的画面。

normal.en: Laconic comes from Laconia, the land of Sparta.
normal.cn: laconic 来自 Laconia，也就是斯巴达的所在地。

normal.en: Think of a reply that arrives before the question has finished.
normal.cn: 想象一个在问题说完前就到达的回答。

normal.en: Link with concise: both cut words, but laconic keeps a dry edge.
normal.cn: 和 concise 联系：两者都删字，但 laconic 保留干燥的锋芒。

normal.en: Say luh-KON-ik; the short middle sounds like a door closing.
normal.cn: 读成 luh-KON-ik，短促的中间音像门关上。

normal.en: The word is about density, not silence: few words, heavy with meaning.
normal.cn: 这个词讲密度，不讲沉默：字少，意义重。

abstract.en: Brevity is powerful because it leaves the other person no room to bargain.
abstract.cn: 简短有力，因为它不给对方讨价还价的空间。

abstract.en: Restraint can say more than elaboration when the feeling is already visible.
abstract.cn: 当情感已经可见，克制能比铺陈说出更多。

abstract.en: Every removed word is a risk taken on the reader's understanding.
abstract.cn: 删掉的每个词，都是对读者理解力的一次冒险。

examples.en: His laconic reply ended the argument faster than a speech would have.
examples.cn: 他的简短回答比一场演说更快结束了争论。

examples.en: Asked whether he agreed, he gave a laconic yes.
examples.cn: 被问是否同意时，他只给了一个「是」。

examples.en: After the news he was laconic, and everyone understood more from that.
examples.cn: 消息之后他很少说话，而大家反而从中懂了更多。

dict_mnemonic.text: lacon（拉科尼亚，斯巴达）+ ic：斯巴达人字少，就是「言简意赅」。

root: 希腊语 Lakonikos（拉科尼亚的），指斯巴达式简短说话

sensesIntro.en: Laconic is brevity with force; the senses differ in whether the force is refusal, humour, restraint or command.
sensesIntro.cn: laconic 是有力的简短；各义项的差别在于这股力是拒绝、幽默、克制，还是命令。

branches.en: Density and the reply that ends talk.
branches.cn: 密度，以及结束谈话的回答。

branches.en: Compressed style and dry humour.
branches.cn: 被压缩的文风与冷幽默。

branches.en: Warnings and orders with no soft edge.
branches.cn: 没有软化边缘的警告与命令。

branches.en: Restraint when feeling is high.
branches.cn: 情感高涨时的克制。

branches.en: The failure mode: too few words for the reader.
branches.cn: 失败模式：对读者来说字太少。

intro.en: The Laconia family is small and place-bound: one region of Greece gave English a whole style of speech.
intro.cn: Laconia 词族很小，且与地点绑定：希腊的一个地区，给了英语一整套说话风格。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; Lakonikos is a place adjective, and the style of the place became the meaning of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根；Lakonikos 是地点形容词，而那个地方的风气成了这个词的意义。

items.meaning: of Laconia and its short speech
items.meaningCN: 拉科尼亚及其简短言语的
items.exampleCN: 他的简短便条说得很少。
这句简短的话终结了辩论。

items.example: Laconia trained its sons to speak little.
items.exampleCN: 拉科尼亚训练儿子们少说话。

items.meaningCN: 斯巴达的，引申为简朴严格

definition_zh: 健谈的；话多的；滔滔不绝的
definition_en: talking a great deal, often more than the situation requires
core_image: 一个人从进门就开始讲，讲到茶凉了、雨停了，手还在比划
scene: 出租车司机从机场一路讲到市区，连红绿灯都没让他停。The loquacious witness supplied three times the detail requested.
sceneCN: 这里 loquacious 指话多的（第 1 个义项：说得很多）；句意为这位健谈的证人提供了三倍于所需的细节。

pos.zh: 健谈的；话多的；滔滔不绝的

senses.title: Talks a great deal
senses.definition: speaks often and at length, beyond what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 说得频繁而长，超过所需
senses.example: The loquacious witness supplied three times the detail requested.
senses.exampleCN: 这位健谈的证人提供了三倍于所需的细节。
senses.why: The word measures quantity, not quality; tone decides whether it is fond or weary.
senses.whyCN: 这个词衡量数量，而非质量；语气决定它是亲昵还是疲惫。

senses.title: Fluent in many words
senses.definition: able to keep producing words without pause
senses.definitionCN: 能不停地产出词句
senses.example: He was loquacious in three languages and silent in none.
senses.exampleCN: 他用三种语言都滔滔不绝，没有一种是沉默的。
senses.why: Fluency here is stamina: the speaker can go on where others stop for breath.
senses.whyCN: 这里的流利是耐力：别人停下来换气的地方，说话者还能继续。

senses.title: The loquacious witness
senses.definition: a person who volunteers far more than asked
senses.definitionCN: 主动提供远多于所问内容的人
senses.example: The loquacious witness nearly talked the case past its point.
senses.exampleCN: 这位话多的证人差点把案子说过头。
senses.why: Institutions that need precise answers find this trait expensive.
senses.whyCN: 需要精确回答的机构，会觉得这种特质代价高昂。

senses.title: A loquacious narrator
senses.definition: a storyteller who lingers over every side path
senses.definitionCN: 在每条岔路都停留的讲述者
senses.example: The loquacious narrator delays the murder by two hundred pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这位絮叨的叙述者把谋杀拖后了两百页。
senses.why: Time in a story is finite, so every detour is paid for by the main line.
senses.whyCN: 故事里的时间是有限的，因此每次绕路都由主线付账。

senses.title: A loquacious mood
senses.definition: a mood in which speech flows easily and refuses to stop
senses.definitionCN: 说话顺畅且停不下来的心境
senses.example: Wine made him loquacious and generous.
senses.exampleCN: 酒让他话多而慷慨。
senses.why: The same person can be silent for a month and loquacious for an evening.
senses.whyCN: 同一个人可以沉默一个月，也可以滔滔不绝一个晚上。

senses.title: A loquacious persona
senses.definition: a public manner built on constant, charming speech
senses.definitionCN: 建立在持续、迷人言谈上的公众形象
senses.example: His loquacious persona hid a careful listener.
senses.exampleCN: 他健谈的人设下藏着一个细心的倾听者。
senses.why: A persona is a performance, and the word can suggest that the talking is cover.
senses.whyCN: 人设是表演，而这个词可能暗示那些话是一层遮盖。

senses.title: Loquacity as defence
senses.definition: speech used to fill space so that a question cannot land
senses.definitionCN: 用言语填满空间，使问题无法落地
senses.example: Her loquacity was a wall that no one could get through.
senses.exampleCN: 她的滔滔不绝是一堵谁也穿不过的墙。
senses.why: Volume can be a form of hiding, since a moving target is harder to pin.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以是一种躲藏，因为移动的目标更难被钉住。

senses.title: Loquacious company
senses.definition: the comfort of someone who keeps the silence filled
senses.definitionCN: 用话填满沉默的陪伴带来的舒适
senses.example: On the long drive his loquacious company kept her awake.
senses.exampleCN: 长途驾驶中，他健谈的陪伴让她保持清醒。
senses.why: The trait that tires can also carry a nervous room through the night.
senses.whyCN: 让人疲惫的特质，也能把紧张的一屋子人撑过夜晚。

intro.en: Loquacious comes from a Latin verb meaning to speak, and it names the speaker who will not stop.
intro.cn: loquacious 来自一个意为「说话」的拉丁动词，命名的是停不下来的说话者。

items.en: Loquax meant talkative, chattering, often with a hint of reproach.
items.cn: loquax 意为「话多的、喋喋的」，常带一点责备。

items.en: Loqui to speak is also behind eloquent, colloquy and soliloquy.
items.cn: loqui（说话）也是 eloquent、colloquy 与 soliloquy 的来源。

items.en: English took the adjective in the 17c., and the noun loquacity came with it.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，名词 loquacity 也随之而来。

items.en: Modern use is usually mild: a loquacious person is tiring, not wicked.
items.cn: 现代用法通常温和：话多的人令人累，却不邪恶。

items.en: The word keeps a formal edge; in speech people more often say talkative.
items.cn: 这个词仍偏正式；口语中人们更常说 talkative。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the speaking root; the near-meaning group measures how much is said.
note.cn: 形近组共享「说话」词根；近义组衡量说了多少。

entries.definition: the habit of talking much.
in a very talkative manner.
fluent and persuasive in speech.
a formal conversation.
liking to talk a lot.
talking too much about unimportant things.
speaking easily and at length.
using more words than needed.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a passenger who keeps talking even after the meter stops.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「计价器都停了、乘客还在讲」的画面。

normal.en: Loquacious contains loqu, to speak, as in eloquent and soliloquy.
normal.cn: loquacious 含 loqu（说话），如 eloquent 与 soliloquy。

normal.en: The -acious ending means full of: full of speech.
normal.cn: -acious 结尾意为「充满」：充满言语。

normal.en: Think of a radio left on in an empty room.
normal.cn: 想象一台留在空房间里的收音机。

normal.en: Say luh-KWAY-shus; the wide vowel sounds like an open mouth.
normal.cn: 读成 luh-KWAY-shus，宽大的元音像一张张开的嘴。

normal.en: Pair it with laconic: one cannot stop, the other will not start.
normal.cn: 和 laconic 配对：一个停不下，一个不肯开始。

abstract.en: Quantity of speech is not the same as communication.
abstract.cn: 说话的数量不等于交流。

abstract.en: Words can fill a room or hide inside it.
abstract.cn: 话语可以填满房间，也可以躲在里面。

abstract.en: The person who talks most is not always the one who has most to say.
abstract.cn: 说得最多的人，不总是最有话说的人。

examples.en: The loquacious witness supplied three times the detail requested.
examples.cn: 这位健谈的证人提供了三倍于所需的细节。

examples.en: He was loquacious in three languages and silent in none.
examples.cn: 他用三种语言都滔滔不绝，没有一种是沉默的。

examples.en: Her loquacity was a wall that no one could get through.
examples.cn: 她的滔滔不绝是一堵谁也穿不过的墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: loqu（说）+ acious（充满）：充满话，就是「健谈、话多」。

root: 拉丁语 loqui（说话）→ loquax（话多的）

sensesIntro.en: Loquacious always measures flow; the senses differ in whether the flow is charm, burden, defence or comfort.
sensesIntro.cn: loquacious 始终衡量流出的量；各义项的差别在于这股流是魅力、负担、防卫，还是安慰。

branches.en: Quantity and fluency, the plain senses.
branches.cn: 数量与流利，最朴素的两个义项。

branches.en: Witnesses and narrators who over-supply.
branches.cn: 提供过多的证人与叙述者。

branches.en: Mood and public persona.
branches.cn: 心境与公众形象。

branches.en: Speech used as a wall.
branches.cn: 被当作墙的言语。

branches.en: The comfort of a filled silence.
branches.cn: 被填满的沉默带来的舒适。

intro.en: The loqu family is about speaking: loquacious talks much, eloquent talks well, soliloquy is speech to oneself.
intro.cn: loqu 词族与说话有关：loquacious 说得多，eloquent 说得好，soliloquy 是对自己说。

latinIntro.en: Latin loqui means to speak; the suffix -ax marks a tendency, so loquax is a person inclined to speak.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 loqui 意为说话；后缀 -ax 标记倾向，因此 loquax 是倾向于说话的人。

items.exampleCN: 这位健谈的向导什么都懂。
她滔滔不绝地解释路线。
他雄辩的回答说服了他们。
这场对谈持续了一小时。
这段独白揭示他的恐惧。
绕圈子的说法避开了那个名字。
那篇大话连篇的演讲让他们厌烦。

definition_zh: 一丝不苟的；极其仔细的；谨小慎微的
definition_en: showing great attention to small details
core_image: 一个人把一叠发票按日期、金额和颜色对齐，又把最上面一张的边角抚平
scene: 她把每份档案的页码都核了两遍，才肯签字。His meticulous notes made the audit take half the expected time.
sceneCN: 这里 meticulous 指一丝不苟（第 1 个义项：对细节极度仔细）；句意为他一丝不苟的笔记让审计只用了预期时间的一半。

pos.zh: 一丝不苟的；极其仔细的

senses.title: Care about small details
senses.definition: giving close attention to details others might skip
senses.definitionCN: 对别人可能略过的细节给予密切注意
senses.example: His meticulous notes made the audit take half the expected time.
senses.exampleCN: 他一丝不苟的笔记让审计只用了预期时间的一半。
senses.why: The word praises the small: it treats the minor as if it mattered, and often it does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词赞美细小之物：它把次要的当作重要的，而它常常确实重要。

senses.title: Meticulous record-keeping
senses.definition: keeping accounts so exact that nothing needs reconstructing
senses.definitionCN: 记账精确到无需事后重建
senses.example: The clerk kept meticulous records of every delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 这位职员对每次交付都做了精细记录。
senses.why: A record is useful only if it can be trusted without being checked again.
senses.whyCN: 记录只有在无需复查就能被信任时才有用。

senses.title: Meticulous preparation
senses.definition: preparing so thoroughly that few surprises remain
senses.definitionCN: 准备得如此彻底，以致少有意外
senses.example: The meticulous preparation removed most of the risk.
senses.exampleCN: 周密的准备去掉了大部分风险。
senses.why: Preparation is a way of buying certainty with time.
senses.whyCN: 准备是用时间购买确定性的一种方式。

senses.title: Meticulous appearance
senses.definition: dressing and grooming with close attention
senses.definitionCN: 在穿着与修饰上极为留意
senses.example: His meticulous appearance suggested a careful mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲究的仪容暗示一颗谨慎的心。
senses.why: Appearance is a public record of private habits, so it can be read as evidence.
senses.whyCN: 仪容是私人习惯的公开记录，因此可以被当作证据来读。

senses.title: Meticulous attention
senses.definition: the act of watching something closely enough to catch small errors
senses.definitionCN: 足够贴近地观察以捕捉小错误
senses.example: A meticulous reading found the one wrong date.
senses.exampleCN: 一次细致的阅读找出了那个错误的日期。
senses.why: Most errors are small and quiet; only attention of this kind hears them.
senses.whyCN: 多数错误又小又安静；只有这种注意力能听见它们。

senses.title: Meticulous criticism
senses.definition: criticism that examines each small claim rather than the whole
senses.definitionCN: 逐一检查小主张而非整体的批评
senses.example: The review was meticulous and therefore slow to accept anything.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇评论细密，因此对任何东西都迟迟不肯接受。
senses.why: Examining every claim protects against error and can also paralyse.
senses.whyCN: 检查每个主张能防错，也能让人瘫痪。

senses.title: Meticulous but slow
senses.definition: the cost of detail: work that cannot be hurried
senses.definitionCN: 细节的代价：无法被催促的工作
senses.example: The meticulous method was right and three weeks late.
senses.exampleCN: 这套细致的方法是对的，但迟了三周。
senses.why: The word can turn critical when detail becomes the master rather than the servant.
senses.whyCN: 当细节成了主人而不是仆人，这个词就会转为批评。

senses.title: Meticulous honesty
senses.definition: a scrupulous accuracy about facts, including one's own
senses.definitionCN: 对事实的严谨准确，包括对自己
senses.example: He was meticulous even about his own mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 他甚至对自己的错误也一丝不苟。
senses.why: Honesty of this kind costs more, because it has no exception for the self.
senses.whyCN: 这种诚实代价更高，因为它对自我不设例外。

intro.en: Meticulous comes from a Latin word for fear, and its modern praise still carries a trace of anxiety.
intro.cn: meticulous 来自一个意为「恐惧」的拉丁词，它现代的赞美里仍带一丝焦虑。

items.en: Meticulosus meant fearful, timid, built from metus, fear.
items.cn: meticulosus 意为「胆怯的、畏缩的」，由 metus（恐惧）构成。

items.en: Metus means fear, dread, and also gives the rare English metus.
items.cn: metus 意为恐惧、畏惧，也给出英语中罕用的 metus。

items.en: English adopted the word in the 19c. with a new sense: careful to the point of anxiety.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪采用这个词，并赋予新义：仔细到近乎焦虑。

items.en: The meaning moved from frightened to scrupulous, because fear makes a person check twice.
items.cn: 意义从「害怕」移向「严谨」，因为恐惧会让人检查两遍。

items.en: Modern English uses it mostly as praise, though a hint of fussiness can remain.
items.cn: 现代英语多把它当赞美，尽管仍可能留一点挑剔的暗示。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fear root; the near-meaning group ranks degrees of care.
note.cn: 形近组共享「恐惧」词根；近义组排列仔细的程度。

entries.definition: with extreme care about detail.
the quality of being very careful.
excessive attention to detail.
easily frightened.
very careful to be correct and fair.
entries.definitionCN: 极其小心以求正确公正的。

entries.definition: done with great and patient care.
entries.definitionCN: 以极大耐心细致完成的。

entries.definition: covering every part, leaving nothing out.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖每一部分、无所遗漏的。

entries.definition: very concerned about cleanliness or detail.
entries.definitionCN: 对洁净或细节极为在意的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of receipts aligned by date, size and colour before anyone asks.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「还没人要求，就把发票按日期、大小与颜色对齐」的画面。

normal.en: Meticulous comes from metus, fear: fear of a mistake is what makes the checking.
normal.cn: meticulous 出自 metus（恐惧）：怕出错，才去检查。

normal.en: Think of someone straightening a picture frame that is already straight.
normal.cn: 想象有人把已经挂正的画框再摆正一次。

normal.en: Say muh-TIK-yuh-lus; the tight middle sounds like a small adjustment.
normal.cn: 读成 muh-TIK-yuh-lus，紧促的中间音像一次微调。

normal.en: Link with timid: both begin in fear, but one ends in care.
normal.cn: 和 timid 联系：两者都始于恐惧，但一个终于细致。

normal.en: Pair it with detail: meticulous is detail with a nervous pulse.
normal.cn: 和 detail 配对：meticulous 是带着紧张脉搏的细节。

abstract.en: Care becomes a virtue when it serves the whole; it becomes a burden when it serves itself.
abstract.cn: 当细致服务于整体，它是美德；当它服务于自身，它是负担。

abstract.en: Checking twice is cheap compared with explaining once.
abstract.cn: 检查两遍比起解释一遍便宜。

abstract.en: The most careful people are often the ones who have seen what a small error costs.
abstract.cn: 最仔细的人，常常是见过小错误代价的人。

examples.en: His meticulous notes made the audit take half the expected time.
examples.cn: 他一丝不苟的笔记让审计只用了预期时间的一半。

examples.en: The clerk kept meticulous records of every delivery.
examples.cn: 这位职员对每次交付都做了精细记录。

examples.en: A meticulous reading found the one wrong date.
examples.cn: 一次细致的阅读找出了那个错误的日期。

dict_mnemonic.text: metic（怕）+ ulous（多……的）：怕出错而反复检查，就是「一丝不苟」。

root: 拉丁语 metus（恐惧）→ meticulosus（胆怯的），十九世纪转为「极其仔细」

sensesIntro.en: Meticulous is attention sharpened by worry; the senses differ in whether the worry serves accuracy, appearance or speed.
sensesIntro.cn: meticulous 是被担忧磨利的注意力；各义项的差别在于这担忧服务于准确、仪容，还是速度。

branches.en: The core act: looking closely enough to catch what others miss.
branches.cn: 核心动作：看得足够近以捕捉他人所漏。

branches.en: Records and preparation built so nothing has to be redone.
branches.cn: 做到无需返工的记录与准备。

branches.en: Appearance and honesty kept at the same standard.
branches.cn: 以同一标准维系的仪容与诚实。

branches.en: The cost side: slowness and over-scrutiny.
branches.cn: 代价面：缓慢与过度审视。

branches.en: Detail as service versus detail as master.
branches.cn: 细节作仆人，与细节作主人。

intro.en: The metic family is small; the same Latin fear also gives timid, which shows where the word began.
intro.cn: metic 词族很小；同一个拉丁语「恐惧」也给出 timid，显示出这个词的起点。

latinIntro.en: Latin metus is fear, and meticulosus is full of it; the modern sense is what fear does to a person who must be right.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 metus 是恐惧，meticulosus 是充满恐惧；现代义就是恐惧对一个必须正确的人所做的事。

items.exampleCN: 他的细致功夫看得出来。
她一丝不苟地清点箱子。
他的一丝不苟救了这个档案。

items.example: The crowd tried to intimidate her.

definition_zh: 极小的；微小的；小写字母的
definition_en: extremely small, or relating to lowercase letters
core_image: 一封写在米粒大小纸片上的信，字迹细到要用放大镜才看得清
scene: 预算表上的数字看起来正常，最后一行的小数却几乎看不见。A minuscule error in the code cost three days.
sceneCN: 这里 minuscule 指极小的（第 4 个义项：微小的细节）；句意为代码里一个极小的错误花了三天。

senses.title: Extremely small
senses.definition: so small that size itself becomes the point
senses.definitionCN: 小到尺寸本身就成了重点
senses.example: The difference was minuscule but the result changed completely.
senses.exampleCN: 差别极小，结果却完全变了。
senses.why: The word does not merely say small; it says small enough to be missed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不只是说小；它说小到会被漏掉。

senses.title: Minuscule handwriting
senses.definition: writing so tiny that it requires close looking
senses.definitionCN: 小到必须贴近才能读的字迹
senses.example: Her minuscule handwriting filled the margins of every page.
senses.exampleCN: 她的蝇头小字填满了每一页的页边。
senses.why: Writing scaled down is still writing; the difficulty moves from the hand to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 被缩小书写的仍是书写；困难从手移到了眼睛。

senses.title: A minuscule risk
senses.definition: a probability so low that it rarely enters planning
senses.definitionCN: 低到很少进入计划的概率
senses.example: The engineers called the risk minuscule and still tested for it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师称这个风险极小，却仍然为它做了测试。
senses.why: Small chances are not the same as no chances; the word measures, it does not dismiss.
senses.whyCN: 小概率不等于没有概率；这个词是衡量，而不是排除。

senses.title: A minuscule detail
senses.definition: a piece of information small in size but able to change a result
senses.definitionCN: 体积很小却能改变结果的一条信息
senses.example: A minuscule error in the code cost three days.
senses.exampleCN: 代码里一个极小的错误花了三天。
senses.why: Details are small in size and large in consequence, which is why the word is useful in warnings.
senses.whyCN: 细节体积小而后果大，这正是这个词在警告中有用的原因。

senses.title: A minuscule budget
senses.definition: an amount of money too small for the task assigned to it
senses.definitionCN: 相对于所派任务而言过少的钱
senses.example: They built the whole service on a minuscule budget.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用一笔微薄的预算搭起了整套服务。
senses.why: The word can carry sympathy or reproach, depending on who set the budget.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以带同情，也可以带责备，取决于谁定了预算。

senses.title: A minuscule portion
senses.definition: a share so small that it hardly registers in the total
senses.definitionCN: 小到在总量里几乎不留痕迹的份额
senses.example: Only a minuscule portion of the archive survives.
senses.exampleCN: 档案中只有极小一部分留存下来。
senses.why: What survives is often minuscule, and history is written from that remainder.
senses.whyCN: 留存下来的常常极小，而历史正是由这点残余写成。

senses.title: A minuscule letter
senses.definition: a lowercase letter, historically the small form in a written line
senses.definitionCN: 书写行里历史上较小的字母形式
senses.example: The manuscript switches from majuscule to minuscule halfway down.
senses.exampleCN: 手稿在中段从小写大写体转为小写体。
senses.why: This sense is technical but literal: minuscule letters are the small ones in a row of writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项专业却字面：minuscule 字母就是一行书写中较小的那些。

senses.title: Minuscule in importance
senses.definition: so slight in significance that it barely counts
senses.definitionCN: 在重要性上轻微到几乎不算数
senses.example: In the long record, this quarrel is minuscule.
senses.exampleCN: 在漫长的记录中，这场争吵微不足道。
senses.why: Here the word moves from size to value, and the two are not the same measure.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词从尺寸移到价值，而两者并非同一种衡量。

intro.en: Minuscule comes from Latin for somewhat less, and it named the small letters before it named small things.
intro.cn: minuscule 来自拉丁语「稍微少一点」，它先命名小写字母，再命名微小之物。

items.en: Minusculus meant somewhat smaller, a diminutive of minus.
items.cn: minusculus 意为「稍小一些」，是 minus 的指小形式。

items.en: Minus means less, and gives minus, minor and minimum in English.
items.cn: minus 意为更少，给出英语的 minus、minor 与 minimum。

items.en: Medieval scribes used minuscula for the small letters, as opposed to capitals.
items.cn: 中世纪抄写者用 minuscula 指小字母，以区别于大写。

items.en: English borrowed it for the script, then extended it to anything very small.
items.cn: 英语先借它指字体，后扩展到任何极小的东西。

items.en: The spelling miniscule is a common error by analogy with mini, but minuscule is standard.
items.cn: 受 mini 类推，miniscule 是常见误拼，而 minuscule 才是标准。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the less root; the near-meaning group ranks smallness.
note.cn: 形近组共享「更少」词根；近义组排列小的程度。

entries.definition: of lowercase lettering.
less, subtracted.
lesser in size or importance.
the smallest possible amount.
extremely small in size.
extremely small or detailed.
so small that a microscope is needed.
so small it need not be considered.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a letter written on a grain of rice.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一封写在米粒上的信」的画面。

normal.en: Minuscule contains minus: less, and then less again.
normal.cn: minuscule 含 minus：少，然后再少。

normal.en: Do not spell it miniscule; the word is minus, not mini.
normal.cn: 别拼成 miniscule；这个词是 minus，不是 mini。

normal.en: Think of the small letters at the bottom of an eye chart.
normal.cn: 想象视力表最底下那几个小字。

normal.en: Say MIH-nuh-skyool; the first syllable is already shrinking.
normal.cn: 读成 MIH-nuh-skyool，第一个音节就已经在缩小。

normal.en: Link with minimum: both measure the bottom of a scale.
normal.cn: 和 minimum 联系：两者都量刻度的底端。

abstract.en: Small size and small importance are different measures, though the word serves both.
abstract.cn: 体积的小与重要性的小是两种衡量，尽管这个词两者都用。

abstract.en: A tiny cause can carry a large effect, which is why small things are worth checking.
abstract.cn: 微小的原因可以带来巨大的效果，所以小东西值得检查。

abstract.en: What is easy to miss is not the same as what does not matter.
abstract.cn: 容易被漏掉的不等于不重要的。

examples.en: A minuscule error in the code cost three days.
examples.cn: 代码里一个极小的错误花了三天。

examples.en: The difference was minuscule but the result changed completely.
examples.cn: 差别极小，结果却完全变了。

examples.en: Only a minuscule portion of the archive survives.
examples.cn: 档案中只有极小一部分留存下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: minus（更少）+ cule（指小）：再少一点，就是「极小」。

root: 拉丁语 minus（更少）→ minusculus（稍小的）

sensesIntro.en: Minuscule starts at the size of letters and ends at the size of importance; the senses differ in which scale is being used.
sensesIntro.cn: minuscule 从字母的尺寸开始，到重要性的尺寸结束；各义项的差别在于用的是哪一把尺。

branches.en: Physical smallness, detail and slight importance.
branches.cn: 物理上的小、细节，以及轻微的重要性。

branches.en: Small writing and the lowercase letter.
branches.cn: 小字迹与小写字母。

branches.en: Small chances, budgets and surviving portions.
branches.cn: 小概率、微薄预算与残存的部分。

branches.en: Measuring a small thing is not the same as dismissing it.
branches.cn: 衡量小物不等于排除小物。

branches.en: Size is one scale, consequence another.
branches.cn: 尺寸是一把尺，后果是另一把。

intro.en: The minus family measures downward: minuscule is the smallest, minor is lesser, minimum is the floor.
intro.cn: minus 词族向下量：minuscule 最小，minor 较小，minimum 是底线。

latinIntro.en: Latin minus means less; the diminutive -culus makes it somewhat less, and the word slid from letters to things.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minus 意为更少；指小后缀 -culus 使其成为「稍少一些」，而这个词从字母滑向了事物。

items.example: The minuscular hand is hard to read.
Keep the cost at a minimum.

items.meaning: to make as small as possible

items.exampleCN: 出现了一道极细的裂缝。

definition_zh: 邪恶的；违法的；穷凶极恶的
definition_en: extremely wicked, especially in a way that breaks moral or legal limits
core_image: 一份写在暗处的名单，每个名字后面都标着日期和价钱
scene: 那份合同看上去合法，条款里却藏着一条专门用来骗老人的安排。The nefarious scheme was hidden in plain language.
sceneCN: 这里 nefarious 指邪恶的（第 2 个义项：卑劣的计谋）；句意为这个恶计藏在平实的措辞里。

pos.zh: 邪恶的；违法的；穷凶极恶的

senses.title: Wicked beyond the law
senses.definition: evil of a kind that violates what is held sacred or lawful
senses.definitionCN: 违反被视为神圣或合法之界限的那种恶
senses.example: The nefarious scheme was hidden in plain language.
senses.exampleCN: 这个恶计藏在平实的措辞里。
senses.why: The word is stronger than merely illegal: it adds a violation of what should never be done.
senses.whyCN: 这个词比「仅仅违法」更强：它加上了一层对「本不该做之事」的违犯。

senses.title: A nefarious scheme
senses.definition: a plan built to harm others while appearing harmless
senses.definitionCN: 为伤害他人而建、却显得无害的计划
senses.example: The nefarious scheme was hidden in plain language.
senses.exampleCN: 这个恶计藏在平实的措辞里。
senses.why: A plan becomes nefarious when its success depends on someone not understanding it.
senses.whyCN: 当一个计划的成功依赖他人看不懂它时，这个计划就是卑劣的。

senses.title: A nefarious trade
senses.definition: an activity or business that profits from what should not be sold
senses.definitionCN: 从本不该被出售之物中获利的行为或生意
senses.example: The nefarious trade in stolen documents continued for years.
senses.exampleCN: 被盗文件的黑市交易持续了多年。
senses.why: Commerce can be orderly and still nefarious, because the harm sits in the goods, not the paperwork.
senses.whyCN: 生意可以井然有序而仍然邪恶，因为伤害在货里，不在文书里。

senses.title: Nefarious intent
senses.definition: a purpose that aims at another person's harm
senses.definitionCN: 以伤害他人为目标的用意
senses.example: The message looked friendly but carried a nefarious intent.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息看似友好，却带着恶意。
senses.why: Intent is invisible, so the word is often applied to what a message was meant to do rather than what it said.
senses.whyCN: 意图不可见，因此这个词常用来指一条消息想要做的事，而不是它说出口的话。

senses.title: A nefarious alliance
senses.definition: a partnership formed for a purpose no honest party would join
senses.definitionCN: 为任何正当一方都不愿加入的目的而形成的伙伴关系
senses.example: The two firms formed a nefarious alliance to fix prices.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司组成邪恶联盟来操纵价格。
senses.why: The word judges the purpose, not the members, which is why it can describe respectable people.
senses.whyCN: 这个词评判的是目的，而非成员，因此它也能形容体面的人。

senses.title: Nefarious means
senses.definition: methods that are condemned even when the goal is arguable
senses.definitionCN: 即使目标尚可争论也仍受谴责的方法
senses.example: They used nefarious means to reach a defensible end.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用卑劣手段去达到一个尚可辩护的目的。
senses.why: Separating ends from means is an old habit, and the word refuses to do it quietly.
senses.whyCN: 把目的与手段分开是旧习惯，而这个词拒绝安静地配合。

senses.title: A nefarious reputation
senses.definition: the public name a person or group earns by such acts
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或团体因这类行为得到的公众名声
senses.example: The family carried a nefarious reputation into the next generation.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人把恶名带进了下一代。
senses.why: A reputation is the shadow a past act casts forward, and the word keeps that shadow attached to a name.
senses.whyCN: 名声是过去行为向前投下的影子，这个词让这道影子继续挂在一个名字上。

senses.title: The banality of the nefarious
senses.definition: the fact that great harm is often done by ordinary, orderly people
senses.definitionCN: 巨大的伤害常由普通而有秩序的人完成这一事实
senses.example: The nefarious part was not dramatic; it was a form signed without reading.
senses.exampleCN: 邪恶之处并不戏剧化；它是一份没读就签的表。
senses.why: The word can be most useful when it points at routine, not at monsters.
senses.whyCN: 当它指向日常流程而不是怪物时，这个词可能最有用。

intro.en: Nefarious comes from Latin for contrary to divine law, and it once meant simply impious.
intro.cn: nefarious 来自拉丁语「违反神法」，最初只指不敬神。

items.en: Nefarius meant wicked, abominable, outside what is permitted.
items.cn: nefarius 意为「邪恶的、可憎的、超出许可的」。

items.en: Nefas meant an unspeakable wrong, a thing against divine law.
items.cn: nefas 意为「不可言说的罪」，违反神法之事。

items.en: Fas meant divine law or right, so nefas was its negation.
items.cn: fas 意为神法、正当，因此 nefas 是它的否定。

items.en: English took the adjective in the 16c. and kept the sense of exceeding all limits.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个形容词，保留了「逾越一切界限」的意思。

items.en: Modern English softened it toward wicked or criminal, often with a slight dramatic air.
items.cn: 现代英语把它软化为「邪恶或犯罪」，常带一点戏剧气。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin wrong root; the near-meaning group ranks kinds of evil.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「不正」的词根；近义组排列恶的种类。

entries.definition: in a wicked manner.
extreme wickedness.
a thing contrary to divine law.
too wicked to be spoken of.
bad in a way that harms deliberately.
suggesting evil or harm to come.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示邪恶或即将来临的伤害。

entries.definition: extremely unjust or morally wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 极不公正或道德败坏的。

entries.definition: behaving like a storybook villain.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a list kept in the dark, with dates and prices beside each name.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一份藏在暗处的名单，每个名字旁都有日期和价钱」的画面。

normal.en: Nefarious contains nefas, Latin for a thing against divine law.
normal.cn: nefarious 含 nefas，拉丁语「违反神法之事」。

normal.en: Think of a contract that is legal in form and rotten in purpose.
normal.cn: 想象一份形式合法、目的腐烂的合同。

normal.en: Say nuh-FAIR-ee-us; the middle sounds like a polite word for an ugly thing.
normal.cn: 读成 nuh-FAIR-ee-us，中间音像用客气话包装丑事。

normal.en: Link with infamous: both name a reputation, one earned by evil.
normal.cn: 和 infamous 联系：两者都指名声，一个由恶行挣得。

normal.en: Pair it with scheme: nefarious rarely describes a person alone.
normal.cn: 和 scheme 配对：nefarious 很少单独形容一个人。

abstract.en: The strongest evil often wears the clothes of ordinary procedure.
abstract.cn: 最强的恶，常穿着日常程序的衣服。

abstract.en: A word like this warns us to look at purpose, not at manners.
abstract.cn: 这样的词提醒我们看目的，而不是看礼貌。

abstract.en: What is legal and what is permitted are not the same question.
abstract.cn: 合法与「被允许」不是同一个问题。

examples.en: The nefarious scheme was hidden in plain language.
examples.cn: 这个恶计藏在平实的措辞里。

examples.en: The nefarious trade in stolen documents continued for years.
examples.cn: 被盗文件的黑市交易持续了多年。

examples.en: They used nefarious means to reach a defensible end.
examples.cn: 他们用卑劣手段去达到一个尚可辩护的目的。

dict_mnemonic.text: ne（不）+ far（神法、正当）+ ious：不合神法，就是「邪恶的」。

root: 拉丁语 nefas（违反神法之事），加形容词后缀 -ius

sensesIntro.en: Nefarious judges purpose rather than paperwork; the senses differ in whether the evil sits in a plan, a trade, an intention or a reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: nefarious 评判的是目的而非文书；各义项的差别在于恶在计谋、交易、用意，还是名声里。

branches.en: Schemes and methods judged by what they do.
branches.cn: 按所为来评判的计谋与手段。

branches.en: Trades that profit from what should not be sold.
branches.cn: 从不该被出售之物获利的交易。

branches.en: Intention and partnership formed for harm.
branches.cn: 为伤害而形成的用意与伙伴关系。

branches.en: The reputation left behind.
branches.cn: 留下的名声。

branches.en: The ordinary, signed, unread form of harm.
branches.cn: 伤害那种普通、已签字、未被阅读的形态。

intro.en: The nefas family is a pair of opposites: fas is what is right, and nefas is what may not be done.
intro.cn: nefas 词族是一对反面：fas 是正当，nefas 是不许做的事。

latinIntro.en: Latin fas names divine law; the negative ne- turns it into a prohibition that no human court invented.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fas 命名神法；否定成分 ne- 把它变成一条并非人间法庭发明的禁令。

items.exampleCN: 他们邪恶地改动了记录。

items.example: The nefariousness of the act shocked them.
items.exampleCN: 这一行为的邪恶令他们震惊。

items.example: Nefas could not be spoken aloud.
Fas allowed the rite to continue.

items.exampleCN: 记录了一桩不可言说的罪。

items.example: The infamous building was torn down.
items.exampleCN: 那座恶名昭彰的建筑被拆了。

definition_zh: 满不在乎；从容不迫；漫不经心
definition_en: a relaxed, unconcerned manner that suggests nothing can disturb it
core_image: 一个人在漏水的船上，先把杯子扶正，再慢慢讲起天气
scene: 火警响了，所有人都在找出口，他还在把咖啡喝完。Her nonchalance convinced no one that she was calm.
sceneCN: 这里 nonchalance 指故作从容（第 1 个义项：看似毫不在意）；句意为她的满不在乎没能让任何人相信她真的镇定。

pos.zh: 满不在乎；从容不迫；漫不经心

senses.title: Apparent unconcern
senses.definition: a manner that shows no worry about what is happening
senses.definitionCN: 对正在发生的事不显露担忧的态度
senses.example: Her nonchalance convinced no one that she was calm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的满不在乎没能让任何人相信她真的镇定。
senses.why: The word describes the surface, and surfaces can be made: what looks careless may be carefully built.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述表面，而表面是可以造出来的：看似无意，可能精心搭成。

senses.title: Calm under pressure
senses.definition: real ease of manner in a situation that would disturb most people
senses.definitionCN: 在多数人会被扰动的场合中真实的从容
senses.example: He met the bad news with the nonchalance of a man who had expected it.
senses.exampleCN: 他以预料之中的人才有的从容面对坏消息。
senses.why: Here the word is sincere: the ease is not performed but comes from having already absorbed the bad news.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词是真诚的：从容不是演出来的，而是因为早已消化了坏消息。

senses.title: Studied indifference
senses.definition: deliberately performed unconcern meant to be noticed
senses.definitionCN: 故意演出来、希望被注意到的漠不关心
senses.example: The nonchalance of his shrug was too quick to be real.
senses.exampleCN: 他那一耸肩的漠然太快，不像是真的。
senses.why: When indifference is performed, the performance itself gives the feeling away.
senses.whyCN: 当漠然被表演时，表演本身就泄露了情感。

senses.title: Nonchalance in dress
senses.definition: an easy, unforced style that refuses to try too hard
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝过度用力的轻松风格
senses.example: The room was furnished with expensive nonchalance.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间以昂贵的随意布置。
senses.why: The word extends from manners to style, because both can show an ease that costs effort to build.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从举止延伸到风格，因为两者都能显出需要费力才能搭出的轻松。

senses.title: Nonchalance as mask
senses.definition: unconcern used to hide fear, anger or interest
senses.definitionCN: 用来掩藏恐惧、愤怒或兴趣的漠然
senses.example: His nonchalance was a mask that slipped when her name came up.
senses.exampleCN: 他的淡然是一张面具，在她名字出现时滑落了。
senses.why: A mask is most visible at the moment it is needed most.
senses.whyCN: 面具在最需要它的时刻最显眼。

senses.title: Nonchalance in danger
senses.definition: a cool manner that steadies other people
senses.definitionCN: 使他人稳定的冷静态度
senses.example: The pilot's nonchalance kept the passengers from panicking.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员的从容防止了乘客恐慌。
senses.why: In a crisis, manner is a public resource: one calm person can lend calm to many.
senses.whyCN: 危机中，态度是公共资源：一个镇定的人可以把镇定借给许多人。

senses.title: The nonchalance of wealth
senses.definition: the ease that comes from being able to afford mistakes
senses.definitionCN: 因为付得起错误代价而生的轻松
senses.example: The nonchalance of the collector annoyed the young artists.
senses.exampleCN: 这位收藏家的随意让年轻艺术家们恼火。
senses.why: Ease looks different depending on who can afford it, and the word can carry that criticism.
senses.whyCN: 轻松看起来不一样，取决于谁付得起，而这个词能带上这层批评。

senses.title: The cost of nonchalance
senses.definition: the harm done when unconcern is taken for competence
senses.definitionCN: 当漠然被当作能力时造成的损害
senses.example: His nonchalance about the deadline lost the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他对截止日期的漫不经心弄丢了合同。
senses.why: The same manner that looks confident can also look careless, and only results separate them.
senses.whyCN: 同一种态度可以显得自信，也可以显得粗心，只有结果能把它们分开。

intro.en: Nonchalance joins not with a French verb meaning to be warm about something, so it means not heated.
intro.cn: nonchalance 把「不」与一个意为「对某事发热」的法语动词接在一起，意思就是「没有热起来」。

items.en: French nonchalance meant indifference, from non- and chaloir.
items.cn: 法语 nonchalance 意为漠不关心，由 non- 与 chaloir 构成。

items.en: Chaloir meant to be warm or concerned about something, from Latin calere.
items.cn: chaloir 意为对某事发热、挂心，出自拉丁语 calere。

items.en: Calere means to be warm, and gives calorie and caloric.
items.cn: calere 意为发热，给出 calorie 与 caloric。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the 18c. as a word for fashionable ease.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入这个名词，指一种时髦的从容。

items.en: Modern English uses it for both genuine coolness and performed indifference.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指真实的冷静，也指表演出的漠然。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the warm root; the near-meaning group separates kinds of coolness.
note.cn: 形近组保留「热」的词根；近义组区分不同种类的冷静。

entries.definition: calmly unconcerned.
in an unconcerned way.
old French for to care or be warm.
a unit of heat or food energy.
lack of interest or concern.
calm control of one's feelings and face.
entries.definitionCN: 对情感与表情的镇定掌控。

entries.definition: assurance that does not wobble under pressure.
cheerful lack of worry.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of someone righting a cup on a leaking boat before mentioning the weather.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「船在漏水，某人先把杯子扶正，再谈起天气」的画面。

normal.en: Nonchalance = non + chaloir, not warm about it.
normal.cn: nonchalance = non + chaloir，对它不发热。

normal.en: The chaloir part hides in calorie: warmth is heat.
normal.cn: chaloir 藏在 calorie 里：暖就是热。

normal.en: Think of a shrug performed exactly one beat too fast.
normal.cn: 想象一次快了半拍的耸肩。

normal.en: Say non-shuh-LAHNS; the soft ending sounds like a dismissal.
normal.cn: 读成 non-shuh-LAHNS，轻柔的结尾像一次打发。

normal.en: Pair it with composure: composure is real, nonchalance may be a surface.
normal.cn: 和 composure 配对：composure 是真的，nonchalance 可能是表面。

abstract.en: Indifference can be strength or theatre, and the difference is usually timing.
abstract.cn: 漠然可以是力量，也可以是戏，而差别通常在时机。

abstract.en: Calm in a crisis is a gift to everyone standing nearby.
abstract.cn: 危机中的镇定是给身边所有人的礼物。

abstract.en: Ease that costs nothing to the person showing it may cost others a great deal.
abstract.cn: 对展示者毫无代价的轻松，可能让别人付出很多。

examples.en: Her nonchalance convinced no one that she was calm.
examples.cn: 她的满不在乎没能让任何人相信她真的镇定。

examples.en: The pilot's nonchalance kept the passengers from panicking.
examples.cn: 飞行员的从容防止了乘客恐慌。

examples.en: His nonchalance about the deadline lost the contract.
examples.cn: 他对截止日期的漫不经心弄丢了合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: non（不）+ chaloir（发热、挂心）：不发热，就是「满不在乎」。

root: 法语 nonchalance，源自 non-（不）与 chaloir（发热、挂心），再上溯拉丁语 calere

sensesIntro.en: Nonchalance is coolness of surface; the senses differ in whether the coolness is real, performed, useful or costly.
sensesIntro.cn: nonchalance 是表面的冷；各义项的差别在于这份冷是真的、演的、有用的，还是代价高的。

core.en: A SURFACE THAT DOES NOT HEAT UP

branches.en: The surface, the performance and the mask.
branches.cn: 表面、表演与面具。

branches.en: Real calm that steady others in danger.
branches.cn: 在危险中稳住他人的真实镇定。

branches.en: Style and the ease that money can buy.
branches.cn: 风格，以及金钱能买到的轻松。

branches.en: The failure when ease is mistaken for competence.
branches.cn: 轻松被误认作能力时的失败。

branches.en: Timing and result decide whether it reads as strength or carelessness.
branches.cn: 时机与结果决定它读作力量还是粗心。

intro.en: The chal family is about heat: nonchalance has none, calorie measures it, and caloric describes it.
intro.cn: chal 词族与热有关：nonchalance 没有热，calorie 衡量热，caloric 描述热。

latinIntro.en: Latin calere means to be warm; French turned it into caring, and non- turned caring into coolness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 calere 意为发热；法语把它变成「挂心」，而 non- 把挂心变成冷淡。

items.meaning: a state of not being warm

items.exampleCN: 他漫不经心地挥了挥手。
她漫不经心地读了裁决。

definition_zh: 细微差别；微妙之处；细微层次
definition_en: a very small difference in meaning, feeling, colour or tone
core_image: 同一片灰布在两种光下显出不同的冷与暖，眼睛要停一会儿才分得出
scene: 两句话几乎一样，只是第二个句子里少了一个「也」。The nuance changed the apology into a complaint.
sceneCN: 这里 nuance 指语义上的细微差别（第 2 个义项：意义中的微差）；句意为这处细微差别把道歉变成了抱怨。

forms.label: 现在分词（使有细微差别）

senses.title: A very small difference
senses.definition: a distinction so slight that it is easy to overlook
senses.definitionCN: 小到容易被忽略的区别
senses.example: The nuance changed the apology into a complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 这处细微差别把道歉变成了抱怨。
senses.why: The word names differences that do not announce themselves; they must be looked for.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名那些不会自我宣告的差别；它们必须被寻找。

senses.title: Nuance in meaning
senses.definition: a small shift in what a word or sentence implies
senses.definitionCN: 一个词或句子所暗示意义的小小偏移
senses.example: The translation missed the nuance of the original.
senses.exampleCN: 译文漏掉了原文的细微含义。
senses.why: Meaning is often carried by what is almost said, and the word marks that almost.
senses.whyCN: 意义常由「几乎说出口」的部分承载，而这个词标记的就是那个「几乎」。

senses.title: Nuance of tone
senses.definition: a slight change in voice that alters how a sentence lands
senses.definitionCN: 让一句话落地方式改变的轻微语音变化
senses.example: Her tone carried a nuance that no transcript could show.
senses.exampleCN: 她的语气带着一种任何文字记录都显示不出的细微。
senses.why: Voice carries information that writing loses; the word marks the part that lives only in sound.
senses.whyCN: 声音承载着书写会丢失的信息，这个词标记的就是只活在声音里的那部分。

senses.title: Nuance in colour
senses.definition: a faint variation within what looks like one colour
senses.definitionCN: 在看似单一的颜色内部的细微变化
senses.example: The painter built the wall from a hundred nuances of grey.
senses.exampleCN: 画家用上百种灰色层次砌成这面墙。
senses.why: Painting made the word visual: one colour is rarely one colour, and its shifts are what the eye reads.
senses.whyCN: 绘画让这个词变得可见：一种颜色很少只是一种颜色，眼睛读的正是它的层次变化。

senses.title: Nuance in law
senses.definition: a small distinction that decides how a rule applies
senses.definitionCN: 决定一条规则如何适用的小区别
senses.example: The case turned on a nuance of contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 这个案子取决于合同法中的一处细节。
senses.why: In law, small differences carry large consequences, which is why the word is at home there.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，小差别带来大后果，因此这个词在那里很自在。

senses.title: Lost nuance
senses.definition: the flattening that happens when a small difference is dropped
senses.definitionCN: 当细微差别被丢掉时发生的扁平化
senses.example: The summary lost every nuance and kept only the verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 摘要丢掉了全部分寸，只留下结论。
senses.why: The word can name an absence: what is missing when a summary keeps the conclusion and drops the shade.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能命名一种缺失：摘要留下结论、丢掉分寸时，缺失的就是它。

senses.title: Nuance in translation
senses.definition: the small shade of meaning that rarely survives a change of language
senses.definitionCN: 很少能在换语言后存活的细微意味
senses.example: Good translation protects the nuance, not the words.
senses.exampleCN: 好的翻译保护细微之处，而不是字面。
senses.why: Translation shows the word at its hardest, because the shade often has no equivalent in the other language.
senses.whyCN: 翻译让这个词的难处显形，因为这种细微在另一种语言里常常没有对应。

senses.title: Nuance as skill
senses.definition: the ability to notice and use small distinctions
senses.definitionCN: 察觉并使用细小区别的能力
senses.example: Diplomacy is mostly a discipline of nuance.
senses.exampleCN: 外交大半是一门把握细微的功夫。
senses.why: The word can name a talent as well as a difference, and the talent is what keeps the difference alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既能命名差别，也能命名才能，而才能让差别得以存活。

intro.en: Nuance comes from a French word for a shade of colour, and its root is the word for cloud.
intro.cn: nuance 来自一个意为「色彩深浅」的法语词，其词根是「云」。

items.en: French nuance meant a shade or gradation of colour.
items.cn: 法语 nuance 意为色彩的深浅或渐变。

items.en: Nuer meant to shade, to vary by degrees, from nue, a cloud.
items.cn: nuer 意为给颜色加层次、逐度变化，出自 nue（云）。

items.en: Nubes means cloud, and gives nubilous and obnubilate.
items.cn: nubes 意为云，给出 nubilous 与 obnubilate。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the 18c., first for colour and then for meaning.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入，先指颜色，后指意义。

items.en: Modern English uses it for any small distinction in feeling, tone or argument.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于情感、语气或论证中的任何细微区别。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the shading root; the near-meaning group names small distinctions.
note.cn: 形近组共享「加层次」的词根；近义组命名各种细小区别。

entries.definition: showing fine distinctions.
the act of making fine distinctions.
the plural form, for several small differences.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指多处细微差别。

entries.definition: cloudy or obscure.
a small degree of difference.
the quality of being delicate and hard to notice.
entries.definitionCN: 精细而难以察觉的性质。

entries.definition: a difference made between two things.
entries.definitionCN: 在两物之间作出的区别。

entries.definition: a stage in a gradual series.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of one grey cloth showing warm and cold under two kinds of light.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「同一块灰布在两种光下显出暖与冷」的画面。

normal.en: Nuance came from clouds: a shade is a thin layer over the same colour.
normal.cn: nuance 来自云：一层薄薄的东西盖在同一种颜色上。

normal.en: The word is about degrees, not opposites.
normal.cn: 这个词讲的是程度，不是对立。

normal.en: Think of two apologies that differ by one small word.
normal.cn: 想象两句只差一个词的道歉。

normal.en: Say NYOO-ahns; the soft ending sounds like a distinction dissolving.
normal.cn: 读成 NYOO-ahns，柔和的结尾像区别在消融。

normal.en: Link with shaded: both are about small changes along a surface.
normal.cn: 和 shaded 联系：两者都指表面上小幅变化。

abstract.en: Most disagreements about meaning are disagreements about nuance.
abstract.cn: 多数关于意义的分歧，是关于细微差别的分歧。

abstract.en: Flattening a distinction is the easiest way to win an argument dishonestly.
abstract.cn: 抹平区别，是用不诚实方式赢得争论最容易的办法。

abstract.en: Perceiving nuance is a skill, and like any skill it can be trained.
abstract.cn: 察觉细微是一种技能，和任何技能一样可以训练。

examples.en: The nuance changed the apology into a complaint.
examples.cn: 这处细微差别把道歉变成了抱怨。

examples.en: The translation missed the nuance of the original.
examples.cn: 译文漏掉了原文的细微含义。

examples.en: The case turned on a nuance of contract law.
examples.cn: 这个案子取决于合同法中的一处细节。

dict_mnemonic.text: nu（云）+ ance（名词）：像云层一样薄薄的层次，就是「细微差别」。

root: 法语 nuance（色彩深浅），源自 nuer（加层次），上溯拉丁语 nubes（云）

sensesIntro.en: Nuance always names a difference too small to announce itself; the senses differ in the surface where the difference appears.
sensesIntro.cn: nuance 始终命名一种小到不会自我宣告的差别；各义项的差别在于这差别出现在什么表面上。

core.en: A DIFFERENCE TOO SMALL TO ANNOUNCE ITSELF
core.cn: 小到不会自我宣告的差别

branches.en: Meaning and tone, where small shifts change everything.
branches.cn: 意义与语气，小偏移改变一切的地方。

branches.en: The visual origin: colour and its degrees.
branches.cn: 视觉本源：颜色与它的度数。

branches.en: Law and translation, where tiny distinctions decide cases.
branches.cn: 法律与翻译，微小区别决定成败之处。

branches.en: The loss that happens when distinctions are dropped.
branches.cn: 区别被丢弃时的损失。

branches.en: The skill that keeps the difference available.
branches.cn: 让差别得以存活的技能。

intro.en: The nuance family is about shading: one noun for the difference, an adjective for a text that keeps them.
intro.cn: nuance 词族与加层次有关：名词指差别，形容词指能保留差别的文本。

latinIntro.en: Latin nubes means cloud; French nuer turned cloud into shading, and shading became meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nubes 意为云；法语 nuer 把云变成「加层次」，而层次又变成了意义。

items.exampleCN: nuer 塑造了这个英语词。

items.example: Nue gave the image of a layer.

items.exampleCN: nubes 是最古老的那一层。

definition_zh: 使模糊；使混乱；故意把话说得难懂
definition_en: to make something unclear, often deliberately
core_image: 有人把一页清楚的说明涂上灰墨，又添了几句术语，让人再也找不到重点
scene: 发布会上的回答绕了三层术语，最后什么也没说明。The report obfuscates the very figures it claims to present.
sceneCN: 这里 obfuscate 指故意使内容难懂（第 1 个义项：使模糊不清）；句意为这份报告把本应呈现的数字弄得更难懂。

senses.title: Make unclear
senses.definition: to darken the meaning of something that could have been clear
senses.definitionCN: 把本可以清楚的东西的意义弄暗
senses.example: The report obfuscates the very figures it claims to present.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把本应呈现的数字弄得更难懂。
senses.why: The word assumes clarity was possible; obscurity here is an act, not a limitation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词假定清晰本是可能的；这里的晦暗是行为，不是能力不足。

senses.title: Obfuscate in speech
senses.definition: to answer in a way that hides rather than explains
senses.definitionCN: 以隐藏而非解释的方式作答
senses.example: He obfuscated for ten minutes and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他含混了十分钟，什么也没说。
senses.why: Speech can be full and empty at once, and the word names that combination.
senses.whyCN: 言语可以同时充盈与空洞，而这个词命名这种组合。

senses.title: Obfuscate a record
senses.definition: to make a record hard to follow so that its gaps are not noticed
senses.definitionCN: 把记录弄得难读，使人注意不到其中的空白
senses.example: The file was obfuscated with duplicate entries.
senses.exampleCN: 这份档案被重复条目搅得看不清。
senses.why: A record can be technically complete and still unreadable, which is how a gap is hidden without a lie.
senses.whyCN: 记录可以在技术上完整却仍无法读清，空白就是这样在不撒谎的情况下被藏起来的。

senses.title: Obfuscate code
senses.definition: to rewrite program code so that humans cannot easily read it
senses.definitionCN: 重写程序代码使人类难以读懂
senses.example: They obfuscated the code before shipping it.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在交付前混淆了代码。
senses.why: This is the technical sense and morally neutral: the machine still runs it perfectly.
senses.whyCN: 这是技术义，道德上中性：机器仍能完美运行它。

senses.title: Obfuscate motives
senses.definition: to hide one's real reasons behind complicated explanations
senses.definitionCN: 用复杂的解释遮住真实理由
senses.example: The long explanation obfuscated a simple motive: profit.
senses.exampleCN: 冗长的解释掩盖了一个简单动机：利润。
senses.why: Complexity is a cheap hiding place: the more explanation, the less chance anyone asks the simple question.
senses.whyCN: 复杂是廉价的藏身处：解释越多，越没人去问那个简单的问题。

senses.title: Obfuscate with detail
senses.definition: to bury the main point under a mass of secondary facts
senses.definitionCN: 用大量次要事实埋掉要点
senses.example: The appendix obfuscates the finding with numbers nobody needed.
senses.exampleCN: 附录用没人需要的数字把发现埋了起来。
senses.why: Too much true information can work exactly like a lie.
senses.whyCN: 过多真实信息，效果可以和谎言一模一样。

senses.title: Obfuscate deliberately
senses.definition: to create confusion on purpose, usually to avoid responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 故意制造混乱，通常为逃避责任
senses.example: The minister obfuscated until the question expired.
senses.exampleCN: 部长一直搅浑，直到问题过期。
senses.why: Deliberate fog aims at time: if the answer arrives after the deadline, the question has already died.
senses.whyCN: 故意制造迷雾瞄准的是时间：如果答案在截止之后才来，问题已经死了。

senses.title: Obfuscation in bureaucracy
senses.definition: the routine fog of forms and procedures that no one can follow
senses.definitionCN: 无人能跟上的表格与程序所构成的日常迷雾
senses.example: The procedure obfuscated a decision that one person could have made.
senses.exampleCN: 这套程序把一个人就能做的决定弄得不可理解。
senses.why: Not every fog is planned; some is simply the sediment of many small safeguards.
senses.whyCN: 并非每片雾都是计划好的；有些只是许多小防范沉积下来的。

intro.en: Obfuscate comes from Latin for darkening over, and it keeps the picture of a surface being covered.
intro.cn: obfuscate 来自拉丁语「盖上变暗」，它保留着表面被覆盖的画面。

items.en: Obfuscare meant to darken, to obscure, built from ob- and fuscare.
items.cn: obfuscare 意为「使暗、使晦」，由 ob- 与 fuscare 构成。

items.en: Fuscare meant to make dark, from fuscus, dark brown.
items.cn: fuscare 意为使暗，出自 fuscus（深褐色）。

items.en: Fuscus meant dark, dusky, and survives in fuscous.
items.cn: fuscus 意为暗的、黝黑的，仍存于 fuscous。

items.en: English took the verb in the 16c.with the literal sense of darkening.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，本义是使变暗。

items.en: Modern English narrowed it to making meaning unclear, usually on purpose.
items.cn: 现代英语把它收窄为「使意义不清」，通常指有意为之。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dark root; the near-meaning group names ways of hiding meaning.
note.cn: 形近组共享「暗」的词根；近义组命名掩藏意义的方式。

entries.definition: the act of making something unclear.
serving to confuse or darken.
made deliberately unclear.
dark brown or dusky.
to make something disordered and unclear.
to keep something from being seen or known.
to make an issue unclear or suspect.
to speak vaguely so as to avoid a clear answer.
entries.definitionCN: 含糊其辞以回避明确回答。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a clear page painted over with grey until nothing can be found.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一页清楚的文件被灰墨涂过，什么也找不到」的画面。

normal.en: Obfuscate = ob + fuscus, dark: to put darkness over something.
normal.cn: obfuscate = ob + fuscus（暗）：把黑暗盖在某物上。

normal.en: Fuscous is the plain adjective for dark; the verb adds a cover.
normal.cn: fuscous 就是「暗」的形容词；动词加上了一层覆盖。

normal.en: Think of a footnote that explains less the longer it runs.
normal.cn: 想象一条越写越不解释的脚注。

normal.en: Say OB-fus-kate; the hard start sounds like a lid coming down.
normal.cn: 读成 OB-fus-kate，硬的起始音像盖子落下。

normal.en: Pair it with clarify: one puts a cover on, the other takes it off.
normal.cn: 和 clarify 配对：一个盖上，一个揭开。

abstract.en: Not every fog is a plan; some is the residue of too many safeguards.
abstract.cn: 并非每片雾都是计划；有些只是过多防范的残余。

abstract.en: Too much true detail can hide a point as effectively as a lie.
abstract.cn: 过多真实细节，能像谎言一样有效地藏起要点。

abstract.en: Where clarity would cost someone, obscurity is often supplied free.
abstract.cn: 在清晰会让人付出代价的地方，晦暗常被免费供应。

examples.en: The report obfuscates the very figures it claims to present.
examples.cn: 这份报告把本应呈现的数字弄得更难懂。

examples.en: He obfuscated for ten minutes and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他含混了十分钟，什么也没说。

examples.en: The long explanation obfuscated a simple motive: profit.
examples.cn: 冗长的解释掩盖了一个简单动机：利润。

dict_mnemonic.text: ob（在上）+ fusc（暗）+ ate（动词）：把暗盖上去，就是「使模糊」。

root: 拉丁语 fuscus（深暗的）→ fuscare（使暗），加 ob-（在上）→ obfuscare

sensesIntro.en: Obfuscate puts a dark layer over something that could be seen; the senses differ in whether the layer is jargon, detail or procedure.
sensesIntro.cn: obfuscate 在本可被看见之物上盖一层暗；各义项的差别在于这层暗是术语、细节，还是程序。

core.en: PUTTING A DARK LAYER OVER THE CLEAR

branches.en: Speech and prose made unreadable.
branches.cn: 被弄得读不懂的言语与文字。

branches.en: Records and code, where confusion has a use.
branches.cn: 混淆确有用途的记录与代码。

branches.en: Motive buried, and detail used as cover.
branches.cn: 被埋掉的动机，以及被当作遮盖的细节。

branches.en: The deliberate version, usually to avoid blame.
branches.cn: 故意的版本，通常为逃避责备。

branches.en: The institutional fog nobody planned.
branches.cn: 无人计划的制度性迷雾。

intro.en: The fusc family is about darkness: fuscous is dark, obfuscate darkens it over, and subfusc is the dim gown of old universities.
intro.cn: fusc 词族与暗有关：fuscous 是暗的，obfuscate 把暗盖上去，subfusc 是旧大学那种暗色长袍。

latinIntro.en: Latin fuscus means dark brown; ob- means over, so the verb pictures a dark wash laid across a surface.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fuscus 意为深褐；ob- 意为在上，因此这个动词描绘一层暗色被刷过表面。

items.exampleCN: 这份备忘录把变动弄模糊了。
这种搅浑式文风掩盖了空白。
暗色的翅膀融进了背景。

items.example: An obscure clause caused the delay.
items.exampleCN: 一条晦涩的条款造成了延误。
